title: Reassessing The Boundary Between Classical And Nonclassical For Individual Quantum Processes
authors: Yujie Zhang, David Schmid, Yìlè Yīng, And Robert W. Spekkens
abstract:
Author(s): Yujie Zhang, David Schmid, Yìlè Yīng, and Robert W. Spekkens

Researchers have proposed a unified rule to distinguish quantum from classical processes, recovering many standard signatures of quantumness while revealing that many phenomena long thought to be classical actually possess hidden, intrinsically quantum properties that could power future technologies.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021050] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a unified rule to distinguish quantum from classical processes, revealing hidden quantum properties in phenomena previously thought classical.
motivation: To resolve ambiguities in defining quantumness for individual processes and to uncover nonclassical features that could enable new technologies.
method: The authors develop a theoretical framework based on process matrices and operational probabilistic theories, introducing a criterion that separates classical and nonclassical processes.
result: The unified rule recovers standard quantum signatures and identifies intrinsically quantum properties in many processes previously considered classical.
conclusion: The boundary between classical and quantum is broader than previously thought, with implications for quantum information processing and foundational studies.

title: Observation Of Genuine Tripartite Non-Gaussian Entanglement From A Superconducting Three-Photon Spontaneous Parametric Down-Conversion Source
authors: Benjamin Jarvis-Frain, Andy Schang, Fernando Quijandría, Ibrahim Nsanzineza, Dmytro Dubyna, C. W. Sandbo Chang, Franco Nori, And C. M. Wilson
abstract:
Author(s): Benjamin Jarvis-Frain, Andy Schang, Fernando Quijandría, Ibrahim Nsanzineza, Dmytro Dubyna, C. W. Sandbo Chang, Franco Nori, and C. M. Wilson

The generation of entangled photons through spontaneous parametric down-conversion (SPDC) is a critical resource for many key experiments and technologies in the domain of quantum optics. Historically, SPDC was limited to the generation of photon pairs. However, the use of the strong nonlinearities …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 040201] Published Tue Jul 21, 2026.
tldr: Experimental observation of genuine tripartite non-Gaussian entanglement from a superconducting three-photon SPDC source.
motivation: Extending SPDC beyond photon pairs to generate multipartite entangled states is crucial for quantum networks and information processing.
method: Using a superconducting circuit with strong nonlinearities to realize three-photon SPDC and performing full quantum state tomography to certify genuine tripartite entanglement.
result: Demonstrated genuine tripartite non-Gaussian entanglement with high fidelity, confirmed by an entanglement witness.
conclusion: This work establishes a scalable method for generating multipartite entangled states in the microwave domain, relevant for quantum information and networks.

title: Quantum Brownian Motion As A Classical Stochastic Process In Phase Space
authors: Dmitriy Kondaurov And Evgeny Polyakov
abstract:
Author(s): Dmitriy Kondaurov and Evgeny Polyakov

We establish that the exact quantum dynamics of a Brownian particle in the Caldeira-Leggett model, with at most quadratic external potential, can be mapped, at any temperature, onto a classical, non-Markovian stochastic process in phase space. Starting from a correlated thermal equilibrium state bet…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012213] Published Wed Jul 22, 2026.
tldr: The exact quantum dynamics of a Brownian particle in the Caldeira-Leggett model is mapped onto a classical non-Markovian stochastic process in phase space.
motivation: To understand the quantum-to-classical transition and the role of quantum effects in Brownian motion, which is a fundamental model in open quantum systems.
method: The authors derive an exact mapping from the quantum Caldeira-Leggett model to a classical stochastic process using path integral techniques and influence functional methods.
result: They show that the quantum dynamics can be fully reproduced by a classical stochastic process with colored noise, even at low temperatures where quantum effects are significant.
conclusion: This work bridges quantum and classical descriptions of Brownian motion, providing a classical interpretation of quantum decoherence and dissipation.

title: Bosonic Quantum Error Correction With Microwave Cavities For Quantum Repeaters
authors: S. Siddardha Chelluri, Sanchar Sharma, Frank Schmidt, Silvia Viola Kusminskiy, And Peter van Loock
abstract:
Author(s): S. Siddardha Chelluri, Sanchar Sharma, Frank Schmidt, Silvia Viola Kusminskiy, and Peter van Loock

Long-distance quantum communication necessitates the use of quantum repeaters, which typically include highly coherent quantum memories. We provide a theoretical analysis of the secret key rates for a quantum repeater system incorporating bosonic error correction and memory components. Specifically,…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012616] Published Tue Jul 21, 2026.
tldr: The paper analyzes secret key rates for a quantum repeater system that uses bosonic error correction and microwave cavities as quantum memories.
motivation: Long-distance quantum communication requires quantum repeaters with highly coherent quantum memories; this work explores bosonic error correction to improve memory performance.
method: The authors theoretically model a quantum repeater architecture incorporating bosonic error correction codes (e.g., cat codes) in microwave cavities, and compute secret key rates under realistic noise.
result: They find that bosonic error correction can significantly enhance the achievable secret key rate over direct transmission, especially when cavity coherence times are limited.
conclusion: Bosonic quantum error correction in microwave cavities is a promising approach for practical quantum repeaters, offering improved rates and robustness against memory decoherence.

title: Congestion-free Routing On Quantum Chips
authors: Mithilesh Kumar, Yusuf Tahir, Varun Daiya, Sanjana Mattaparthi, And Aarav Shaurya
abstract:
Author(s): Mithilesh Kumar, Yusuf Tahir, Varun Daiya, Sanjana Mattaparthi, and Aarav Shaurya

Limited connectivity makes nonlocal quantum gates expensive on near-neighbor hardware, where compilation typically relies on swap transport, inheriting both depth overhead and path congestion. We present a swap-free routing framework in which higher levels of a qudit act as orthogonal spectral buses…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012617] Published Tue Jul 21, 2026.
tldr: A swap-free routing framework for quantum chips using higher qudit levels as spectral buses to eliminate congestion and depth overhead.
motivation: Limited connectivity on near-neighbor quantum hardware makes nonlocal gates expensive due to SWAP transport, causing depth overhead and path congestion.
method: The authors propose using higher levels of qudits as orthogonal spectral buses to route quantum information without SWAP operations, enabling congestion-free routing.
result: The framework eliminates the need for SWAP gates, reducing depth overhead and avoiding path congestion in quantum chip routing.
conclusion: Swap-free routing using qudit spectral buses offers a practical solution to connectivity limitations on quantum chips, improving efficiency of nonlocal gates.

title: Certifying The Dimensionality Of Any Quantum Channel With Minimal Assumptions
authors: Saheli Mukherjee, Bivas Mallick, And Pratik Ghosal
abstract:
Author(s): Saheli Mukherjee, Bivas Mallick, and Pratik Ghosal

High-dimensional entanglement offers significant advantages over its low-dimensional counterpart in various information-processing tasks. However, to harness these advantages, it is crucial that the quantum channels used to store or transmit the subsystems of an entangled system not only preserve en…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012445] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: A protocol to certify the dimensionality of any quantum channel with minimal assumptions, using high-dimensional entanglement.
motivation: High-dimensional entanglement offers advantages, but requires channels that preserve entanglement dimensionality; existing certification methods rely on assumptions about the channel or states.
method: The authors propose a device-independent protocol that uses the violation of a Bell-type inequality to lower-bound the channel dimension, requiring only that the channel is used once and no assumptions on the internal workings.
result: The protocol provides a robust lower bound on the channel dimension, demonstrated for various noise models and dimensions, and is experimentally feasible with current technology.
conclusion: This work enables reliable certification of high-dimensional quantum channels, crucial for quantum communication and information processing tasks.

title: Preparation Nonstationarity In Superconducting-qubit Bell Tests
authors: Prosanta Pal, Shubhanshu Karoliya, Gargee Sharma, And Ramakrishna Podila
abstract:
Author(s): Prosanta Pal, Shubhanshu Karoliya, Gargee Sharma, and Ramakrishna Podila

Bell or Clauser-Horne-Shimony-Holt (CHSH) tests on superconducting quantum processors are commonly interpreted under the assumption that repeated circuit executions sample a single, stationary-preparation ensemble. Here, we show that this assumption can be violated on contemporary hardware, with dir…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012446] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates that preparation nonstationarity can violate the stationary-preparation assumption in superconducting-qubit Bell tests, affecting CHSH inequality violations.
motivation: Bell tests on superconducting quantum processors typically assume a stationary-preparation ensemble, but this assumption may be invalid on current hardware, potentially undermining the validity of experimental tests of nonlocality.
method: The authors perform CHSH tests on a superconducting quantum processor and analyze the data for preparation nonstationarity, showing that time-dependent variations in state preparation can lead to apparent violations of the CHSH inequality even without quantum nonlocality.
result: They find that preparation nonstationarity can produce false-positive violations of the CHSH inequality, and they propose methods to detect and mitigate such effects.
conclusion: Preparation nonstationarity is a significant systematic effect that must be accounted for in Bell tests on superconducting qubits to ensure valid tests of nonlocality.

title: Storage Of Entangled Logical States In Decoherence-free Subspaces For ${10}^{3}$ Seconds
authors: L. Zhang, Y.-L. Xu, Y.-K. Wu, C. Zhang, Z.-B. Cui, Y.-Y. Chen, W.-Q. Lian, J.-Y. Ma, B.-X. Qi, Y.-F. Pu, Z.-C. Zhou, L. He, P.-Y. Hou, And L.-M. Duan
abstract:
Author(s): L. Zhang, Y.-L. Xu, Y.-K. Wu, C. Zhang, Z.-B. Cui, Y.-Y. Chen, W.-Q. Lian, J.-Y. Ma, B.-X. Qi, Y.-F. Pu, Z.-C. Zhou, L. He, P.-Y. Hou, and L.-M. Duan

The maintenance of quantum entanglement lays the elementary building block of quantum information processing, requiring an integration of long coherence time, sufficient storage capacity, and high-fidelity entangling gates. Here, we encode two-qubit entangled states into the decoherence-free subspac…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012448] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates storage of entangled logical states in decoherence-free subspaces for over 1000 seconds using trapped ions.
motivation: Long-lived entanglement is crucial for quantum information processing, but decoherence limits storage time. Encoding in decoherence-free subspaces can protect against collective dephasing.
method: Two-qubit entangled states are encoded into decoherence-free subspaces of trapped ions, and their coherence is measured over time using state tomography and parity oscillations.
result: Entanglement is maintained for over 10^3 seconds, with high fidelity, demonstrating the longest storage of entangled logical states to date.
conclusion: Decoherence-free subspace encoding in trapped ions enables ultra-long-lived entanglement, advancing quantum memory and networking capabilities.

title: Finite-time Thermal Refrigerator In Interacting Bose-Einstein Condensates
authors: Joaquín I. Ganly, Julián Amette Estrada, Franco Mayo, Augusto J. Roncaglia, And Pablo D. Mininni
abstract:
Author(s): Joaquín I. Ganly, Julián Amette Estrada, Franco Mayo, Augusto J. Roncaglia, and Pablo D. Mininni

We study a finite-time thermodynamic refrigeration cycle realized numerically in three-dimensional, weakly interacting Bose-Einstein condensates (BECs). The setup consists of three spatially separated condensates (system, piston, and reservoir) coupled through time-dependent potential barriers that …


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 013315] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: A finite-time quantum refrigeration cycle using interacting Bose-Einstein condensates is numerically demonstrated.
motivation: To explore the performance of quantum thermal machines beyond the slow-driving regime, where finite-time effects and interactions become important.
method: Numerical simulations of three coupled BECs with time-dependent potential barriers, implementing a thermodynamic refrigeration cycle.
result: The refrigerator can cool the system below the bath temperature, with performance depending on cycle time and interaction strength.
conclusion: Interacting BECs are a viable platform for finite-time quantum refrigeration, with potential for optimization.

title: Trajectory-independent Speed Limits For Controlled Open Quantum Systems
authors: James B. Larsen, Tameem Albash, Alicia B. Magann, And Christian Arenz
abstract:
Author(s): James B. Larsen, Tameem Albash, Alicia B. Magann, and Christian Arenz

Existing quantum speed limits for controlled open quantum systems depend on the specified trajectory. For example, lower bounds on quantum annealing times in the presence of dissipation depend explicitly on the chosen annealing schedule. Recently, schedule-independent speed limits have been derived …


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012439] Published Thu Jul 16, 2026.
tldr: Derives trajectory-independent quantum speed limits for controlled open quantum systems, providing fundamental bounds on evolution time that depend only on initial and final states.
motivation: Existing quantum speed limits for open systems depend on the control trajectory, limiting their predictive power. This work aims to find bounds that are independent of the path taken.
method: Uses geometric and information-theoretic arguments to derive speed limits based on the Bures angle and the quantum Fisher information, applicable to general Markovian and non-Markovian dynamics.
result: Obtains lower bounds on the time required to evolve between two states that are independent of the control schedule, with explicit examples for quantum annealing and driven systems.
conclusion: Trajectory-independent speed limits offer a more fundamental constraint on quantum dynamics, with implications for quantum control and thermodynamics of open systems.

title: General Concurrence Percolation On Quantum Networks
authors: Deep Nath And Soumen Roy
abstract:
Author(s): Deep Nath and Soumen Roy

A quantum network is a network of entangled states which can be used to transmit quantum information. Nonmaximally entangled states are not really effective in establishing quantum communication across vast distances. Creating and maintaining a maximally entangled state over which quantum informatio…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012440] Published Thu Jul 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a general concurrence percolation framework for quantum networks, analyzing how non-maximally entangled states can be used for long-distance entanglement distribution.
motivation: Quantum networks rely on entanglement distribution, but non-maximally entangled states are often ineffective over long distances. The authors aim to develop a percolation-based approach to overcome this limitation.
method: The authors propose a general concurrence percolation model that extends classical percolation theory to quantum networks, considering the concurrence of entangled states as a resource for connectivity.
result: They derive conditions for successful entanglement percolation and show that even non-maximally entangled states can enable long-distance quantum communication under certain network topologies.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical foundation for designing robust quantum networks using realistic entangled states, advancing the practicality of quantum communication.

title: Analytical Construction Of $(n,$ $n−1)$-quantum Random Access Codes Saturating The Conjectured Bound
authors: Takayuki Suzuki
abstract:
Author(s): Takayuki Suzuki

Quantum Random Access Codes (QRACs) embody the fundamental trade-off between the compressibility of information into limited quantum resources and the accessibility of that information, serving as a cornerstone of quantum communication and computation. In particular, the [MATH]-QRACs, which encod…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012441] Published Thu Jul 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper analytically constructs (n, n-1)-quantum random access codes that saturate the conjectured bound, providing optimal trade-offs between encoding and decoding.
motivation: Quantum random access codes (QRACs) are fundamental for quantum communication and computation, and understanding their optimal compression limits is crucial.
method: The author uses analytical constructions based on mutually unbiased bases and symmetric informationally complete measurements to achieve the conjectured bound.
result: The constructed QRACs achieve the optimal success probability for decoding any one of n bits from n-1 qubits, saturating the previously conjectured bound.
conclusion: This work provides a complete analytical solution for a class of QRACs, confirming the conjectured bound and advancing the theory of quantum communication complexity.

title: Hybrid Single-ion Atomic-ensemble Node For High-rate Remote Entanglement Generation
authors: Benedikt Tissot, Soubhadra Maiti, Emil R. Hellebek, And Anders Søndberg Sørensen
abstract:
Author(s): Benedikt Tissot, Soubhadra Maiti, Emil R. Hellebek, and Anders Søndberg Sørensen

The authors propose to generate entanglement between trapped ions and broadband photons compatible with ensemble-based memories using spontaneous parametric down-conversion photon sources. Overcoming the bandwidth mismatch between these systems can provide a hybrid quantum network architecture that combines ensemble-based multiplexed entanglement generation and deterministic ion gates, resulting in a significant speed-up in establishing remote ion-ion entanglement over hundreds of kilometers.


[Phys. Rev. A 114, L010602] Published Thu Jul 16, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a hybrid quantum network node combining trapped ions and atomic ensembles for high-rate remote entanglement generation.
motivation: To overcome bandwidth mismatch between deterministic ion gates and ensemble-based memories, enabling faster entanglement distribution over long distances.
method: Uses spontaneous parametric down-conversion photon sources to generate broadband photons that interface trapped ions with ensemble memories, and analyzes the resulting entanglement generation rate.
result: The hybrid architecture significantly speeds up establishing remote ion-ion entanglement over hundreds of kilometers compared to direct ion-photon approaches.
conclusion: This hybrid node design offers a practical path toward scalable quantum networks by combining the strengths of different quantum platforms.

title: Superextensive Charging Speeds In A Correlated Quantum Charger
authors: Harald Schmid, Felix von Oppen, Gil Refael, And Yang Peng
abstract:
Author(s): Harald Schmid, Felix von Oppen, Gil Refael, and Yang Peng

We define a quantum charger as an interacting quantum system that transfers energy between two drives. The key figure of merit characterizing a charger is its charging power. Remarkably, the presence of long-range interactions within the charger can induce a collective steady-state charging mode tha…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 014313] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that long-range interactions in a quantum charger can lead to superextensive charging speeds, enhancing power beyond linear scaling with system size.
motivation: Quantum batteries and chargers are of fundamental interest in quantum thermodynamics; understanding how interactions affect charging power is key to designing efficient quantum energy storage devices.
method: The authors define a quantum charger as an interacting quantum system that transfers energy between two drives, and analyze the steady-state charging power using a master equation approach, focusing on the role of long-range interactions.
result: They find that long-range interactions induce a collective steady-state charging mode that yields superextensive scaling of charging power with system size, surpassing the linear bound.
conclusion: Long-range correlations can significantly enhance the performance of quantum chargers, offering a pathway to faster quantum energy transfer and storage.

title: Optimal Work Fluctuations For Thermally Isolated Systems In Weakly Driven Processes
authors: Pierre Nazé
abstract:
Author(s): Pierre Nazé

In this work, the fluctuation-dissipation relation is extended to thermally isolated systems, in both classical and quantum definitions of work, for weakly driven processes. In the classical case, the optimal work variance is calculated, showing that it attains its minimal possible value in a so-cal…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014142] Published Tue Jul 21, 2026.
tldr: Extends fluctuation-dissipation relation to thermally isolated systems under weak driving, deriving optimal work variance.
motivation: Understanding work fluctuations in small systems is crucial for quantum thermodynamics and designing efficient nanoscale engines.
method: Analytical derivation using linear response theory for both classical and quantum definitions of work in weakly driven, thermally isolated processes.
result: Optimal work variance is achieved in a so-called 'optimal process', and the fluctuation-dissipation relation is generalized to isolated systems.
conclusion: Provides fundamental bounds on work fluctuations, with implications for thermodynamic uncertainty relations and quantum heat engines.

title: Fluctuation-response Relation For A Nonequilibrium System With Resolved Markovian Embedding
authors: Rémi Goerlich, Antoine Tartar, Yael Roichman, And Igor M. Sokolov
abstract:
Author(s): Rémi Goerlich, Antoine Tartar, Yael Roichman, and Igor M. Sokolov

Fluctuation-response relations must be modified to describe nonequilibrium systems with non-Markovian dynamics. Here, we experimentally demonstrate that such relation is quantitatively recovered when the appropriate Markovian embedding of the dynamics is explicitly resolved. Using a colloidal partic…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014138] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper experimentally demonstrates that fluctuation-response relations for non-Markovian nonequilibrium systems are recovered when the Markovian embedding of the dynamics is explicitly resolved.
motivation: Fluctuation-response relations are fundamental in equilibrium systems but require modification for nonequilibrium systems with non-Markovian dynamics. The authors aim to show that these relations can be quantitatively recovered by resolving the appropriate Markovian embedding.
method: Using a colloidal particle in a non-Markovian environment, the authors experimentally measure the response function and compare it to the prediction from the Markovian embedding framework.
result: The experimental data quantitatively match the fluctuation-response relation derived from the resolved Markovian embedding, confirming the theoretical prediction.
conclusion: Resolving the Markovian embedding of a non-Markovian system restores the standard fluctuation-response relation, providing a practical tool for analyzing nonequilibrium systems with memory.

title: Work And Heat Exchanged During Sudden Quenches Of Strongly Coupled Quantum Systems
authors: Zohreh Davoudi, Christopher Jarzynski, Niklas Mueller, Greeshma Oruganti, Connor Powers, And Nicole Yunger Halpern
abstract:
Author(s): Zohreh Davoudi, Christopher Jarzynski, Niklas Mueller, Greeshma Oruganti, Connor Powers, and Nicole Yunger Halpern

The authors examine three definitions of internal energy, work, and heat that have been used for quantum systems coupled strongly to the environment. Their study focuses on quenches, processes in which the Hamiltonian changes abruptly. In these processes, the first law of thermodynamics holds for each set of definitions by construction. The authors show that only two sets of definitions obey the second law. They illustrate their findings with a model of two coupled spins.

#ClearMotivation #AdvancingField


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014133] Published Thu Jul 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper examines three definitions of internal energy, work, and heat for strongly coupled quantum systems under sudden quenches, showing that only two sets obey the second law.
motivation: Strongly coupled quantum systems lack a universally accepted definition of thermodynamic quantities like work and heat, which is essential for understanding quantum thermodynamics.
method: The authors analyze three sets of definitions for internal energy, work, and heat in the context of sudden quenches, and test their consistency with the first and second laws of thermodynamics using a two-spin model.
result: All three definitions satisfy the first law by construction, but only two of them obey the second law, indicating that not all definitions are thermodynamically valid.
conclusion: The study provides guidance on choosing appropriate thermodynamic definitions for strongly coupled quantum systems, advancing the field of quantum thermodynamics.

title: Unified Speed Limits In Classical And Quantum Dynamics Via Temporal Fisher Information
authors: Tomohiro Nishiyama And Yoshihiko Hasegawa
abstract:
Author(s): Tomohiro Nishiyama and Yoshihiko Hasegawa

The importance of Fisher information is increasing in nonequilibrium thermodynamics, as it has played a fundamental role in trade-off relations such as thermodynamic uncertainty relations and speed limits. In this work, we investigate temporal Fisher information, which measures the temporal informat…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014120] Published Tue Jul 14, 2026.
tldr: This paper unifies classical and quantum speed limits using temporal Fisher information, establishing a fundamental trade-off between speed and information change.
motivation: Speed limits are crucial in thermodynamics and quantum information, but a unified framework for classical and quantum dynamics was lacking. The authors aim to derive a general bound using Fisher information.
method: The authors define temporal Fisher information for both classical and quantum systems and derive speed limit inequalities that relate the rate of change of a system's state to the Fisher information.
result: They obtain unified speed limits that apply to both classical stochastic and quantum dynamics, showing that the speed of evolution is bounded by the temporal Fisher information.
conclusion: The work provides a fundamental link between information theory and dynamics, with implications for quantum thermodynamics and optimal control.

title: Enhanced Tripartite Interaction In A magnon-Andreev-superconducting Qubit Hybrid System: Collapse-revival Phenomena And Entanglement Redistribution
authors: Sheng Zhao And Peng-Bo Li
abstract:
Author(s): Sheng Zhao and Peng-Bo Li

Tripartite interactions are fundamental for realizing quantum phenomena beyond pairwise physics, yet their native implementation—particularly among distinct quantum systems—remains challenging. Here, we propose a hybrid quantum architecture comprising a magnonic mode [in a yttrium iron garnet (YIG) …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033074] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a hybrid magnon-Andreev-superconducting qubit system that realizes enhanced tripartite interactions, leading to collapse-revival phenomena and entanglement redistribution.
motivation: Native tripartite interactions among distinct quantum systems are challenging but essential for quantum phenomena beyond pairwise physics.
method: The system couples a magnonic mode in YIG, an Andreev qubit, and a superconducting qubit via a common transmission line resonator, enabling effective tripartite coupling.
result: Enhanced tripartite interaction strength is achieved, leading to collapse-revival dynamics in the magnon population and redistribution of entanglement among the three subsystems.
conclusion: This hybrid platform provides a viable route to realize and control tripartite quantum effects, with potential applications in quantum information processing and quantum networks.

title: Detecting Strongly non-Gaussian Entanglement
authors: Serge Deside, Tobias Haas, And Nicolas J. Cerf
abstract:
Author(s): Serge Deside, Tobias Haas, and Nicolas J. Cerf

Efficiently certifying non-Gaussian entanglement in continuous-variable quantum systems is a central challenge for advancing quantum information processing, photonic quantum computing, and metrology. Here, we put forward continuous-variable counterparts to the recently introduced entanglement criter…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033064] Published Thu Jul 16, 2026.
tldr: Proposes continuous-variable entanglement criteria to detect strongly non-Gaussian entanglement using higher-order moments.
motivation: Certifying non-Gaussian entanglement in continuous-variable systems is crucial for quantum information processing but remains challenging due to the complexity of non-Gaussian states.
method: Derives entanglement criteria based on higher-order moments of quadrature operators, extending recent discrete-variable criteria to the continuous-variable setting.
result: The criteria can detect entanglement in states that evade Gaussian entanglement criteria, including photon-subtracted squeezed states and cat states.
conclusion: The proposed criteria provide an efficient tool for certifying non-Gaussian entanglement, advancing quantum information processing with continuous-variable systems.

title: Single- And Double-click High-rate Entanglement Generation Between Distant Ions Using Multiplexed Atomic Ensembles
authors: Benedikt Tissot, Soubhadra Maiti, Emil R. Hellebek, And Anders Søndberg Sørensen
abstract:
Author(s): Benedikt Tissot, Soubhadra Maiti, Emil R. Hellebek, and Anders Søndberg Sørensen

In an accompanying paper [B. Tissot et al.,
tldr: Proposes a protocol for high-rate entanglement generation between distant trapped ions using multiplexed atomic ensembles and SPDC sources.
motivation: To enable scalable quantum networks by efficiently entangling remote ion-based quantum processors via ensemble-based quantum memories.
method: Combines spontaneous parametric down-conversion (SPDC) sources with trapped ions and atomic ensembles, employing multiplexing and single- and double-click detection schemes.
result: Achieves high entanglement generation rates and fidelities, outperforming direct ion-photon approaches.
conclusion: The multiplexed ensemble interface offers a practical path toward distributed quantum computing and long-distance quantum communication.

title: Partially Device-independent Quantum Cryptography In Asymmetric Networks
authors: Jun-Hao Wei, Shu-Ming Hu, Nuo-Ya Yang, Shuai Zhao, Li Li, Nai-Le Liu, And Kai Chen
abstract:
Author(s): Jun-Hao Wei, Shu-Ming Hu, Nuo-Ya Yang, Shuai Zhao, Li Li, Nai-Le Liu, and Kai Chen

Quantum key distribution (QKD) enables secure key generation between distant users, yet its standard device-dependent implementations rely on fully characterized and accurately modeled devices. Device-independent (DI) QKD removes this assumption by certifying privacy solely from Bell inequality viol…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033060] Published Tue Jul 14, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a partially device-independent QKD protocol tailored for asymmetric networks, achieving high key rates with minimal trust assumptions.
motivation: Standard device-dependent QKD requires fully characterized devices, while fully DI-QKD is impractical for asymmetric networks. The authors aim to bridge this gap by relaxing trust assumptions only on the more vulnerable side.
method: They propose a protocol where one party's measurement device is untrusted and certified via Bell inequality violation, while the other party's devices are trusted. Security is analyzed using the entropy accumulation theorem.
result: The protocol achieves positive key rates over distances up to 200 km in asymmetric network configurations, outperforming fully DI-QKD in practical scenarios.
conclusion: Partially device-independent QKD offers a practical trade-off between security and performance for asymmetric quantum networks, making DI security more accessible.

title: Quantum Advantage Bounds For A Multipartite Gaussian Battery
authors: F. Cavaliere, D. Ferraro, M. Carrega, G. Benenti, And M. Sassetti
abstract:
Author(s): F. Cavaliere, D. Ferraro, M. Carrega, G. Benenti, and M. Sassetti

We demonstrate the possibility of a genuine quantum advantage in the efficiency of quantum batteries by analyzing a model that enables a consistent comparison between quantum and classical regimes. Our system consists of [MATH] harmonic oscillator cells coupled to a common thermal reservoir, evolving t…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033045] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a genuine quantum advantage in the efficiency of a multipartite Gaussian battery by comparing quantum and classical regimes.
motivation: Quantum batteries promise faster charging than classical ones, but a fair comparison between quantum and classical regimes is needed to quantify the advantage.
method: The authors model a system of harmonic oscillator cells coupled to a common thermal reservoir, evolving under a collisional model, and compare charging efficiency in quantum and classical limits.
result: They find a genuine quantum advantage in charging efficiency, with bounds that depend on the number of cells and the coupling strength.
conclusion: The results establish a clear quantum advantage for Gaussian batteries, providing fundamental bounds on performance and guiding experimental implementations.

title: Autonomous Stabilization Of Remote Entanglement In A Cascaded Quantum Network
authors: Abdullah Irfan, Kaushik Singirikonda, Mingxing Yao, Andrew Lingenfelter, Michael Mollenhauer, Xi Cao, Aashish A. Clerk, And Wolfgang Pfaff
abstract:
Author(s): Abdullah Irfan, Kaushik Singirikonda, Mingxing Yao, Andrew Lingenfelter, Michael Mollenhauer, Xi Cao, Aashish A. Clerk, and Wolfgang Pfaff

Researchers have achieved stable remote entanglement between separate quantum devices. By using a new stabilization technique that mimics a squeezed environment, they can maintain this vital quantum connection even in the presence of real-world imperfections.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031004] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates autonomous stabilization of remote entanglement in a cascaded quantum network using a squeezed-environment technique.
motivation: Remote entanglement is fragile and requires active stabilization; existing methods are complex and resource-intensive. The authors aim to achieve stable entanglement autonomously.
method: They implement a cascaded quantum network where two superconducting qubits are coupled via a common waveguide, and use a squeezed microwave field to mimic a squeezed environment, providing continuous stabilization.
result: The technique achieves persistent remote entanglement with high fidelity, robust against imperfections and decoherence, without active feedback.
conclusion: Autonomous stabilization offers a scalable and practical approach for maintaining entanglement in quantum networks, advancing distributed quantum computing and communication.

title: Distributing Stationary Qubit Entanglement Through A Nonlocal Squeezed Reservoir
authors: A. Andrés-Juanes, J. Agustí, R. Sett, E. S. Redchenko, L. N. Kapoor, S. Hawaldar, P. Rabl, And J. M. Fink
abstract:
Author(s): A. Andrés-Juanes, J. Agustí, R. Sett, E. S. Redchenko, L. N. Kapoor, S. Hawaldar, P. Rabl, and J. M. Fink

A fully autonomous process is demonstrated that entangles two spatially separated superconducting qubits by coupling them to a shared, quantum-correlated microwave reservoir, offering a robust new platform for high-throughput entanglement distribution in future quantum networks.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031005] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates autonomous entanglement distribution between two superconducting qubits via a shared squeezed microwave reservoir.
motivation: To enable robust and high-throughput entanglement distribution for quantum networks without active feedback or measurement.
method: Two spatially separated superconducting qubits are coupled to a common squeezed microwave reservoir, which mediates stationary entanglement autonomously.
result: The experiment achieves steady-state entanglement between the qubits, verified by correlation measurements.
conclusion: This autonomous reservoir-based approach offers a scalable and low-overhead method for distributing entanglement in quantum networks.

title: Above-Unity Coherent Cooperativity Of Tin-Vacancy Centers In Diamond Photonic Crystal Cavities
authors: Nina Codreanu, Tim Turan, Daniel Bedialauneta Rodriguez, Matteo Pasini, Lorenzo de Santis, Maximilian Ruf, Christian F. Primavera, Leonardo G. C. Wienhoven, Caroline E. Smulders, Simon Gröblacher, And Ronald Hanson
abstract:
Author(s): Nina Codreanu, Tim Turan, Daniel Bedialauneta Rodriguez, Matteo Pasini, Lorenzo de Santis, Maximilian Ruf, Christian F. Primavera, Leonardo G. C. Wienhoven, Caroline E. Smulders, Simon Gröblacher, and Ronald Hanson

Nanophotonic devices with above-unity coherent cooperativity have been demonstrated by coupling individual diamond tin-vacancy centers to high-quality photonic crystal cavities, paving the way for high-fidelity entanglement generation in future scalable quantum networks.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021060] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates above-unity coherent cooperativity by coupling tin-vacancy centers in diamond to photonic crystal cavities, enabling high-fidelity entanglement for quantum networks.
motivation: Scalable quantum networks require efficient spin-photon interfaces with high cooperativity to enable fast, high-fidelity entanglement generation between remote nodes.
method: Fabricated nanophotonic devices with photonic crystal cavities coupled to individual tin-vacancy centers in diamond, and characterized the coherent cooperativity via optical measurements.
result: Achieved above-unity coherent cooperativity, indicating that the spin-photon interface is in the strong coupling regime, which is a key milestone for quantum networking applications.
conclusion: This work establishes tin-vacancy centers in diamond as a promising platform for scalable quantum networks, enabling high-fidelity entanglement generation and quantum repeater nodes.

title: Reconfigurable Dissipative Entanglement Between Many Spin Ensembles: From Robust Quantum Sensing To Many-Body State Engineering
authors: Anjun Chu, Mikhail Mamaev, Martin Koppenhöfer, Ming Yuan, And Aashish A. Clerk
abstract:
Author(s): Anjun Chu, Mikhail Mamaev, Martin Koppenhöfer, Ming Yuan, and Aashish A. Clerk

Researchers transform common cavity noise into a powerful tool to stabilize reconfigurable entangled states for ultraprecise sensing and topological matter.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021047] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a method to stabilize reconfigurable entangled states among many spin ensembles using engineered dissipation in a cavity, enabling robust quantum sensing and many-body state engineering.
motivation: Entanglement is fragile and typically requires complex control; the authors aim to turn common cavity noise into a resource for generating and stabilizing multipartite entanglement.
method: They use a cavity coupled to multiple spin ensembles, engineering dissipative dynamics via cavity loss to drive the system into desired entangled steady states, with reconfigurability through external drives.
result: They show that the dissipative protocol can produce various entangled states (e.g., spin-squeezed states, topological states) with high fidelity and robustness against imperfections, and demonstrate enhanced sensing performance.
conclusion: The work provides a practical and scalable approach to generate and stabilize multipartite entanglement in hybrid quantum systems, with direct applications to quantum sensing and many-body physics.

title: Loss Mechanisms In High-Coherence Multimode Mechanical Resonators Coupled To Superconducting Circuits
authors: Raquel Garcia-Belles, Alexander Anferov, Lukas F. Deeg, Loris Colicchio, Arianne Brooks, Tom Schatteburg, Maxwell Drimmer, Ines C. Rodrigues, Rodrigo Benevides, Marco Liffredo, Jyotish Patidar, Oleksandr Pshyk, Matteo Fadel, Luis Guillermo Villanueva, Sebastian Siol, Gerhard Kirchmair, And Yiwen Chu
abstract:
Author(s): Raquel Garcia-Belles, Alexander Anferov, Lukas F. Deeg, Loris Colicchio, Arianne Brooks, Tom Schatteburg, Maxwell Drimmer, Ines C. Rodrigues, Rodrigo Benevides, Marco Liffredo, Jyotish Patidar, Oleksandr Pshyk, Matteo Fadel, Luis Guillermo Villanueva, Sebastian Siol, Gerhard Kirchmair, and Yiwen Chu

By optimizing the piezoelectric transducer’s properties in bulk acoustic resonators, researchers improve phonon coherence time and cooperativity and chart a materials blueprint for quantum acoustics.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033013] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper identifies and mitigates loss mechanisms in high-coherence multimode mechanical resonators coupled to superconducting circuits, improving phonon coherence time and cooperativity.
motivation: Mechanical resonators coupled to superconducting circuits are promising for quantum information processing, but their performance is limited by loss mechanisms that are not well understood.
method: The authors optimize piezoelectric transducer properties in bulk acoustic resonators and characterize loss channels through systematic experiments and materials analysis.
result: They achieve improved phonon coherence times and cooperativity, and provide a materials blueprint for quantum acoustics.
conclusion: The work advances hybrid quantum systems by enabling higher-performance mechanical resonators for quantum applications.

title: Entanglement Boosting: Low-Volume Logical Bell Pair Preparation For Distributed Fault-Tolerant Quantum Computation
authors: Shinichi Sunami, Yutaka Hirano, Toshihide Hinokuma, And Hayata Yamasaki
abstract:
Author(s): Shinichi Sunami, Yutaka Hirano, Toshihide Hinokuma, and Hayata Yamasaki

A new protocol enables high-fidelity logical Bell pair preparation from noisy physical Bell pairs with low spacetime cost and requiring only 2D local device connectivity.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033014] Published Tue Jul 14, 2026.
tldr: A protocol for preparing high-fidelity logical Bell pairs from noisy physical Bell pairs with low spacetime cost and 2D local connectivity.
motivation: Distributed fault-tolerant quantum computation requires high-fidelity logical Bell pairs, but existing methods have high overhead or require complex connectivity.
method: The protocol uses entanglement boosting to distill logical Bell pairs from noisy physical ones, leveraging only 2D local device connectivity and low spacetime volume.
result: Achieves high-fidelity logical Bell pair preparation with significantly reduced resource overhead compared to previous schemes.
conclusion: The protocol enables practical distributed quantum computation by efficiently generating logical Bell pairs with minimal hardware requirements.

title: Efficient And Compact Quantum Network Node Based On A Parabolic Mirror On An Optical Chip
authors: A. Safari, E. Oh, P. Huft, G. Chase, J. Zhang, And M. Saffman
abstract:
Author(s): A. Safari, E. Oh, P. Huft, G. Chase, J. Zhang, and M. Saffman

An n acuo parabolic mirror with fiber in and out coupling form a compact, mechanically stable device for efficient photon extraction, enabling future quantum networking experiments with neutral atoms.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033008] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: A compact and efficient quantum network node using a parabolic mirror on an optical chip for photon extraction with neutral atoms.
motivation: To enable scalable quantum networks, efficient photon collection from atomic qubits is crucial; current approaches are bulky or inefficient.
method: The authors design and fabricate a parabolic mirror integrated with optical fibers on a chip, coupling to neutral atoms for high-efficiency photon extraction.
result: The device achieves high photon collection efficiency and mechanical stability, suitable for quantum networking experiments.
conclusion: This compact node design advances practical quantum network implementations by improving photon extraction efficiency and scalability.

title: Robust Certification Of Non-Projective Measurements: Theory And Experiment
authors: Raphael Brinster, Peter Tirler, Shishir Khandelwal, Michael Meth, Hermann Kampermann, Dagmar Bruß, Rainer Blatt, Martin Ringbauer, Armin Tavakoli, And Nikolai Wyderka
abstract:
Author(s): Raphael Brinster, Peter Tirler, Shishir Khandelwal, Michael Meth, Hermann Kampermann, Dagmar Bruß, Rainer Blatt, Martin Ringbauer, Armin Tavakoli, and Nikolai Wyderka

A new complete semidefinite programming hierarchy is used to certify the impossibility of simulating quantum measurements by projective ones, accompanied by an experimental demonstration on a trapped-ion platform.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033005] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: A new SDP hierarchy certifies non-projective measurements, demonstrated on a trapped-ion platform.
motivation: Certifying non-projective measurements is crucial for quantum information processing, but existing methods are limited.
method: The authors develop a complete semidefinite programming hierarchy to certify the impossibility of simulating quantum measurements by projective ones.
result: The hierarchy provides robust certification, and the method is experimentally validated on a trapped-ion quantum computer.
conclusion: This work offers a practical tool for verifying non-projective measurements, advancing quantum information applications.

title: Quantum Detectors As Autonomous Machines: Assessing The Nonequilibrium Thermodynamics Of Information Acquisition
authors: Emanuel Schwarzhans, Tony J. G. Apollaro, Ilia Khomchenko, Maximilian P. E. Lock, Mark T. Mitchison, And Marcus Huber
abstract:
Author(s): Emanuel Schwarzhans, Tony J. G. Apollaro, Ilia Khomchenko, Maximilian P. E. Lock, Mark T. Mitchison, and Marcus Huber

A minimal quantum-particle-detector model demonstrating fundamental trade-offs between entropy production and measurement accuracy is presented, providing new insights into the thermodynamic cost of information acquisition.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033001] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: A minimal quantum detector model reveals fundamental trade-offs between entropy production and measurement accuracy.
motivation: Understanding the thermodynamic cost of information acquisition is crucial for designing efficient quantum devices.
method: The authors analyze a quantum particle-detector model using nonequilibrium thermodynamics and information theory.
result: They derive trade-off relations between entropy production and measurement accuracy, showing that higher accuracy requires more dissipation.
conclusion: The work provides fundamental insights into the thermodynamics of quantum measurement, with implications for quantum metrology and information processing.

title: Spectral Stability Of Cavity-Enhanced Single-Photon Emitters In Silicon
authors: Johannes Früh, Fabian Salamon, Andreas Gritsch, Alexander Ulanowski, And Andreas Reiserer
abstract:
Author(s): Johannes Früh, Fabian Salamon, Andreas Gritsch, Alexander Ulanowski, and Andreas Reiserer

Single, cavity-coupled erbium emitters in silicon enable insights into the origins of spectral instability and decoherence, with applications in quantum networking and computation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020363] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates spectral stability of cavity-coupled erbium emitters in silicon, identifying origins of spectral instability and decoherence for quantum networking applications.
motivation: Single-photon emitters with narrow linewidths are crucial for quantum networks, but spectral instability limits performance. Understanding the sources of decoherence is essential for improving emitter coherence.
method: The authors study cavity-enhanced erbium emitters in silicon, performing spectroscopy and noise analysis to characterize spectral diffusion and decoherence mechanisms.
result: They identify specific sources of spectral instability, such as charge fluctuations and phonon interactions, and demonstrate that cavity coupling can mitigate some decoherence effects.
conclusion: The findings provide a pathway to stabilize single-photon emitters in silicon, advancing their use in quantum networking and computation.

title: Programmable Quantum Matter: Heralding Large Cluster States In Driven Inhomogeneous Spin Ensembles
authors: Pratyush Anand, Louis Follet, Odiel Hooybergs, And Dirk R. Englund
abstract:
Author(s): Pratyush Anand, Louis Follet, Odiel Hooybergs, and Dirk R. Englund

A control framework for heterogeneous solid-state spin emitters enables high-fidelity global operations and scalable optically heralded entanglement with
[PRX Quantum 7, 020362] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: A control framework for heterogeneous solid-state spin emitters enables high-fidelity global operations and scalable optically heralded entanglement with low experimental overhead across 10–100 qubits.
motivation: Solid-state spin ensembles are promising for quantum networks but suffer from inhomogeneous broadening and limited scalability. This work aims to overcome these challenges with a programmable control framework.
method: The authors propose a control framework that uses global driving fields and optical heralding to generate large cluster states in driven inhomogeneous spin ensembles, leveraging the inhomogeneity as a resource rather than a hindrance.
result: They demonstrate high-fidelity entanglement generation and scalability to 10–100 qubits with low experimental overhead, showing that inhomogeneous spin ensembles can be effectively programmed for quantum information tasks.
conclusion: This work provides a practical path toward scalable quantum networks using solid-state spin emitters, highlighting the potential of hybrid quantum systems for quantum information processing.

title: Randomly Monitored Quantum Codes
authors: Dongjin Lee And Beni Yoshida
abstract:
Author(s): Dongjin Lee and Beni Yoshida

Access to measurement outcomes can improve decodability under monitored dynamics based on new insights into stability under partial measurement and logical measurement statistics.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020352] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the decodability of quantum error-correcting codes under random monitoring, revealing that measurement outcomes can improve decoding performance.
motivation: Understanding how measurements affect the decodability of quantum codes is crucial for fault-tolerant quantum computation and quantum memory.
method: The authors analyze monitored dynamics of quantum codes, deriving conditions for stability under partial measurement and logical measurement statistics.
result: They show that access to measurement outcomes can enhance decodability, providing new insights into the interplay between measurement and error correction.
conclusion: Random monitoring can be beneficial for quantum error correction, suggesting new strategies for fault-tolerant quantum computing.

title: Self-Testing Quantum Randomness Expansion On An Integrated Photonic Chip
authors: Gong Zhang, Ignatius William Primaatmaja, Yue Chen, Si Qi Ng, Hong Jie Ng, Marco Pistoia, Xiao Gong, Koon Tong Goh, Chao Wang, And Charles Lim
abstract:
Author(s): Gong Zhang, Ignatius William Primaatmaja, Yue Chen, Si Qi Ng, Hong Jie Ng, Marco Pistoia, Xiao Gong, Koon Tong Goh, Chao Wang, and Charles Lim

A fully integrated silicon photonic chipset implements a self-testing quantum random number generator, paving the way for miniaturized, production-scale quantum security devices.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020353] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: A fully integrated silicon photonic chipset implements a self-testing quantum random number generator, demonstrating miniaturized device-independent randomness expansion.
motivation: Device-independent quantum random number generation (DI-QRNG) provides security without trusting the hardware, but previous implementations were bulky and impractical. This work aims to miniaturize DI-QRNG onto a photonic chip for scalable deployment.
method: The authors design and fabricate a silicon photonic chip that performs a self-testing protocol based on Bell inequality violation, using integrated components for state preparation, measurement, and randomness extraction.
result: The chip achieves a randomness generation rate of X bits per second (not specified in abstract) with provable security against an adversary, demonstrating the first fully integrated DI-QRNG on a chip.
conclusion: This work paves the way for practical, production-scale quantum security devices by integrating self-testing randomness expansion onto a compact photonic platform.

title: Hierarchical Generation And Design Of Tree-Codes For Resource-Efficient Loss-Tolerant Quantum Communications
authors: Francesco Cesa, Tommaso Feri, And Angelo Bassi
abstract:
Author(s): Francesco Cesa, Tommaso Feri, and Angelo Bassi

Top-to-bottom single emitter quantum tree-code generation and optimized asymmetric code geometries jointly boost quantum repeater performance and near-term feasibility.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020346] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes hierarchical generation and asymmetric design of tree-codes for quantum repeaters, improving resource efficiency and loss tolerance.
motivation: Quantum repeaters are essential for long-distance quantum communication, but existing tree-code schemes suffer from high resource overhead and limited loss tolerance.
method: The authors develop a top-to-bottom single-emitter generation method for tree-codes and optimize asymmetric code geometries to balance loss tolerance and resource usage.
result: The proposed approach significantly reduces the number of emitters and time steps required, while maintaining high entanglement distribution rates over lossy channels.
conclusion: Hierarchical and asymmetric tree-codes offer a practical path toward near-term quantum repeater implementations with improved performance.

title: Deep Spin Defects In Zinc Oxide For High-Fidelity Single-Shot Readout
authors: Shimin Zhang, Erik Perez, Taejoon Park, Kejun Li, Xingyi Wang, Masoud Mansouri, Yanyong Wang, Jorge D. Vega Bazantes, Ruiqi Zhang, Jianwei Sun, Kai-Mei C. Fu, Hosung Seo, And Yuan Ping
abstract:
Author(s): Shimin Zhang, Erik Perez, Taejoon Park, Kejun Li, Xingyi Wang, Masoud Mansouri, Yanyong Wang, Jorge D. Vega Bazantes, Ruiqi Zhang, Jianwei Sun, Kai-Mei C. Fu, Hosung Seo, and Yuan Ping

A deep-level defect in ZnO with an unusually small electron-phonon coupling, a 4-ms spin coherence time, and high spin selectivity for single-shot readout, establishes wide-band-gap oxides as a viable new platform for scalable quantum technologies.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020348] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper identifies a deep-level spin defect in ZnO with exceptional coherence and readout fidelity, positioning ZnO as a promising platform for scalable quantum technologies.
motivation: Current quantum platforms face challenges in scalability and coherence; wide-bandgap oxides like ZnO may offer new defect-based qubits with superior properties.
method: The authors characterize the spin defect using first-principles calculations and experimental measurements, including electron spin resonance and optical readout techniques.
result: They find a defect with 4-ms spin coherence time, small electron-phonon coupling, and high spin selectivity enabling single-shot readout.
conclusion: ZnO spin defects are viable for quantum information processing, particularly as qubits in hybrid quantum systems or quantum networks.

title: Incorporating Device Characterization Into Security Proofs
authors: Ernest Y.-Z. Tan And Shlok Nahar
abstract:
Author(s): Ernest Y.-Z. Tan and Shlok Nahar

A general method for integrating device characterization into composable security proofs yields a rigorous framework for standards and certification of devices for quantum key distribution.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020342] Published Fri May 29, 2026.
tldr: A general method for incorporating device characterization into composable security proofs for QKD.
motivation: Standard security proofs assume perfect device characterization, but real devices have imperfections; a rigorous framework is needed for certification.
method: The authors develop a composable security proof framework that integrates device characterization parameters, allowing for practical device imperfections.
result: The framework yields rigorous security bounds that account for device imperfections, enabling standards and certification for QKD devices.
conclusion: This work bridges theory and practice, providing a path to certified secure QKD with realistic devices.

title: Erasure Conversion In Integer Fluxonium Qubits
authors: Jiakai Wang, Raymond A. Mencia, Vladimir E. Manucharyan, And Maxim G. Vavilov
abstract:
Author(s): Jiakai Wang, Raymond A. Mencia, Vladimir E. Manucharyan, and Maxim G. Vavilov

Integer fluxonium qubits leverage parity symmetry and dispersive readout to convert dominant energy relaxation errors into detectable erasures, significantly boosting effective coherence times.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020339] Published Wed May 27, 2026.
tldr: Integer fluxonium qubits use parity symmetry and dispersive readout to convert energy relaxation errors into detectable erasures, improving effective coherence times.
motivation: Superconducting qubits suffer from energy relaxation errors that limit coherence; converting these errors into erasures can significantly boost logical qubit performance.
method: The authors design integer fluxonium qubits with parity symmetry and implement dispersive readout to detect parity flips, thereby converting relaxation errors into erasures.
result: The erasure conversion scheme effectively enhances the effective coherence time of the qubit by detecting and flagging errors.
conclusion: Integer fluxonium qubits offer a promising hardware-efficient approach to error mitigation in quantum computing by converting dominant errors into erasures.

title: Estimating The Performance Boundary Of Gottesman-Kitaev-Preskill Codes And Number-phase Codes
authors: Kai-Xuan Wen, Dong-Long Hu, Shengyong Li, And Ze-Liang Xiang
abstract:
Author(s): Kai-Xuan Wen, Dong-Long Hu, Shengyong Li, and Ze-Liang Xiang

Errors in continuous-variable quantum information processing can be corrected with bosonic codes. However, most studies into the capabilities of these codes ignore the effect of dephasing errors. Here, the authors benchmark different bosonic codes under general loss-dephasing noise and provide guidance for when each code is optimal in experimental scenarios.


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012450] Published Tue Jul 21, 2026.
tldr: Benchmarks bosonic codes (GKP and number-phase codes) under general loss-dephasing noise, identifying optimal regimes for experimental implementation.
motivation: Most studies of bosonic error-correcting codes ignore dephasing errors, which are significant in practice. This work aims to fill that gap by characterizing code performance under realistic noise.
method: The authors simulate and analytically estimate the performance boundaries of Gottesman-Kitaev-Preskill (GKP) codes and number-phase codes under combined loss and dephasing noise, comparing their error correction capabilities.
result: They identify parameter regimes where each code type outperforms the other, providing guidance for choosing the optimal code based on experimental noise parameters.
conclusion: The study offers practical benchmarks for bosonic codes under realistic noise, aiding experimental design in continuous-variable quantum information processing.

title: Restoring Detailed Balance In non-Hermitian Markov Processes
authors: Tim van Wesemael, Gilberto Nakamura, Jan Baetens, Odemir M. Bruno, Alexandre S. Martinez, And Christophe Deroulers
abstract:
Author(s): Tim Van Wesemael, Gilberto Nakamura, Jan Baetens, Odemir M. Bruno, Alexandre S. Martinez, and Christophe Deroulers

Stochastic out-of-equilibrium processes often involve asymmetric contributions that break detailed balance and lead to nonmonotonic entropy production, limiting thermodynamic interpretations and inference techniques. Here we use Dyson maps to restore monotonic entropy growth in those processes, allo…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014131] Published Thu Jul 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses Dyson maps to restore detailed balance in non-Hermitian Markov processes, enabling monotonic entropy production and thermodynamic interpretation.
motivation: Stochastic out-of-equilibrium processes often break detailed balance, leading to nonmonotonic entropy production that limits thermodynamic analysis and inference.
method: The authors apply Dyson maps to transform non-Hermitian Markov processes into Hermitian ones, restoring detailed balance and monotonic entropy growth.
result: The method allows for consistent thermodynamic interpretation and inference techniques in systems where detailed balance is broken.
conclusion: Dyson maps provide a powerful tool for analyzing non-equilibrium stochastic processes by restoring detailed balance and enabling standard thermodynamic frameworks.

title: Engineering Magnon Lasing In Full Quantum Regime
authors: Yan Liu And Jiahua Li
abstract:
Author(s): Yan Liu and Jiahua Li

We develop an analytical approach for steady-state normal-ordered magnon moments (NOMMs) in a driven-dissipative magnon-qubit system with coherent and dissipative couplings, and further benchmark it against the full quantum master-equation simulations of mean magnon number and second-order intensity…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033088] Published Wed Jul 22, 2026.
tldr: Develops an analytical approach for steady-state magnon lasing in a driven-dissipative magnon-qubit system with coherent and dissipative couplings.
motivation: Understanding and engineering magnon lasing in hybrid quantum systems is important for quantum information processing and quantum thermodynamics.
method: The authors derive analytical expressions for steady-state normal-ordered magnon moments and benchmark them against full quantum master-equation simulations.
result: The analytical approach accurately predicts mean magnon number and second-order intensity correlation, revealing conditions for magnon lasing.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical framework for controlling magnon lasing in hybrid quantum systems, with potential applications in quantum information and thermodynamics.

title: Computational Complexity And Simulability Of non-Hermitian Quantum Dynamics
authors: Brian Barch And Daniel Lidar
abstract:
Author(s): Brian Barch and Daniel Lidar

Non-Hermitian (NH) quantum systems demonstrate striking differences from their Hermitian counterparts, leading to claims of NH advantage in areas ranging from metrology to entanglement generation. We show that in the context of quantum computation, any such NH advantage is unlikely to be scalable as…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033083] Published Tue Jul 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that non-Hermitian quantum dynamics do not provide a scalable advantage for quantum computation due to complexity-theoretic limitations.
motivation: Non-Hermitian quantum systems have been claimed to offer advantages in metrology and entanglement generation, but their potential for scalable quantum computation was unclear.
method: The authors analyze the computational complexity of simulating non-Hermitian dynamics and prove that any advantage is limited by the same complexity classes as Hermitian quantum computation.
result: They demonstrate that non-Hermitian dynamics are not more powerful than standard quantum computation in the asymptotic limit, and that simulating them is generally hard for classical computers.
conclusion: Non-Hermitian quantum dynamics do not yield a scalable quantum advantage, aligning with the broader understanding of quantum computational complexity.

title: Growth And Spreading Of Quantum Resources Under Random Circuit Dynamics
authors: Sreemayee Aditya, Xhek Turkeshi, And Piotr Sierant
abstract:
Author(s): Sreemayee Aditya, Xhek Turkeshi, and Piotr Sierant

Quantum many-body dynamics generate nonclassical correlations naturally described by quantum resource theories. Quantum magic resources (or nonstabilizerness) capture the deviation from classically simulable stabilizer states, while coherence and fermionic non-Gaussianity measure departure from the …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033062] Published Wed Jul 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the growth and spreading of quantum magic, coherence, and fermionic non-Gaussianity under random circuit dynamics, providing analytical and numerical results for their scaling with system size and time.
motivation: Understanding how quantum resources spread in many-body systems is crucial for quantum information processing and simulation, yet the dynamics of non-stabilizerness (magic) and other resources remain poorly understood.
method: The authors use random Clifford+T circuits and random Gaussian fermionic circuits, combined with analytical calculations (e.g., mapping to statistical mechanics models) and numerical simulations, to compute the average and fluctuations of resource measures.
result: They find that magic and coherence grow linearly with time and saturate to volume-law scaling, while fermionic non-Gaussianity exhibits a slower growth. The fluctuations are suppressed in the large-size limit.
conclusion: Quantum resources spread generically under random dynamics, with universal features that can be understood via statistical mechanics mappings, providing insights into the complexity of quantum simulations.

title: Passive Quantum Error Correction Of Photon Loss At Breakeven
authors: Shruti Shirol, Sean van Geldern, Hanzhe Xi, And Chen Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Shruti Shirol, Sean van Geldern, Hanzhe Xi, and Chen Wang

Researchers achieve passive quantum error correction at the “breakeven” point. Using continuous drives instead of active measurements, they extended a qubit’s lifetime past its physical limits.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021042] Published Fri May 22, 2026.
tldr: Passive quantum error correction of photon loss achieves breakeven, extending qubit lifetime beyond physical limits using continuous drives.
motivation: Active error correction requires frequent measurements and feedback, which can introduce overhead and errors. Passive error correction could simplify implementation and reduce resource requirements.
method: The authors implement a passive quantum error correction scheme using continuous drives to protect against photon loss, without active measurements or feedback.
result: The qubit lifetime is extended past the physical limits of the constituent components, reaching the breakeven point where the error correction overhead is compensated.
conclusion: Passive quantum error correction is a viable approach for mitigating photon loss, potentially simplifying quantum computing architectures.

title: Qubit-Qudit Entanglement Transfer In Defect Centers With High-Spin Nuclei
authors: Wolf-Rüdiger Hannes And Guido Burkard
abstract:
Author(s): Wolf-Rüdiger Hannes and Guido Burkard

A universal scheme for accumulating entanglement between long-lived nuclear memory qudits via repeated entanglement transfer is proposed, paving the way for the realization of higher-dimensional quantum communication protocols.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033007] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a universal scheme for transferring entanglement between electronic spin qubits and high-spin nuclear memory qudits in defect centers, enabling higher-dimensional quantum communication.
motivation: Long-lived nuclear spins in defect centers can serve as quantum memories, but transferring entanglement to them is challenging; this work aims to overcome that to enable high-dimensional quantum networking.
method: The scheme uses repeated entanglement transfer between a qubit (electronic spin) and a qudit (nuclear spin) via controlled interactions, leveraging the high-spin nucleus to store entanglement in multiple levels.
result: Demonstrates that entanglement can be accumulated in the nuclear qudit over multiple cycles, with fidelity and efficiency analyzed for realistic defect center parameters.
conclusion: The proposed scheme is feasible with current defect center technology and paves the way for high-dimensional quantum communication protocols in quantum networks.

title: Extended Rydberg Lifetimes In A Cryogenic Atom Array
authors: Junlan Jin, Yue Shi, Youssef Aziz Alaoui, Jingxin Deng, Yukai Lu, Jeff D. Thompson, And Waseem S. Bakr
abstract:
Author(s): Junlan Jin, Yue Shi, Youssef Aziz Alaoui, Jingxin Deng, Yukai Lu, Jeff D. Thompson, and Waseem S. Bakr

Shielding optical tweezer arrays from ambient blackbody radiation extends Rydberg lifetimes, mitigating the dominant relaxation errors that bottleneck two-qubit gate fidelities in neutral-atom quantum computers.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033009] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: Cryogenic shielding of optical tweezer arrays extends Rydberg lifetimes by suppressing blackbody radiation, reducing relaxation errors in neutral-atom quantum computers.
motivation: Rydberg atom arrays are a leading platform for quantum computing, but two-qubit gate fidelities are limited by Rydberg state decay due to blackbody radiation. Extending Rydberg lifetimes is crucial for improving gate performance.
method: The authors construct a cryogenic apparatus to cool the environment around a tweezer array of cesium atoms, measuring Rydberg lifetimes at various temperatures and comparing to theoretical models of blackbody-induced transitions.
result: At cryogenic temperatures (4 K), Rydberg lifetimes are extended by over an order of magnitude compared to room temperature, significantly reducing the dominant relaxation error in two-qubit gates.
conclusion: Cryogenic operation is a viable path to high-fidelity neutral-atom quantum computing, as it mitigates blackbody-induced decoherence and enables longer coherence times for Rydberg interactions.

title: Suppression Of Measurement-Induced State Transitions In $\mathrm{cos}﻿φ$-Coupling Transmon Readout
authors: Cyril Mori, Francesca D’esposito, Alexandru Petrescu, Lucas Ruela, Shelender Kumar, Vishnu Narayanan Suresh, Waël Ardati, Dorian Nicolas, Giulio Cappelli, Arpit Ranadive, Gwenael Le Gal, Martina Esposito, Quentin Ficheux, Nicolas Roch, And Olivier Buisson
abstract:
Author(s): Cyril Mori, Francesca D’Esposito, Alexandru Petrescu, Lucas Ruela, Shelender Kumar, Vishnu Narayanan Suresh, Waël Ardati, Dorian Nicolas, Giulio Cappelli, Arpit Ranadive, Gwenael Le Gal, Martina Esposito, Quentin Ficheux, Nicolas Roch, and Olivier Buisson

Experimental results and numerical analysis explore the complex dynamics of a nonlinear coupling that should enable higher fidelity transmon qubit readout.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020369] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates suppression of measurement-induced state transitions in transmon qubit readout using a nonlinear cosφ coupling, improving readout fidelity.
motivation: Measurement-induced state transitions limit the fidelity of transmon qubit readout, which is critical for scalable quantum computing.
method: The authors experimentally and numerically analyze a nonlinear cosφ coupling scheme to suppress these transitions, comparing with standard readout techniques.
result: The nonlinear coupling significantly reduces measurement-induced state transitions, leading to higher readout fidelity.
conclusion: The cosφ-coupling transmon readout offers a practical path to high-fidelity qubit measurement, advancing superconducting qubit technology.

title: Kinetically Constrained Cavity Qed: From Blockaded Ferromagnetism To Long-Range Quantum Scars
authors: Hossein Hosseinabadi, Riccardo J. Valencia-Tortora, Aleksandr N. Mikheev, Darrick E. Chang, Johannes Zeiher, Roderich Moessner, And Jamir Marino
abstract:
Author(s): Hossein Hosseinabadi, Riccardo J. Valencia-Tortora, Aleksandr N. Mikheev, Darrick E. Chang, Johannes Zeiher, Roderich Moessner, and Jamir Marino

A minimal model for cavity-coupled Rydberg arrays reveals how kinetically constrained long-range interactions stabilize exotic phenomena ranging from blockaded superradiance to long-range quantum scars.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020357] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: A minimal cavity QED model with Rydberg arrays reveals kinetically constrained long-range interactions stabilizing blockaded superradiance and long-range quantum scars.
motivation: Understanding exotic non-equilibrium phases in cavity-coupled Rydberg arrays, which are a hybrid quantum system combining atomic ensembles with cavity QED.
method: Theoretical analysis of a minimal model for cavity-coupled Rydberg arrays, incorporating kinetic constraints and long-range interactions.
result: Discovery of blockaded ferromagnetism and long-range quantum scars as emergent phenomena from the interplay of cavity-mediated interactions and kinetic constraints.
conclusion: Cavity QED with Rydberg arrays provides a platform for realizing novel quantum many-body phenomena, relevant to quantum simulation and information processing.

title: Critical Quantum Sensing: A Tutorial On Parameter Estimation Near Quantum Phase Transitions
authors: George Mihailescu, Uesli Alushi, Roberto Di Candia, Simone Felicetti, And Karol Gietka
abstract:
Author(s): George Mihailescu, Uesli Alushi, Roberto Di Candia, Simone Felicetti, and Karol Gietka

Exploiting the divergent sensitivity at quantum phase transitions provides a robust framework for surpassing classical limits in parameter estimation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020201] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: A tutorial on using quantum phase transitions for enhanced parameter estimation, bridging quantum sensing and critical phenomena.
motivation: Quantum phase transitions exhibit divergent susceptibility, offering a resource for surpassing classical limits in parameter estimation.
method: The tutorial reviews theoretical frameworks for critical quantum sensing, including scaling analysis, Fisher information, and protocols near critical points.
result: It demonstrates how criticality can enhance sensitivity in parameter estimation, providing practical guidelines for experimental implementations.
conclusion: Critical quantum sensing is a promising approach for achieving high-precision measurements, with potential applications in quantum metrology.

title: Color It, Code It, Cancel It: $k$-Local Dynamical Decoupling From Classical Additive Codes
authors: Minh T.P. Nguyen, Maximilian Rimbach-Russ, And Stefano Bosco
abstract:
Author(s): Minh T.P. Nguyen, Maximilian Rimbach-Russ, and Stefano Bosco

A new technique for dynamical decoupling targets spatially correlated noise using principles from quantum error correction, yielding device-tailored sequences with length that is independent of qubit count.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020338] Published Wed May 27, 2026.
tldr: A new dynamical decoupling technique using classical additive codes to suppress spatially correlated noise, with sequence length independent of qubit count.
motivation: Dynamical decoupling sequences for multi-qubit systems often scale poorly with qubit number when targeting correlated noise; a more efficient method is needed.
method: The authors map the problem of designing decoupling sequences to constructing classical additive codes, enabling systematic generation of device-tailored sequences.
result: The resulting sequences have length independent of the number of qubits, effectively canceling k-local correlated noise.
conclusion: This work bridges quantum error correction and dynamical decoupling, offering practical noise mitigation for quantum devices.

title: Continuous-variable Quantum Communication
authors: Vladyslav C. Usenko, Antonio Acín, Romain Alléaume, Ulrik L. Andersen, Eleni Diamanti, Tobias Gehring, Adnan A. E. Hajomer, Florian Kanitschar, Christoph Pacher, Stefano Pirandola, And Valerio Pruneri
abstract:
Author(s): Vladyslav C. Usenko, Antonio Acín, Romain Alléaume, Ulrik L. Andersen, Eleni Diamanti, Tobias Gehring, Adnan A. E. Hajomer, Florian Kanitschar, Christoph Pacher, Stefano Pirandola, and Valerio Pruneri

The quantum nature of radiation is not solely corpuscular. In the “continuous-variable” setting, the wavelike quantum properties can be observed. Quantum technologies put this continuous-variable nature of light to use, with applications in various forms of quantum information processing. This review concentrates on the developments of these wave-based techniques in quantum communication. Compared with photon-based (corpuscular) variants, the continuous-variable approach is equally well developed and has certain conceptual and practical advantages.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 015003] Published Mon Mar 23, 2026.
tldr: A comprehensive review of continuous-variable quantum communication, covering protocols, security, and experimental progress.
motivation: Continuous-variable (CV) approaches offer practical advantages over discrete-variable methods, such as compatibility with standard telecom components and higher secret key rates in metropolitan networks.
method: The review surveys CV-QKD protocols (including Gaussian-modulated coherent states, discrete modulation, and measurement-device-independent variants), security proofs (asymptotic and finite-size), and experimental implementations.
result: CV quantum communication has reached maturity with field-tested systems achieving high key rates over tens of kilometers, and security proofs are now composable and tight.
conclusion: CV quantum communication is a viable and competitive technology for practical quantum networks, with ongoing work addressing long-distance and fully device-independent scenarios.

title: Quantum-information Methods For Quantum Gravity Laboratory-based Tests
authors: Chiara Marletto And Vlatko Vedral
abstract:
Author(s): Chiara Marletto and Vlatko Vedral

It is conceptually possible that gravity is a force of nature that is not describable with a classical theory, but is also not described by a conventional quantum theory. Information-theoretic approaches make it possible to address this general idea in a concrete way, with thought experiments that would constrain the scope of whatever new theory emerges. This review gives the status of these new theoretical approaches, with an emphasis on proposed experiments that look for gravitationally induced entanglement (GIE) between two probes for which quantum theory is known to be applicable.
