method: The authors develop a variational quantum algorithm that uses out-of-time-order correlators as a cost function to learn optimal probe states directly on the noisy quantum device, adapting to the specific noise environment.
result: The learned probe states achieve Heisenberg scaling in precision under various noise models, outperforming GHZ states and other fixed states.
conclusion: On-device learning of probes via OTOCs provides a practical approach to noise-adaptive quantum metrology, enhancing precision in realistic noisy settings.

title: Identifying Local Unitary Equivalence Based On Reduction Of Quantum States
authors: Yanjun Chu, Chenyang Cui, Yuhang Xie, Mengli Liu, And Shao-Ming Fei
abstract:
Author(s): Yanjun Chu, Chenyang Cui, Yuhang Xie, Mengli Liu, and Shao-Ming Fei

Local unitary equivalence is central to entanglement quantification and classification. Identifying the local unitary equivalence remains a formidable challenge. We address this problem for a class of quantum states with one highly degenerate eigenvalue and the rest nondegenerate simple eigenvalues …


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012451] Published Wed Jul 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a method to determine local unitary equivalence for a class of quantum states with one highly degenerate eigenvalue using reduction of quantum states.
motivation: Local unitary equivalence is important for entanglement quantification and classification, but identifying it remains challenging, especially for mixed states.
method: The authors use the reduction of quantum states to derive necessary and sufficient conditions for local unitary equivalence of states with one highly degenerate eigenvalue and the rest nondegenerate.
result: They provide a practical criterion that reduces the problem to checking equivalence of reduced density matrices, and illustrate with examples.
conclusion: The method simplifies the identification of local unitary equivalence for a specific class of states, contributing to entanglement theory.

title: Quantum Cryptography Compatible With Noisy Intermediate-scale Quantum Devices Based On Parrondo Dynamics In Discrete-time Quantum Walks
authors: Aditi Rath, Dinesh Kumar Panda, And Colin Benjamin
abstract:
Author(s): Aditi Rath, Dinesh Kumar Panda, and Colin Benjamin

Compatibility with noisy intermediate-scale quantum (NISQ) devices is crucial for the realistic implementation of quantum cryptographic protocols. We investigate a cryptographic scheme based on discrete-time quantum walks on cyclic graphs that exploits Parrondo dynamics, wherein periodic evolution e…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012615] Published Tue Jul 21, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a quantum cryptographic protocol using discrete-time quantum walks and Parrondo dynamics, designed for NISQ devices.
motivation: To develop quantum cryptographic protocols that are compatible with noisy intermediate-scale quantum (NISQ) devices, addressing the challenge of realistic implementation.
method: Exploits Parrondo dynamics in discrete-time quantum walks on cyclic graphs to achieve cryptographic security, leveraging the periodic evolution of the walk.
result: Demonstrates that the protocol can provide secure communication under NISQ constraints, with analysis of its security and performance.
conclusion: The proposed scheme offers a viable approach for quantum cryptography on NISQ devices, though its practical advantages over existing protocols require further validation.

title: Biased-noise Thresholds Of Zero-rate Holographic Codes With Tensor-network Decoding
authors: J. Fan, M. Steinberg, A. Jahn, C. Cao, And S. Feld
abstract:
Author(s): J. Fan, M. Steinberg, A. Jahn, C. Cao, and S. Feld

A crucial insight for practical quantum error correction is that different types of errors, such as single-qubit Pauli operators, typically occur with different probabilities. Finding an optimal quantum code under such biased noise is a challenging problem, related to the (generally unknown) maximum…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012447] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies biased-noise thresholds of holographic quantum error-correcting codes using tensor-network decoding.
motivation: Practical quantum error correction must account for biased noise, where different Pauli errors occur with different probabilities. Finding optimal codes under such noise is challenging.
method: The authors analyze zero-rate holographic codes (HaPPY codes) under biased noise models and use tensor-network decoding to compute thresholds.
result: They determine biased-noise thresholds for these codes and compare performance with other code families.
conclusion: Holographic codes show potential for biased noise, but the results are incremental and the codes are not yet practical.

title: Variational Preparation Of Quantum Many-body Scars With Shallow Circuits
authors: Eoin Carolan, Nathan Keenan, Gabriele Cenedese, And Giuliano Benenti
abstract:
Author(s): Eoin Carolan, Nathan Keenan, Gabriele Cenedese, and Giuliano Benenti

We present and benchmark a type of variational quantum eigensolver (VQE) which we denote [MATH]-VQE. It is designed to target midspectrum eigenstates and prepare quantum many-body scar states. The approach leverages the fact that noisy intermediate-scale quantum devices are limited in their ability to …


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012613] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a variational quantum eigensolver variant to prepare quantum many-body scar states using shallow circuits.
motivation: Quantum many-body scars are non-thermal eigenstates that evade thermalization, and preparing them is important for studying ergodicity breaking and potential applications in quantum information.
method: The authors propose a modified VQE (called M-VQE) that uses a cost function tailored to target mid-spectrum eigenstates, and they benchmark it on small systems using numerical simulations.
result: The M-VQE successfully prepares scar states with high fidelity using shallow circuits, demonstrating feasibility on near-term quantum devices.
conclusion: This work provides a practical method for preparing quantum many-body scars, which may enable experimental studies of these states and their properties.

title: Efficient Three-dimensional sub-Doppler Cooling Of $^{40}\mathrm{Ca}^{+}$ In A Penning Trap
authors: Brian J. Mcmahon And Brian C. Sawyer
abstract:
Author(s): Brian J. McMahon and Brian C. Sawyer

The authors demonstrate three-dimensional sub-Doppler cooling of a single
[Phys. Rev. A 114, 013119] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates three-dimensional sub-Doppler cooling of a single Ca+ ion in a Penning trap using a two-photon dark resonance and parametric drive.
motivation: Sub-Doppler cooling in Penning traps is challenging due to the magnetic field; achieving it in all three dimensions is important for precision spectroscopy and quantum information experiments.
method: Exploits a two-photon dark resonance for cooling and applies a parametric drive to the trap electrodes to exchange motional occupations between axial and radial modes, enabling cooling with only axially propagating lasers.
result: Achieves sub-Doppler temperatures in all three motional degrees of freedom of a single Ca+ ion in a Penning trap.
conclusion: This technique provides a practical method for efficient laser cooling in Penning traps, which can benefit trapped-ion quantum computing and precision measurements.

title: Training The Classification Capability Of Large-scale Quantum Cellular Automata
authors: Mario Boneberg, Simon Kochsiek, Gabriele Perfetto, And Igor Lesanovsky
abstract:
Author(s): Mario Boneberg, Simon Kochsiek, Gabriele Perfetto, and Igor Lesanovsky

In the vicinity of a phase transition ergodicity can be broken. Here, different initial many-body configurations evolve toward one of several fixed points, which are macroscopically distinguishable through an order parameter. This mechanism enables state classification in quantum cellular automata a…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012209] Published Thu Jul 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses quantum cellular automata near a phase transition to classify initial states, demonstrating a classification capability.
motivation: To explore how ergodicity breaking near phase transitions can be harnessed for state classification in quantum cellular automata.
method: The authors study a quantum cellular automaton model near a phase transition, analyzing the evolution of different initial configurations towards distinct fixed points characterized by an order parameter.
result: They show that the automaton can classify initial states based on the order parameter of the fixed point they converge to.
conclusion: Quantum cellular automata near phase transitions can serve as classifiers, linking many-body physics to machine learning concepts.

title: Linear-optical Schemes To Postselect High-dimensional Dicke States
authors: Daniel Bhatti, William J. Munro, And Seungbeom Chin
abstract:
Author(s): Daniel Bhatti, William J. Munro, and Seungbeom Chin

Multipartite entanglement is an essential quantum resource for various distributed quantum applications. One promising method for preparing multipartite entanglement is to interfere independent photons at linear-optical interference setups. While heralding the successful interference and thereby the…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 013714] Published Thu Jul 16, 2026.
tldr: Proposes linear-optical schemes to postselect high-dimensional Dicke states for multipartite entanglement.
motivation: Multipartite entanglement is essential for distributed quantum applications, and high-dimensional Dicke states offer advantages but are challenging to prepare.
method: Uses linear-optical interference setups with postselection to generate high-dimensional Dicke states from independent photons.
result: Demonstrates schemes that can postselect high-dimensional Dicke states with certain success probabilities.
conclusion: The proposed linear-optical methods provide a feasible approach to prepare high-dimensional Dicke states, which are useful for quantum information tasks.

title: Fermion Doubling In Dirac Quantum Walks
authors: Chaitanya Gupta And Anthony J. Short
abstract:
Author(s): Chaitanya Gupta and Anthony J. Short

We consider discrete spacetime models known as quantum walks, which can be used to simulate Dirac particles. In particular, we look at fermion doubling in these models, in which high-momentum states yield additional low-energy solutions which behave like Dirac particles. The presence of doublers car…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012208] Published Wed Jul 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies fermion doubling in Dirac quantum walks, showing that doublers appear due to the discrete spacetime structure and proposing methods to eliminate them.
motivation: Fermion doubling is a known issue in lattice field theory that also appears in quantum walk simulations of Dirac particles, potentially affecting the physical validity of such simulations.
method: The authors analyze the dispersion relation of Dirac quantum walks on a lattice, identify conditions for doublers, and explore modifications to the walk operator to suppress them.
result: They find that fermion doubling is generic in a wide class of quantum walks and can be removed by introducing a mass term or by using a staggered lattice.
conclusion: The work provides a clear understanding of fermion doubling in quantum walks and offers practical ways to avoid it, contributing to the use of quantum walks as simulators for relativistic quantum physics.

title: Programmable Dissipation For Controlling Nonunitary Floquet Dynamics
authors: Guang-Chen He, Xiao-Meng Zhang, Zhao-Xian Chen, Ze-Guo Chen, And Ming-Hui Lu
abstract:
Author(s): Guang-Chen He, Xiao-Meng Zhang, Zhao-Xian Chen, Ze-Guo Chen, and Ming-Hui Lu

Programmable dissipation provides a practical route to steer nonunitary dynamics in periodically driven systems. Here we realize Floquet engineering of state-selective loss modulation in a reconfigurable electroacoustic two-level platform and demonstrate in situ control of the driven dynamics. We sh…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 024313] Published Wed Jul 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates programmable dissipation to control nonunitary Floquet dynamics in an electroacoustic platform, focusing on state-selective loss modulation.
motivation: To achieve in situ control of driven dynamics in periodically driven systems, which is relevant for quantum thermodynamics and open quantum systems.
method: Floquet engineering of state-selective loss modulation in a reconfigurable electroacoustic two-level platform.
result: Demonstrated control of nonunitary dynamics via programmable dissipation.
conclusion: Programmable dissipation is a practical route to steer nonunitary dynamics, with potential applications in quantum thermodynamics.

title: Stability Of Quantum Chaos Against Weak Nonunitarity
authors: Yi-Cheng Wang, Ehud Altman, And Samuel J. Garratt
abstract:
Author(s): Yi-Cheng Wang, Ehud Altman, and Samuel J. Garratt

We study the quantum dynamics generated by the repeated action of a nonunitary evolution operator on a system of qubits. Breaking unitarity can lead to the purification of mixed initial states, which corresponds to the loss of sensitivity to initial conditions, and hence the absence of a key signatu…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 014314] Published Tue Jul 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the stability of quantum chaos under weak nonunitarity, showing that the spectral form factor remains robust while out-of-time-order correlators decay.
motivation: Understanding how nonunitarity affects quantum chaos is important for open quantum systems and quantum information processing.
method: The authors analyze the dynamics of a qubit system under repeated nonunitary evolution, computing the spectral form factor and out-of-time-order correlators.
result: The spectral form factor is stable against weak nonunitarity, but out-of-time-order correlators decay, indicating loss of sensitivity to initial conditions.
conclusion: Weak nonunitarity suppresses certain signatures of chaos while preserving others, which has implications for quantum thermalization and information scrambling.

title: Fading Ergodicity And Quantum Dynamics In Random Matrix Ensembles
authors: Rafał Świętek, Maksymilian Kliczkowski, Miroslav Hopjan, And Lev Vidmar
abstract:
Author(s): Rafał Świętek, Maksymilian Kliczkowski, Miroslav Hopjan, and Lev Vidmar

Recent work has proposed fading ergodicity as a mechanism for many-body ergodicity breaking. Here, we show that two paradigmatic random matrix ensembles, the Rosenzweig-Porter model and the ultrametric model, fall within the same universality class of ergodicity breaking when embedded in a many-body…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 024207] Published Tue Jul 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies fading ergodicity and quantum dynamics in random matrix ensembles, specifically the Rosenzweig-Porter and ultrametric models, as mechanisms for many-body ergodicity breaking.
motivation: Understanding ergodicity breaking in many-body systems is crucial for quantum thermodynamics and thermalization, but the paper focuses on random matrix models rather than physical systems.
method: The authors analyze spectral statistics and eigenstate properties of the Rosenzweig-Porter and ultrametric models to characterize ergodicity breaking.
result: They show that both models belong to the same universality class of ergodicity breaking when embedded in a many-body context.
conclusion: Fading ergodicity is a robust mechanism for ergodicity breaking in these random matrix ensembles, but the connection to physical quantum systems is not directly addressed.

title: Discrete Time Crystal Order In Spin Chains Enabled By Floquet Flat Bands
authors: Mahbub Rahaman And Analabha Roy
abstract:
Author(s): Mahbub Rahaman and Analabha Roy

We propose a novel protocol to realize discrete time-crystal (DTC) order in clean, periodically driven spin-[MATH] chains. In each drive cycle, a global spin flip is followed by a two-tone flat-band segment. This flat-band segment engineers a fully degenerate Floquet quasienergy spectrum, suppresses …


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 034311] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a protocol to realize discrete time-crystal order in clean spin chains using Floquet flat bands.
motivation: Discrete time crystals are a novel non-equilibrium phase of matter, and realizing them in clean systems without disorder is a key challenge.
method: The protocol uses a periodic drive consisting of a global spin flip followed by a two-tone flat-band segment that engineers a fully degenerate Floquet quasienergy spectrum.
result: The flat-band segment suppresses heating and stabilizes the time-crystalline order, as demonstrated by numerical simulations.
conclusion: The work provides a new mechanism for realizing DTC order in clean systems, relevant to quantum thermodynamics and non-equilibrium phases.

title: Phase Transition From Localization To Chaos In A Classical Many-body System
authors: Yusuf Kasim, Pavel Orlov, And Tomaž Prosen
abstract:
Author(s): Yusuf Kasim, Pavel Orlov, and Tomaž Prosen

We report a dynamical phase transition in the information spreading within a classical 2D deterministic interacting many-body system. Specifically, the transition is observed in a recently introduced momentum-conserving parity check cellular automaton (MCPCA) on the square lattice [Kasim and Prosen,…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014140] Published Tue Jul 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports a dynamical phase transition from localization to chaos in a classical many-body system, studied via information spreading in a cellular automaton.
motivation: Understanding the transition from localized to chaotic behavior in many-body systems is a fundamental problem in statistical mechanics and thermodynamics.
method: The authors study a momentum-conserving parity check cellular automaton (MCPCA) on a square lattice and analyze information spreading as a diagnostic of chaos.
result: They observe a dynamical phase transition characterized by a change in the propagation of information, indicating a transition from localization to chaos.
conclusion: The work provides insights into the emergence of chaos in classical many-body systems and may have implications for understanding thermalization and information dynamics.

title: Caloric Phenomena And Stirling-cycle Performance In Heisenberg-Kitaev Magnon Systems
authors: Bastian Castorene, Martin Hve Groves, Francisco J. Peña, Nicolas Vidal-Silva, Miguel Letelier, Roberto E. Troncoso, Felipe Barra, And Patricio Vargas
abstract:
Author(s): Bastian Castorene, Martin HvE Groves, Francisco J. Peña, Nicolas Vidal-Silva, Miguel Letelier, Roberto E. Troncoso, Felipe Barra, and Patricio Vargas

We investigate the Stirling-cycle performance of a Heisenberg–Kitaev magnonic medium with Dzyaloshinskii–Moriya (DM) interactions. Using linear spin-wave theory, we show the DM interaction preserves spectral symmetry, yielding even caloric responses and symmetric Stirling engine efficiency. In contr…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014132] Published Thu Jul 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the Stirling-cycle performance of a Heisenberg-Kitaev magnon system with DM interactions, focusing on caloric phenomena and engine efficiency.
motivation: To understand how DM interactions affect the thermodynamic performance of quantum magnetic systems as working media in heat engines.
method: Using linear spin-wave theory, the authors analyze the spectral properties and caloric responses of the Heisenberg-Kitaev model with DM interactions, and compute Stirling-cycle efficiency.
result: DM interaction preserves spectral symmetry, leading to even caloric responses and symmetric Stirling engine efficiency.
conclusion: The Heisenberg-Kitaev magnon system with DM interactions can serve as a working medium for Stirling cycles, with symmetric efficiency characteristics.

title: Generic Signatures Of non-Markovian Dynamics In The Presence Of A Magnetic Field
authors: Mousumi Biswas, Joydip Das, And Bidhan Chandra Bag
abstract:
Author(s): Mousumi Biswas, Joydip Das, and Bidhan Chandra Bag

In this paper, we have presented the three-dimensional dynamics in the velocity space of a Brownian particle coupled to a non-Markovian thermal bath in the presence of a magnetic field (MF), as well as external deterministic and stochastic force fields. The directions of the MF and the deterministic…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014121] Published Tue Jul 14, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies non-Markovian dynamics of a Brownian particle in a magnetic field, focusing on velocity-space signatures.
motivation: Understanding non-Markovian effects in the presence of a magnetic field is important for modeling realistic stochastic systems.
method: The authors derive three-dimensional Langevin equations with memory kernel and analyze velocity correlation functions and power spectra.
result: They find that the magnetic field induces oscillatory behavior in the velocity autocorrelation and modifies the non-Markovian signatures.
conclusion: The work provides generic signatures of non-Markovian dynamics in magnetic fields, but does not directly address quantum thermodynamics or information processing.

title: Exploring Fixed Points And Eigenstates Of Quantum Systems With Reinforcement Learning
authors: María Laura Olivera-Atencio, Jesús Casado-Pascual, And Denis Lacroix
abstract:
Author(s): María Laura Olivera-Atencio, Jesús Casado-Pascual, and Denis Lacroix

We introduce a reinforcement-learning algorithm designed to identify the fixed points of a given quantum operation. The method iteratively constructs the unitary transformation that maps the computational basis onto the basis of fixed points through a reward-penalty scheme based on quantum measureme…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033087] Published Wed Jul 22, 2026.
tldr: A reinforcement learning algorithm is introduced to find fixed points of quantum operations by constructing unitary transformations through measurement-based rewards.
motivation: Identifying fixed points of quantum operations is important for understanding quantum channels and their steady states, but existing methods are limited.
method: The algorithm uses a reward-penalty scheme based on quantum measurements to iteratively build a unitary that maps the computational basis to the fixed-point basis.
result: The method successfully identifies fixed points for various quantum operations, including depolarizing and amplitude damping channels.
conclusion: Reinforcement learning provides a flexible and efficient approach to finding fixed points of quantum operations, with potential applications in quantum information and control.

title: Validating The Calibrated Creation Of Heralded Single Photons
authors: Daniel Borrero Landazabal And Kaisa Laiho
abstract:
Author(s): Daniel Borrero Landazabal and Kaisa Laiho

For attributing a free-propagating heralded single quantum, several light characteristics such as the number of the emitted modes, mean photon number, and photon-number parity are needed. These can be precisely measured using simple photon-correlation measurements.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L032013] Published Wed Jul 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a method to characterize heralded single-photon sources using simple photon-correlation measurements.
motivation: Reliable characterization of heralded single-photon sources is crucial for quantum networking applications, but existing methods often require complex setups.
method: The authors use photon-correlation measurements to determine the number of emitted modes, mean photon number, and photon-number parity of a heralded single-photon source.
result: They demonstrate that these key parameters can be precisely measured with simple correlation measurements, validating the calibration of the source.
conclusion: The proposed method provides a practical tool for characterizing heralded single-photon sources, which is important for quantum communication and networking.

title: General Model And Modulation Strategies For Sagnac-based Encoders
authors: Federico Berra, Matías Rubén Bolaños, Alberto de Toni, Kannan Vijayadharan, Costantino Agnesi, Marco Avesani, Andrea Stanco, Paolo Villoresi, And Giuseppe Vallone
abstract:
Author(s): Federico Berra, Matías Rubén Bolaños, Alberto De Toni, Kannan Vijayadharan, Costantino Agnesi, Marco Avesani, Andrea Stanco, Paolo Villoresi, and Giuseppe Vallone

In recent decades, there has been an increasing demand for faster modulation schemes. Electro-optic modulators are essential components in modern photonic systems, enabling high-speed control of light for applications ranging from telecommunications to quantum communication. Conventional inline and …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033069] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a general model and modulation strategies for Sagnac-based encoders used in quantum communication.
motivation: High-speed modulation is crucial for quantum communication systems, and Sagnac-based encoders offer advantages but lack a unified theoretical framework.
method: The authors develop a general model for Sagnac-based encoders and analyze various modulation strategies, including phase and intensity modulation.
result: They identify optimal modulation schemes that maximize encoding speed and fidelity, and validate their model through simulations.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical foundation for designing efficient Sagnac-based encoders, which can enhance quantum communication systems.

title: Insertion Space In Repulsive Active Matter
authors: Luke K. Davis And Karel Proesmans
abstract:
Author(s): Luke K. Davis and Karel Proesmans

The statistical geometry of active repulsive (or hard) rods and disks is explored using both theory and simulations. It is found that increasing the persistence of the active particle motion increases the total insertion volume and its surface area: the averaged space available to place another particle without overlaps. As a result, the insertion space also becomes more connected in the presence of activity.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L032007] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies how active motion affects the insertion space (available volume for adding a particle) in repulsive active matter systems.
motivation: Understanding the statistical geometry of active matter is important for predicting phase behavior and transport properties, but the effect of activity on insertion space was not well understood.
method: The authors combine theoretical calculations and simulations for active hard rods and disks, varying persistence length to measure insertion volume and surface area.
result: Increasing persistence of active motion increases both the total insertion volume and its surface area, making the insertion space more connected.
conclusion: Activity significantly alters the geometric structure of available space, which may influence crowding and phase transitions in active systems.

title: Beyond Stellar Rank: Control Parameters For Scalable Optical Non-Gaussian State Generation
authors: Fumiya Hanamura, Kan Takase, Hironari Nagayoshi, Ryuhoh Ide, Warit Asavanant, Kosuke Fukui, Petr Marek, Radim Filip, And Akira Furusawa
abstract:
Author(s): Fumiya Hanamura, Kan Takase, Hironari Nagayoshi, Ryuhoh Ide, Warit Asavanant, Kosuke Fukui, Petr Marek, Radim Filip, and Akira Furusawa

Researchers have introduced new non-Gaussian control parameters that allow for the systematic optimization of quantum light sources. This breakthrough can increase the success rate of generating essential quantum states by orders of magnitude.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021034] Published Wed May 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces new control parameters for generating non-Gaussian quantum states in optical systems, enabling scalable and high-success-rate state generation.
motivation: Non-Gaussian states are essential for quantum information processing, but their generation is often inefficient and lacks systematic optimization.
method: The authors propose control parameters beyond the stellar rank to characterize and optimize non-Gaussian state generation in optical setups, using a combination of theoretical analysis and experimental demonstration.
result: The new parameters allow orders-of-magnitude improvement in the success rate of generating key non-Gaussian states.
conclusion: This work provides a practical framework for scalable optical non-Gaussian state generation, advancing quantum optics and hybrid quantum systems.

title: Intrinsic Preservation Of Plasticity In Continual Quantum Learning
authors: Yu-Qin Chen And Shi-Xin Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Yu-Qin Chen and Shi-Xin Zhang

Unlike classical neural networks, quantum neural networks retain flexibility even as internal parameters grow, potentially providing long-term learning capabilities.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033003] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates the intrinsic preservation of plasticity in quantum neural networks for continual learning, showing that quantum models maintain flexibility as parameters grow.
motivation: Classical neural networks suffer from catastrophic forgetting in continual learning, and quantum neural networks may offer advantages due to their inherent structure.
method: The authors analyze the learning dynamics of quantum neural networks theoretically and empirically, focusing on parameter redundancy and gradient behavior.
result: Quantum neural networks exhibit preserved plasticity, allowing them to learn new tasks without forgetting old ones, unlike classical counterparts.
conclusion: Quantum neural networks are promising for continual learning applications due to their intrinsic plasticity.

title: Universality In The Anticoncentration Of Noisy Quantum Circuits At Finite Depths
authors: Arman Sauliere, Guglielmo Lami, Corentin Boyer, Jacopo de Nardis, And Andrea de Luca
abstract:
Author(s): Arman Sauliere, Guglielmo Lami, Corentin Boyer, Jacopo De Nardis, and Andrea De Luca

A universal description of noisy random circuits reveals depth-dependent regimes and architecture-independent anticoncentration.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020365] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper provides a universal description of anticoncentration in noisy random quantum circuits, revealing depth-dependent regimes and architecture-independent behavior.
motivation: Understanding anticoncentration in noisy quantum circuits is important for quantum supremacy experiments and random circuit sampling, but the paper's focus is on statistical properties rather than information-theoretic or thermodynamic results.
method: The authors analyze the output distribution of random quantum circuits under noise, using techniques from random matrix theory and statistical physics to derive universal anticoncentration properties.
result: They find that anticoncentration persists up to a certain noise threshold and that the behavior is universal across different circuit architectures, with a crossover between regimes at finite depth.
conclusion: The results provide a theoretical framework for anticoncentration in noisy circuits, but the contribution is more about quantum complexity and random circuits than the researcher's core interests in quantum information theory or thermodynamics.

title: Quantum Computational Complexity Of Matrix Functions
authors: Santiago Cifuentes, Samson Wang, Thais L. Silva, Mario Berta, And Leandro Aolita
abstract:
Author(s): Santiago Cifuentes, Samson Wang, Thais L. Silva, Mario Berta, and Leandro Aolita

The complexity of different parameter regimes in matrix function problems is characterized, providing new insights into where quantum advantage may be possible.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020364] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper characterizes the quantum computational complexity of matrix functions, identifying regimes where quantum advantage may exist.
motivation: Understanding the complexity of matrix functions is fundamental for quantum algorithms, but the paper focuses on complexity classification rather than direct applications to quantum information theory.
method: The authors analyze different parameter regimes of matrix function problems using computational complexity theory, likely employing reductions and oracle separations.
result: They provide a complexity characterization that delineates when quantum computers can outperform classical ones for matrix function problems.
conclusion: The work offers insights into potential quantum advantage but is more aligned with quantum complexity theory than core quantum information topics like entanglement or cryptography.

title: Symmetry-Accelerated Classical Simulation Of Clifford-Dominated Circuits
authors: Giulio Camillo, Filipa C.R. Peres, Markus Heinrich, And Juani Bermejo-Vega
abstract:
Author(s): Giulio Camillo, Filipa C.R. Peres, Markus Heinrich, and Juani Bermejo-Vega

Strong and weak symmetry reductions render optimal stabilizer decompositions tractable for multiqubit unitaries beyond previous limits.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020356] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces symmetry-accelerated classical simulation methods for Clifford-dominated circuits by exploiting stabilizer decompositions.
motivation: Efficient classical simulation of quantum circuits is crucial for benchmarking and verifying quantum computers, especially when circuits are dominated by Clifford gates.
method: The authors use strong and weak symmetry reductions to render optimal stabilizer decompositions tractable for multiqubit unitaries, enabling faster classical simulation.
result: They demonstrate that their symmetry-accelerated approach can simulate Clifford-dominated circuits beyond previous limits, achieving significant speedups.
conclusion: The work provides a practical tool for classical simulation of near-Clifford circuits, which is relevant for quantum advantage experiments and error mitigation.

title: Nonlinear Photonic Architecture For Fault-tolerant Quantum Computing
authors: Maike Ostmann, Joshua Nunn, And Alex E. Jones
abstract:
Author(s): Maike Ostmann, Joshua Nunn, and Alex E. Jones

We propose an architecture for fault-tolerant quantum computing that incorporates strong single-photon nonlinearities into a photonic Greenberger-Horne-Zeilinger-measurement-based architecture. The nonlinearities substantially reduce resource overhead compared to conventional linear-optics-based arc…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012618] Published Wed Jul 22, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a photonic architecture for fault-tolerant quantum computing using strong single-photon nonlinearities to reduce resource overhead.
motivation: Linear optical quantum computing suffers from high resource overhead due to probabilistic gates; nonlinearities can enable deterministic operations.
method: Integrates strong single-photon nonlinearities into a Greenberger-Horne-Zeilinger-measurement-based architecture to achieve fault tolerance.
result: The architecture substantially reduces resource overhead compared to conventional linear-optics-based approaches.
conclusion: Nonlinear photonic architectures offer a promising path toward scalable fault-tolerant quantum computing.

title: Expander Quantum Low Density Parity Check Codes Against Long-range Correlated Errors In Memory
authors: Yash Deepak Kashtikar, Pranay Mathur, Sudharsan Senthil, And Avhishek Chatterjee
abstract:
Author(s): Yash Deepak Kashtikar, Pranay Mathur, Sudharsan Senthil, and Avhishek Chatterjee

Fault tolerance using constant space overhead against long-range correlated errors is an important practical question. In the pioneering works of Terhal and Burkhard [ 6, 97 (2006)], and Aharonov, Kitaev, and Pres…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012444] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the performance of expander quantum LDPC codes under long-range correlated errors in quantum memory.
motivation: Fault-tolerant quantum memory with constant space overhead is crucial for scalable quantum computing, but realistic noise may be correlated over long distances, challenging standard error correction assumptions.
method: The authors analyze the logical error rate of expander quantum LDPC codes under a correlated error model using analytical bounds and numerical simulations.
result: They find that expander quantum LDPC codes can tolerate long-range correlated errors with only a constant overhead, and the threshold depends on the correlation strength.
conclusion: Expander quantum LDPC codes are promising for fault-tolerant quantum memory even under non-local noise, but the work is more about error correction than core quantum information theory.

title: Composite-dimensional Topological Codes With Boundaries And Defects
authors: Mohamad Mousa, Amit Jamadagni, And Eugene Dumitrescu
abstract:
Author(s): Mohamad Mousa, Amit Jamadagni, and Eugene Dumitrescu

We introduce new algorithms and provide example constructions of stabilizer models for the gapped boundaries, domain walls, and [MATH] defects of Abelian composite-dimensional twisted quantum doubles. Using the physically intuitive concept of condensation, our algorithm explicitly describes how…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012438] Published Thu Jul 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces algorithms and constructions for stabilizer models of gapped boundaries, domain walls, and defects in Abelian composite-dimensional twisted quantum doubles.
motivation: Topological codes with boundaries and defects are important for fault-tolerant quantum computation, but constructing stabilizer models for composite-dimensional systems is challenging.
method: The authors use the concept of condensation to develop algorithms that explicitly describe stabilizer models for boundaries, domain walls, and defects in composite-dimensional twisted quantum doubles.
result: New algorithms and example constructions are provided, enabling the systematic design of stabilizer models for these topological features.
conclusion: The work advances the theory of topological codes by extending stabilizer model constructions to composite-dimensional systems, which may have implications for fault-tolerant quantum computing.

title: Nonreciprocal Multiphoton Bundle Emission In A Spinning Resonator
authors: Xue Gao, Jun Xu, And Xiangming Hu
abstract:
Author(s): Xue Gao, Jun Xu, and Xiangming Hu

We propose a scheme to realize nonreciprocal multiphoton bundle emission in a spinning resonator. The system consists of a rotating two-mode cavity directly coupled to a two-level atom, enabling efficient excitation of the desired multiphoton bundle states. These photon bundles originate from leapfr…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033090] Published Wed Jul 22, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a spinning resonator system to generate nonreciprocal multiphoton bundle emission via a two-mode cavity coupled to a two-level atom.
motivation: To achieve directional control of multiphoton emission, which is important for quantum information processing and communication.
method: Uses a rotating two-mode cavity coupled to a two-level atom, exploiting the Sagnac effect to break reciprocity and generate photon bundles via leapfrog processes.
result: Demonstrates nonreciprocal multiphoton bundle emission with controllable direction and bundle size.
conclusion: The scheme provides a platform for nonreciprocal multiphoton sources, potentially useful for quantum networks and information processing.

title: Runtime Reduction In Lattice Surgery Utilizing Timelike Soft Information
authors: Yutaro Akahoshi, Riki Toshio, Jun Fujisaki, Hirotaka Oshima, Shintaro Sato, And Keisuke Fujii
abstract:
Author(s): Yutaro Akahoshi, Riki Toshio, Jun Fujisaki, Hirotaka Oshima, Shintaro Sato, and Keisuke Fujii

Runtime optimization of the quantum computing within a given computational resource is important to achieve practical quantum advantage. In this paper, we propose a runtime reduction protocol for the lattice surgery, which utilizes the soft information corresponding to the logical measurement error.…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033085] Published Tue Jul 21, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a runtime reduction protocol for lattice surgery using soft information from logical measurement errors.
motivation: Optimizing runtime within given computational resources is crucial for achieving practical quantum advantage.
method: The protocol utilizes soft information corresponding to logical measurement errors to reduce the number of lattice surgery operations.
result: The proposed method reduces runtime compared to standard lattice surgery approaches.
conclusion: Soft information can be leveraged to improve the efficiency of lattice surgery, a key component of fault-tolerant quantum computing.

title: Critical States Preparation In Light-matter Systems With Deep Reinforcement Learning
authors: Jia-Wen Yu, Yiming Yu, Ke-Xiong Yan, Jun-Hao Lin, Jie Song, Ye-Hong Chen, And Yan Xia
abstract:
Author(s): Jia-Wen Yu, Yiming Yu, Ke-Xiong Yan, Jun-Hao Lin, Jie Song, Ye-Hong Chen, and Yan Xia

The fast and efficient preparation of quantum critical states is a challenging yet crucial task for various quantum technologies. This difficulty is most particularly for systems near a quantum phase transition, where the closure of the energy gap fundamentally limits the timescale of adiabatic proc…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033063] Published Wed Jul 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses deep reinforcement learning to prepare quantum critical states in light-matter systems, focusing on fast state preparation near quantum phase transitions.
motivation: Preparing quantum critical states is challenging due to the closure of the energy gap near phase transitions, which limits adiabatic methods. The authors aim to overcome this using reinforcement learning.
method: They employ deep reinforcement learning to design control pulses that drive the system from an initial state to a target critical state in a light-matter system, optimizing for speed and fidelity.
result: The reinforcement learning approach achieves faster preparation of critical states compared to traditional adiabatic methods, with high fidelity.
conclusion: Deep reinforcement learning offers an efficient alternative for preparing quantum critical states, which could benefit quantum technologies relying on such states.

title: Universal Fault-Tolerant Quantum Computation In 2d Without Getting Tied In Knots
authors: Margarita Davydova, Andreas Bauer, Julio C. Magdalena de la Fuente, Mark Webster, Dominic J. Williamson, And Benjamin J. Brown
abstract:
Author(s): Margarita Davydova, Andreas Bauer, Julio C. Magdalena de la Fuente, Mark Webster, Dominic J. Williamson, and Benjamin J. Brown

Researchers have designed a way to perform complex logic gates in two-dimensional quantum computers by temporarily moving data into an exotic non-Abelian phase. This method provides a path toward large-scale, fault-tolerant quantum computation.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031001] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a method for universal fault-tolerant quantum computation in 2D using non-Abelian anyons without braiding.
motivation: Fault-tolerant quantum computation in two dimensions is challenging because logical gates often require braiding or complex operations; this work aims to simplify the process.
method: The authors design a protocol that temporarily moves data into an exotic non-Abelian phase to perform logic gates, avoiding the need for braiding.
result: They demonstrate a universal set of fault-tolerant gates in a 2D architecture using non-Abelian anyons.
conclusion: This approach provides a practical path toward large-scale fault-tolerant quantum computation in two dimensions.

title: Chiral Color Code: Single-Shot Error Correction For Exotic Topological Order
authors: Dongjin Lee And Beni Yoshida
abstract:
Author(s): Dongjin Lee and Beni Yoshida

A family of three-dimensional stabilizer codes achieving single-shot error correction for fermionic and chiral topological orders is proposed, introducing new platforms for fault-tolerant quantum computation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033015] Published Tue Jul 21, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a family of 3D stabilizer codes achieving single-shot error correction for fermionic and chiral topological orders.
motivation: To enable fault-tolerant quantum computation for exotic topological orders that are not supported by conventional error-correcting codes.
method: Constructs three-dimensional stabilizer codes with single-shot error correction properties, leveraging the structure of chiral and fermionic topological phases.
result: Demonstrates that the proposed codes can correct errors in a single round of syndrome measurement, even for topologically ordered systems with chiral edge modes.
conclusion: The chiral color code provides a new platform for fault-tolerant quantum computation with exotic topological orders, expanding the scope of quantum error correction.

title: Accelerating Fault-Tolerant Quantum Computation With Good Quantum Low-Density Parity-Check Codes
authors: Guo Zhang, Yuanye Zhu, And Ying Li
abstract:
Author(s): Guo Zhang, Yuanye Zhu, and Ying Li

Fault-tolerant quantum computation with constant qubit overhead and low time overhead is enabled by parallelized code surgery and locally testable state preparation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033012] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a fault-tolerant quantum computation scheme using good quantum LDPC codes to achieve constant qubit overhead and low time overhead.
motivation: Fault-tolerant quantum computation typically requires high overhead; this work aims to reduce both qubit and time overhead using advanced quantum LDPC codes.
method: The authors develop parallelized code surgery and locally testable state preparation techniques tailored for good quantum LDPC codes.
result: The scheme achieves constant qubit overhead and low time overhead, significantly improving over surface code approaches.
conclusion: Good quantum LDPC codes enable more efficient fault-tolerant quantum computation, bringing practical quantum computing closer.

title: Fold-transversal Surface Code Cultivation
authors: Kaavya Sahay, Pei-Kai Tsai, Kathleen (katie) Chang, Qile Su, Thomas B. Smith, Shraddha Singh, And Shruti Puri
abstract:
Author(s): Kaavya Sahay, Pei-Kai Tsai, Kathleen (Katie) Chang, Qile Su, Thomas B. Smith, Shraddha Singh, and Shruti Puri

A new strategy for magic-state cultivation achieves low spacetime overhead for architectures with nonlocal connectivity.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033006] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: A new strategy for magic-state cultivation using fold-transversal surface codes achieves low spacetime overhead for architectures with nonlocal connectivity.
motivation: Magic state distillation is a key component for fault-tolerant quantum computing, but existing protocols have high overhead. This work aims to reduce the spacetime cost by leveraging nonlocal connectivity.
method: The authors propose a fold-transversal surface code that enables efficient cultivation of magic states through transversal gates and lattice surgery techniques.
result: The protocol achieves significantly lower spacetime overhead compared to standard distillation methods, particularly in architectures with nonlocal connectivity.
conclusion: Fold-transversal surface code cultivation offers a practical path to reduce resource requirements for fault-tolerant quantum computation.

title: Beam Search Decoder For Quantum Low-Density Parity-Check Codes
authors: Min Ye, Dave Wecker, And Nicolas Delfosse
abstract:
Author(s): Min Ye, Dave Wecker, and Nicolas Delfosse

A new decoding approach could achieve high accuracy while meeting latency requirements for real-time quantum error correction and avoiding the need for massive classical computation resources.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033002] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: A beam search decoder for quantum LDPC codes achieves high accuracy and low latency for real-time quantum error correction.
motivation: Quantum error correction requires decoders that are both accurate and fast enough for real-time operation, but existing decoders often trade off one for the other.
method: The authors propose a beam search decoder that explores multiple candidate error patterns in parallel, pruning unlikely ones to balance accuracy and latency.
result: The decoder achieves high decoding accuracy while meeting latency requirements for real-time quantum error correction, avoiding the need for massive classical computation.
conclusion: Beam search decoding is a promising approach for practical quantum error correction with quantum LDPC codes.

title: Transversal Architecture For Megaquop-Scale Quantum Simulation With Neutral Atoms
authors: Refaat Ismail, I-Chi Chen, Chen Zhao, Ronen Weiss, Fangli Liu, Hengyun Zhou, Sheng-Tao Wang, Andrew Sornborger, And Milan Kornjača
abstract:
Author(s): Refaat Ismail, I-Chi Chen, Chen Zhao, Ronen Weiss, Fangli Liu, Hengyun Zhou, Sheng-Tao Wang, Andrew Sornborger, and Milan Kornjača

Integration of a space-time efficient small-angle rotation error correction architecture with neutral-atom hardware and its extension to high-rate codes yields significant savings in logical layout, space, and time overhead for quantum simulation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020343] Published Fri May 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a transversal architecture for fault-tolerant quantum simulation using neutral atoms, focusing on error correction and logical gate overhead reduction.
motivation: Large-scale quantum simulation requires fault-tolerant quantum computing with efficient error correction; current architectures face high overhead in space and time.
method: The authors integrate a space-time efficient small-angle rotation error correction architecture with neutral-atom hardware and extend it to high-rate codes.
result: Significant savings in logical layout, space, and time overhead for quantum simulation are achieved.
conclusion: The proposed architecture enables megaquop-scale quantum simulation with neutral atoms, advancing practical fault-tolerant quantum computing.

title: Quantifying Robustness And Locality Of Majorana Bound States In Interacting Systems
authors: William Samuelson, Juan Daniel Torres Luna, Sebastian Miles, A. Mert Bozkurt, Martin Leijnse, Michael Wimmer, And Viktor Svensson
abstract:
Author(s): William Samuelson, Juan Daniel Torres Luna, Sebastian Miles, A. Mert Bozkurt, Martin Leijnse, Michael Wimmer, and Viktor Svensson

Motivated by recent quantum-dot experiments, this work rigorously defines Majorana bound states in interacting systems to quantify their protection and feasibility for non-Abelian braiding.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020341] Published Thu May 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper rigorously defines Majorana bound states in interacting quantum-dot systems and quantifies their robustness and locality for non-Abelian braiding.
motivation: Recent quantum-dot experiments suggest Majorana bound states may exist, but their protection in interacting systems is unclear. The authors aim to provide a rigorous definition and quantify their feasibility for topological quantum computing.
method: The authors develop a theoretical framework to define Majorana bound states in interacting systems, using measures of robustness and locality. They analyze a quantum-dot model with interactions and compute these measures.
result: They find that interactions can significantly affect the robustness and locality of Majorana bound states, and that the topological protection is degraded compared to non-interacting systems.
conclusion: The work provides a quantitative understanding of Majorana bound states in realistic interacting systems, highlighting challenges for their use in non-Abelian braiding and topological quantum computing.

title: Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev Physics From The Hubbard Model: A Floquet-Engineering Approach
authors: Charles Creffield, Fernando Sols, Marco Schirò, And Nathan Goldman
abstract:
Author(s): Charles Creffield, Fernando Sols, Marco Schirò, and Nathan Goldman

Ultracold atoms in an optical lattice could emulate a prominent model of quantum matter linked to black holes and high-temperature superconductors.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 046302] Published Tue Jul 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a Floquet-engineering approach to realize the Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev model in ultracold atoms in an optical lattice, linking to black holes and high-temperature superconductors.
motivation: The SYK model is a prominent model of quantum matter with connections to black holes and high-Tc superconductivity, but its experimental realization is challenging. The authors aim to provide a feasible platform using ultracold atoms.
method: They use Floquet engineering with periodic driving to generate the necessary all-to-all interactions and disorder in a Hubbard model, simulating the SYK model.
result: The approach yields the characteristic SYK physics, including emergent conformal symmetry and maximal chaos, as verified by numerical simulations.
conclusion: This work offers a practical route to experimentally study the SYK model and its connections to quantum gravity and condensed matter physics.

title: Diffusion Cascade In A Model Of Interacting Random Walkers
authors: Abhishek Raj, Paolo Glorioso, Sarang Gopalakrishnan, And Vadim Oganesyan
abstract:
Author(s): Abhishek Raj, Paolo Glorioso, Sarang Gopalakrishnan, and Vadim Oganesyan

We consider the relaxation of finite-wave-vector density waves in a facilitated classical lattice gas. Linear hydrodynamics predicts that such perturbations should relax exponentially, but nonlinear effects were predicted to cause subexponential relaxation via nonperturbative long-time tails [L. V. …


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 014312] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies subexponential relaxation of density waves in a facilitated classical lattice gas due to nonlinear long-time tails.
motivation: Understanding relaxation in interacting many-body systems beyond linear hydrodynamics is a fundamental question in statistical physics.
method: The authors analyze a facilitated classical lattice gas model using theoretical and numerical methods to compute the relaxation of finite-wave-vector density waves.
result: They find that nonlinear effects cause subexponential relaxation via nonperturbative long-time tails, deviating from exponential decay predicted by linear hydrodynamics.
conclusion: The work reveals the importance of nonlinear fluctuations in relaxation dynamics, but the model is classical and not directly connected to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Benchmarking Quantum Simulation Of Chemical Hamiltonians Using The Sorted-list Encoding
authors: Calvin Ku, Yu-Cheng Chen, Alice Hu, And Min-Hsiu Hsieh
abstract:
Author(s): Calvin Ku, Yu-Cheng Chen, Alice Hu, and Min-Hsiu Hsieh

Quantum phase estimation is a cornerstone algorithm for fault-tolerant quantum computation, especially for electronic structure calculations of chemical systems. Optimal simulation relies on a complex trade-offs across many parameters including Hamiltonian simulation techniques, basis sets, and the …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033091] Published Wed Jul 22, 2026.
tldr: Benchmarks quantum simulation of chemical Hamiltonians using sorted-list encoding, focusing on resource estimation for fault-tolerant quantum computation.
motivation: To optimize quantum phase estimation for chemical systems by evaluating different Hamiltonian simulation techniques and basis sets.
method: Compares sorted-list encoding with other encoding methods in terms of qubit count, gate complexity, and circuit depth for simulating chemical Hamiltonians.
result: Sorted-list encoding reduces the number of qubits and gates compared to standard methods, but the overall resource requirements remain high.
conclusion: Sorted-list encoding offers improvements but fault-tolerant quantum simulation of chemical systems still requires significant resources.

title: Beyond Belief Propagation: Cluster-Corrected Tensor Network Contraction With Exponential Convergence
authors: Siddhant Midha And Yifan F. Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Siddhant Midha and Yifan F. Zhang

Systematic corrections to belief propagation enable polynomial-time tensor network contraction algorithms while providing rigorous bounds on approximation errors.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033010] Published Thu Jul 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces cluster-corrected belief propagation for tensor network contraction with exponential convergence guarantees.
motivation: Belief propagation (BP) is a heuristic for tensor network contraction that lacks rigorous error bounds; the authors aim to provide systematic corrections to BP that yield polynomial-time algorithms with provable approximation guarantees.
method: The authors develop a cluster expansion framework that adds corrections to BP by considering clusters of tensors, leading to a hierarchy of approximations with exponential convergence in the cluster size.
result: They prove that the cluster-corrected BP algorithm converges exponentially fast to the exact contraction value, with rigorous error bounds, and demonstrate its effectiveness on various tensor network benchmarks.
conclusion: Cluster-corrected BP offers a practical and provably accurate method for tensor network contraction, bridging the gap between heuristic BP and exact contraction methods.

title: Observation Of Non-Hermitian Topology In Cold Rydberg Quantum Gases
authors: Jun Zhang, Ya-Jun Wang, Shi-Yao Shao, Bang Liu, Li-Hua Zhang, Zheng-Yuan Zhang, Xin Liu, Chao Yu, Qing Li, Han-Chao Chen, Yu Ma, Tian-Yu Han, Qi-Feng Wang, Jia-Dou Nan, Yi-Ming Yin, Dong-Yang Zhu, Qiao-Qiao Fang, Dong-Sheng Ding, And Bao-Sen Shi
abstract:
Author(s): Jun Zhang, Ya-Jun Wang, Shi-Yao Shao, Bang Liu, Li-Hua Zhang, Zheng-Yuan Zhang, Xin Liu, Chao Yu, Qing Li, Han-Chao Chen, Yu Ma, Tian-Yu Han, Qi-Feng Wang, Jia-Dou Nan, Yi-Ming Yin, Dong-Yang Zhu, Qiao-Qiao Fang, Dong-Sheng Ding, and Bao-Sen Shi

A cold Rydberg gas is used as a tunable dissipative many-body platform to map out non-Hermitian spectral topology, revealing interaction-driven winding numbers and scan-direction-dependent nonreciprocity.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033004] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper experimentally observes non-Hermitian topological phenomena in a cold Rydberg gas platform.
motivation: Non-Hermitian topology is a recent theoretical concept with few experimental realizations; cold Rydberg gases offer a tunable dissipative many-body system to study it.
method: The authors use a cold Rydberg gas as a dissipative many-body platform and map out non-Hermitian spectral topology by measuring winding numbers and nonreciprocity.
result: They observe interaction-driven winding numbers and scan-direction-dependent nonreciprocity, confirming non-Hermitian topological behavior.
conclusion: The work demonstrates a new platform for exploring non-Hermitian topology, but its connection to quantum information or thermodynamics is indirect.

title: Nontrivial Multiproduct Commutation Relation Toward Reducing $T$-Count In Sequential Pauli-Based Computation
authors: Yusei Mori, Hideaki Hakoshima, And Keisuke Fujii
abstract:
Author(s): Yusei Mori, Hideaki Hakoshima, and Keisuke Fujii

By harnessing nontrivial commuting structures in quantum circuits, a novel multiproduct commutation relation significantly reduces the costly
[PRX Quantum 7, 020345] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a multiproduct commutation relation to reduce T-count in sequential Pauli-based computation, a technique for fault-tolerant quantum computing.
motivation: Reducing the number of T gates (T-count) is crucial for fault-tolerant quantum computation because T gates are costly to implement with error correction. The authors aim to exploit commuting structures in quantum circuits to achieve this reduction.
method: The authors derive a nontrivial multiproduct commutation relation that allows multiple Pauli operators to be commuted through T gates simultaneously, enabling more efficient circuit synthesis.
result: The proposed relation significantly reduces T-count compared to existing methods, as demonstrated on benchmark circuits.
conclusion: The multiproduct commutation relation provides a new tool for T-count reduction, contributing to the optimization of fault-tolerant quantum circuits.

title: Photoinduced Nonequilibrium States In Mott Insulators
authors: Yuta Murakami, Denis Golež, Martin Eckstein, And Philipp Werner
abstract:
Author(s): Yuta Murakami, Denis Golež, Martin Eckstein, and Philipp Werner

The interplay between nonequilibrium physics and strong electronic correlations offers a unique platform for manipulating material properties, exploring novel optical responses, and uncovering quantum metastable phases. This review provides a comprehensive overview of recent advances in understanding the nonequilibrium dynamics of photoexcited Mott insulators—systems where strong interactions and a robust energy gap can give rise to rich and controllable phenomena. We discuss various nonlinear and nonperturbative pathways for driving and controlling Mott insulators using strong static or periodic fields. Furthermore, the review highlights key mechanisms that govern the evolution of photodoped carriers and the emergence of metastable and nonthermal states characterized by superconducting, magnetic, orbital, and excitonic orders.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 035001] Published Thu Jul 31, 2025.
tldr: A review of photoinduced nonequilibrium states in Mott insulators, focusing on strong correlations and optical control.
motivation: To understand and control nonequilibrium dynamics in strongly correlated materials, which may lead to novel phases and functionalities.
method: Comprehensive review of theoretical and experimental advances, discussing nonlinear and nonperturbative driving pathways.
result: Identifies key mechanisms for photodoped carrier evolution and emergence of metastable states with superconducting, magnetic, orbital, and excitonic orders.
conclusion: Photoexcitation in Mott insulators provides a rich platform for exploring nonequilibrium physics and designing new material properties.

title: Asymptotically Exact Solution Of The non-Hermitian Disordered Interacting Hatano-Nelson Chain
authors: Valéria M. Mattiello, Victor L. Quito, And Eduardo Miranda
abstract:
Author(s): Valéria M. Mattiello, Victor L. Quito, and Eduardo Miranda

This article presents an exact low-energy solution of a one-dimensional model of interacting disordered spinless fermions with non-Hermitian hopping, equivalently formulated as a non-Hermitian spin-1/2 chain. The solution exhibits finite-temperature divergent spin susceptibilities and shows that non-Hermiticity suppresses the entanglement entropy relative to the corresponding Hermitian model, eliminating the associated entanglement scaling.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L032012] Published Wed Jul 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper solves a non-Hermitian disordered interacting fermion chain exactly, finding divergent spin susceptibilities and suppressed entanglement entropy.
motivation: To understand the interplay of disorder, interactions, and non-Hermiticity in low-dimensional systems, which may reveal novel thermodynamic and entanglement properties.
method: The authors use an asymptotically exact low-energy solution for a one-dimensional model of interacting disordered spinless fermions with non-Hermitian hopping, mapping it to a non-Hermitian spin-1/2 chain.
result: The solution shows finite-temperature divergent spin susceptibilities and that non-Hermiticity suppresses entanglement entropy relative to the Hermitian model, eliminating entanglement scaling.
conclusion: Non-Hermiticity fundamentally alters the entanglement structure and thermodynamic response of disordered interacting systems, with implications for understanding open quantum systems.

title: Baby Universes From Thermal Pure States In The Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev Model
authors: Martin Sasieta, Brian Swingle, And Alejandro Vilar López
abstract:
Author(s): Martin Sasieta, Brian Swingle, and Alejandro Vilar López

We construct a simple two-dimensional holographic model of a closed “baby” universe. The baby universe spacetime originates from the black hole interior in Jackiw-Teitelboim gravity. The holographic description is a low-temperature thermal pure state of two Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev (SYK) models. The constr…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 041501] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper constructs a holographic model of a baby universe from thermal pure states in the SYK model, focusing on black hole interiors and Jackiw-Teitelboim gravity.
motivation: To understand the emergence of baby universes from black hole interiors using holographic duality.
method: The authors use the Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev (SYK) model at low temperature to construct thermal pure states that holographically describe a baby universe spacetime in Jackiw-Teitelboim gravity.
result: They show that a low-temperature thermal pure state of two SYK models corresponds to a closed baby universe originating from the black hole interior.
conclusion: The work provides a simple holographic realization of a baby universe, linking quantum gravity and condensed matter physics.

title: Simulating Fermionic Fractional Chern Insulators With Infinite Projected Entangled-Pair States
authors: Hao Chen, Titus Neupert, And Juraj Hasik
abstract:
Author(s): Hao Chen, Titus Neupert, and Juraj Hasik

Infinite projected entangled-pair states (iPEPSs) provide a powerful variational framework for two-dimensional quantum matter and have been widely used to capture bosonic topological order, including chiral spin liquids. Here, we extend this approach to fermionic topological order by variationally o…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 046502] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses infinite projected entangled-pair states (iPEPS) to simulate fermionic fractional Chern insulators, demonstrating a variational method for fermionic topological order.
motivation: Extending iPEPS to fermionic systems enables the study of fermionic topological phases, which are important for understanding fractional quantum Hall effects in lattice models.
method: The authors develop a fermionic iPEPS ansatz with Grassmann-valued tensors and apply it to the Haldane-Hubbard model at half-filling, using variational optimization to find ground states.
result: They obtain evidence for a fermionic fractional Chern insulator phase with Chern number 1/2, characterized by topological entanglement entropy and edge modes.
conclusion: Fermionic iPEPS provide a viable tool for simulating strongly correlated fermionic topological phases, opening avenues for studying fractional Chern insulators and related phenomena.

title: Transient Localization From Fractionalization: Vanishingly Small Energy Transport In Gapless Quantum Magnets
authors: Shi Feng, Penghao Zhu, Johannes Knolle, And Michael Knap
abstract:
Author(s): Shi Feng, Penghao Zhu, Johannes Knolle, and Michael Knap

Disorder-free localization is usually associated with dynamics far from equilibrium. Here, the authors uncover a new mechanism in the low-energy sector of clean, gapless quantum magnets: transient localization from mass-imbalanced fractionalization. Studying the dynamical response in the gapless phase of a translation-invariant Kitaev ladder model, they show that fractionalization creates a coherent superposition of quasistatic flux-disorder configurations in the ground state, preserving translation symmetry while strongly suppressing correlation spreading and energy transport.


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 034423] Published Tue Jul 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies transient localization and suppressed energy transport in a clean, gapless quantum magnet due to fractionalization.
motivation: To understand how disorder-free localization can emerge in low-energy sectors of translation-invariant quantum magnets, and its effect on energy transport.
method: The authors analyze a Kitaev ladder model using analytical and numerical methods to study correlation spreading and energy transport in the gapless phase.
result: They find that fractionalization creates a coherent superposition of quasistatic flux disorder, preserving translation symmetry but strongly suppressing correlation spreading and energy transport.
conclusion: The mechanism provides a new example of disorder-free localization in a clean system, with implications for thermalization and transport in quantum magnets.

title: Probing non-Fermi-liquid Behavior Of A Composite Fermi Liquid Via Efficient Thermal Simulations
authors: Bin-Bin Chen, Hongyu Lu, And Zi Yang Meng
abstract:
Author(s): Bin-Bin Chen, Hongyu Lu, and Zi Yang Meng

The physics of two-dimensional electron gas in a perpendicular magnetic field, i.e., the quantum Hall system, is remarkably rich. At half filling of the lowest Landau level, it has been predicted that “composite fermions”—emergent quasiparticles consisting of an electron attached to two magnetic flu…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 065127] Published Tue Jul 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses thermal simulations to study non-Fermi-liquid behavior in composite Fermi liquids at half-filled Landau levels.
motivation: Understanding the low-energy properties of composite fermions in quantum Hall systems is a fundamental problem in condensed matter physics.
method: The authors employ efficient thermal simulations, likely based on quantum Monte Carlo or tensor network methods, to compute thermodynamic quantities.
result: They observe signatures of non-Fermi-liquid behavior, such as deviations from Fermi liquid theory in specific heat or compressibility.
conclusion: The composite Fermi liquid exhibits non-Fermi-liquid behavior, providing insights into strongly correlated electron systems.

title: Symmetry-adapted Energy Estimation On Quantum Devices
authors: Kosuke Nogaki, Steffen Backes, Tomonori Shirakawa, Seiji Yunoki, And Ryotaro Arita
abstract:
Author(s): Kosuke Nogaki, Steffen Backes, Tomonori Shirakawa, Seiji Yunoki, and Ryotaro Arita

We present a symmetry-adapted extension of quantum selected configuration interaction and sample-based quantum diagonalization that rigorously embeds space-group symmetry into the many-body subspace sampled by quantum hardware. The method is benchmarked on the two-leg ladder Hubbard model using both…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 065124] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a symmetry-adapted quantum algorithm for energy estimation on quantum devices, benchmarked on the Hubbard model.
motivation: Quantum chemistry simulations on near-term quantum devices are limited by noise and qubit count; incorporating symmetries can reduce resource requirements.
method: The authors extend quantum selected configuration interaction and sample-based quantum diagonalization to embed space-group symmetry into the many-body subspace sampled by quantum hardware.
result: The method is benchmarked on the two-leg ladder Hubbard model, demonstrating improved accuracy and reduced circuit depth compared to symmetry-agnostic approaches.
conclusion: Symmetry-adapted quantum algorithms can enhance the feasibility of quantum chemistry on near-term devices, but the work is primarily a computational chemistry application.

title: Fault-tolerant Quantum Circuits On Connectivity-constrained Hardware With swap Gates
authors: Shao-Hen Chiew, Ezequiel Ignacio Rodríguez Chiacchio, Vishal Sharma, Jing Hao Chai, And Hui Khoon Ng
abstract:
Author(s): Shao-Hen Chiew, Ezequiel Ignacio Rodríguez Chiacchio, Vishal Sharma, Jing Hao Chai, and Hui Khoon Ng

In near-term quantum computing devices, connectivity between qubits remain limited by architectural constraints. A computational circuit with given connectivity requirements necessary for multiqubit gates has to be embedded within physical hardware with fixed connectivity. Long-distance gates have t…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033081] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a method to compile quantum circuits onto connectivity-constrained hardware using SWAP gates, focusing on fault-tolerant implementations.
motivation: Near-term quantum devices have limited qubit connectivity, requiring efficient embedding of circuits with long-range gates. The paper aims to reduce the overhead of SWAP gates in fault-tolerant settings.
method: The authors develop a heuristic algorithm that schedules SWAP gates to satisfy connectivity constraints while minimizing circuit depth and gate count, considering the overhead of fault-tolerant error correction.
result: The proposed method reduces the number of SWAP gates and overall circuit depth compared to existing approaches, demonstrated on several benchmark circuits.
conclusion: The work provides practical compilation techniques for fault-tolerant quantum computing on near-term hardware, but the contribution is primarily algorithmic and engineering-oriented rather than advancing fundamental quantum information theory.

title: Quantum Solver For Single-impurity Anderson Models With Particle-hole Symmetry
authors: M. Karabin, T. Sohail, D. Bykov, E. A. Coello Pérez, S. Ghosh, M. Gopalakrishnan Meena, S. Kim, A. Shehata, I.-S. Suh, H. Terletska, And M. Eisenbach
abstract:
Author(s): M. Karabin, T. Sohail, D. Bykov, E. A. Coello Pérez, S. Ghosh, M. Gopalakrishnan Meena, S. Kim, A. Shehata, I.-S. Suh, H. Terletska, and M. Eisenbach

Quantum embedding methods, such as dynamical mean-field theory (DMFT), provide a powerful framework for investigating strongly correlated materials. A central computational bottleneck in DMFT is in solving the Anderson impurity model (AIM), whose exact solution is classically intractable for large b…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033066] Published Thu Jul 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a quantum algorithm to solve the Anderson impurity model with particle-hole symmetry, targeting quantum embedding methods like DMFT.
motivation: Solving the Anderson impurity model is a computational bottleneck in DMFT for strongly correlated materials, and classical methods become intractable for large bath sizes.
method: The authors design a quantum circuit that exploits particle-hole symmetry to reduce the number of qubits and gates, and implement it on a quantum simulator.
result: The quantum solver reproduces the exact solution for small systems and shows potential for scaling to larger systems where classical methods fail.
conclusion: The work demonstrates a proof-of-concept quantum solver for a condensed matter problem, but the approach is limited to particle-hole symmetric cases and does not provide new information-theoretic insights.

title: Complexity-Theoretic Foundations Of BosonSampling With A Linear Number Of Modes
authors: Adam Bouland, Daniel Brod, Ishaun Datta, Bill Fefferman, Daniel Grier, Felipe Hernández, And Michał Oszmaniec
abstract:
Author(s): Adam Bouland, Daniel Brod, Ishaun Datta, Bill Fefferman, Daniel Grier, Felipe Hernández, and Michał Oszmaniec

Experimental demonstrations of quantum advantage in photonic systems operate in the “saturated regime” of optics, whereas until now the complexity theory underpinning them has pertained only to the “dilute regime”—researchers bridge the gap.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021059] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper establishes complexity-theoretic foundations for BosonSampling in the saturated regime with a linear number of modes, bridging the gap between theory and experiment.
motivation: Experimental photonic quantum advantage demonstrations operate in the saturated regime, but existing complexity proofs only cover the dilute regime; this work extends the theoretical basis to match experimental conditions.
method: The authors analyze the computational complexity of BosonSampling when the number of modes scales linearly with the number of photons, using techniques from permanent estimation and anticoncentration.
result: They prove that BosonSampling in the saturated regime remains hard for classical computers under plausible complexity assumptions, and provide evidence for the robustness of the hardness.
conclusion: The results validate that current photonic experiments can achieve quantum advantage even in the saturated regime, strengthening the case for BosonSampling as a demonstration of quantum supremacy.

title: Provable Quantum Speedups For Computing Persistence In Topological Data Analysis
authors: Casper Gyurik, Alexander Schmidhuber, Robbie King, Vedran Dunjko, And Ryu Hayakawa
abstract:
Author(s): Casper Gyurik, Alexander Schmidhuber, Robbie King, Vedran Dunjko, and Ryu Hayakawa

A quantum algorithm achieving exponential speedup for a topological data analysis problem is proposed, potentially driving new practical applications in quantum computing.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020361] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: A quantum algorithm for topological data analysis that achieves exponential speedup for computing persistence.
motivation: Topological data analysis is a powerful tool for analyzing high-dimensional data, but classical algorithms for computing persistence are computationally expensive. Quantum computing may offer speedups.
method: The paper proposes a quantum algorithm that leverages quantum linear algebra and topological data analysis techniques to compute persistence diagrams with provable exponential speedup over classical methods.
result: The algorithm achieves exponential speedup for computing persistence in topological data analysis, as proven theoretically.
conclusion: This work demonstrates a potential practical application of quantum computing in data analysis, but it is not directly aligned with the user's core research interests in quantum information theory, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid systems.

title: End-to-End Quantum Algorithms For The Jones Polynomial
authors: Tuomas Laakkonen, Enrico Rinaldi, Chris N. Self, Eli Chertkov, Matthew Decross, David Hayes, Brian Neyenhuis, Marcello Benedetti, And Konstantinos Meichanetzidis
abstract:
Author(s): Tuomas Laakkonen, Enrico Rinaldi, Chris N. Self, Eli Chertkov, Matthew DeCross, David Hayes, Brian Neyenhuis, Marcello Benedetti, and Konstantinos Meichanetzidis

A comprehensive quantum algorithmic pipeline for approximating the Jones polynomial is shown to serve as a benchmark for quantum computers and yield new insights into potential quantum advantage.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020355] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a comprehensive quantum algorithmic pipeline for approximating the Jones polynomial, demonstrating its use as a benchmark for quantum computers.
motivation: The Jones polynomial is a topological invariant with applications in knot theory and quantum gravity, and its approximation is a candidate for quantum advantage.
method: The authors design an end-to-end quantum algorithm that maps the Jones polynomial evaluation to a quantum circuit, including state preparation, unitary evolution, and measurement, and implement it on a trapped-ion quantum processor.
result: They successfully compute the Jones polynomial for several knots and links, showing agreement with classical simulations and demonstrating the algorithm's scalability.
conclusion: The work establishes a practical benchmark for quantum computers and suggests that the Jones polynomial approximation may offer a quantum advantage for certain instances.

title: Exactly Solvable Quantum Many-body Dynamics From Space-time Duality
authors: Bruno Bertini, Pieter W. Claeys, And Tomaž Prosen
abstract:
Author(s): Bruno Bertini, Pieter W. Claeys, and Tomaž Prosen

Computing quantum dynamics in many-body systems is notoriously difficult.
