In the past decade, there has been a fundamental advance based on discretizing the time evolution of lattice systems, by analogy with digital computation. Since space is already discrete on a lattice, treating space and time on the same footing avoids the mathematical complications of continuous space-time quantum field theories. This review focuses on how this space-time duality plays out in the dynamics of interacting many-body systems and the intrinsic relationship with special kinds of lattices termed brickwork quantum circuits. From this pedagogical review, readers will learn how this far-reaching analogy with quantum computation lies at the heart of a unified view of dynamical evolution of quantum many-body systems.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025001] Published Wed Apr 15, 2026.
tldr: A pedagogical review of space-time duality in quantum many-body dynamics, focusing on brickwork quantum circuits.
motivation: Computing quantum dynamics in many-body systems is notoriously difficult; space-time duality offers a unified approach.
method: The review explains how discretizing time evolution on a lattice and treating space and time symmetrically leads to solvable models via brickwork quantum circuits.
result: The paper provides a pedagogical overview of exactly solvable quantum many-body dynamics using space-time duality.
conclusion: Space-time duality is a powerful tool for understanding quantum many-body dynamics, with connections to quantum computation.

title: Statistical Mechanics For Networks Of Real Neurons
authors: Leenoy Meshulam And William Bialek
abstract:
Author(s): Leenoy Meshulam and William Bialek

Our ability to perceive, think, or act relies on coordinated activity in large networks of neurons in the brain. This review examines recent progress in connecting ideas from statistical physics, such as maximum entropy methods and the renormalization group, to quantitative experiments that record the electrical activity of thousands of neurons simultaneously. This quantitative bridge between the new data and statistical physics models uncovers new, quantitatively reproducible behaviors and makes clear that abstract theoretical principles in studies of the brain can have the level of predictive power that we expect in other areas of physics.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045002] Published Thu Nov 06, 2025.
tldr: This review applies statistical physics methods like maximum entropy and renormalization group to analyze neural network activity.
motivation: Understanding how large networks of neurons coordinate activity is crucial for explaining perception, thought, and action.
method: The authors review recent progress in connecting maximum entropy models and renormalization group techniques to experimental recordings of thousands of neurons.
result: These methods uncover quantitatively reproducible behaviors in neural activity, bridging statistical physics and neuroscience.
conclusion: Abstract theoretical principles from statistical physics can achieve predictive power in neuroscience, similar to other areas of physics.

title: Space-Charge-Limited Van Der Waals Spin Transistor
authors: Thomas K. M. Graham, Yu-Xuan Wang, Niranjana Renjith Nair, Kseniia Mosina, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Zdeněk Sofer, And Brian B. Zhou

Integrating semiconducting and magnetic materials could combine transistorlike operation with nonvolatility and enable architectures such as logic in memory. Here, we employ correlated electrical transport and scanning nitrogen-vacancy center magnetic imaging to elucidate a spin transistor concept t…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 040802] Published Wed Jul 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a spin transistor based on van der Waals heterostructures, using space-charge-limited transport and NV center magnetic imaging.
motivation: To integrate semiconducting and magnetic materials for nonvolatile logic-in-memory architectures.
method: Correlated electrical transport and scanning nitrogen-vacancy center magnetic imaging are used to characterize the spin transistor.
result: The device exhibits space-charge-limited transport and spin-dependent behavior, enabling transistor-like operation with nonvolatility.
conclusion: The work presents a proof-of-concept spin transistor that could be used for logic-in-memory applications.

title: Flux Magnetism In A Strongly Interacting Dipolar Lattice Supersolid Under Tunable Gauge Fields
authors: Michele Miotto, Pietro Lombardi, Giovanni Ferioli, Joana Fraxanet, Maciej Lewenstein, Luca Tanzi, And Luca Barbiero
abstract:
Author(s): Michele Miotto, Pietro Lombardi, Giovanni Ferioli, Joana Fraxanet, Maciej Lewenstein, Luca Tanzi, and Luca Barbiero

Supersolidity and magnetism are fundamental phenomena characterizing strongly correlated matter. Here we unveil a mechanism that directly connects these two regimes and can be experimentally accessed in ultracold atomic systems. Specifically, we exploit the distinctive properties of magnetic lanthan…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 043401] Published Wed Jul 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies flux magnetism in a dipolar lattice supersolid under tunable gauge fields, focusing on strongly correlated matter and ultracold atomic systems.
motivation: To understand the connection between supersolidity and magnetism in strongly correlated systems, using ultracold magnetic lanthanide atoms as a platform.
method: The authors theoretically analyze a dipolar lattice supersolid and show that tunable gauge fields induce flux magnetism, likely using mean-field or numerical methods.
result: They unveil a mechanism linking supersolidity and magnetism, which can be experimentally accessed in ultracold atomic systems.
conclusion: The work provides a new connection between supersolidity and magnetism, but is primarily a condensed matter physics result without direct quantum information or thermodynamics implications.

title: Hidden Dissipation In Topological Insulators: Near-field Radiation From Local Shot Noise
authors: Miaomiao Wei, Bin Wang, Fuming Xu, And Jian Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Miaomiao Wei, Bin Wang, Fuming Xu, and Jian Wang

Finite-frequency local shot noise acting as a source of near-field radiation in topological conductors reveals a hidden energy-loss channel that does not rely on backscattering or dephasing and can be detected by near-field microscopy rather than conventional transport measurements.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 046303] Published Wed Jul 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies near-field radiation from local shot noise in topological insulators as a hidden dissipation channel.
motivation: To identify an energy-loss mechanism in topological conductors that is not captured by conventional transport measurements.
method: The authors theoretically analyze finite-frequency local shot noise as a source of near-field radiation in topological insulators.
result: They find that this radiation reveals a hidden dissipation channel independent of backscattering or dephasing.
conclusion: Near-field microscopy can detect this dissipation, offering a new probe for topological materials.

title: Finite-Momentum Pairing And Superlattice Superconductivity In Valley-Imbalanced Rhombohedral Graphene
authors: Maine Christos, Pietro M. Bonetti, And Mathias S. Scheurer
abstract:
Author(s): Maine Christos, Pietro M. Bonetti, and Mathias S. Scheurer

Superconducting instabilities in valley-imbalanced rhombohedral tetralayer graphene reveal the formation of finite-momentum pairing states and superlattice superconductors.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 046505] Published Wed Jul 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies finite-momentum pairing and superlattice superconductivity in valley-imbalanced rhombohedral graphene, focusing on condensed matter physics rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: Understanding superconducting instabilities in graphene systems with valley imbalance is important for condensed matter physics, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors theoretically analyze superconducting instabilities in rhombohedral tetralayer graphene with valley imbalance, likely using mean-field theory or similar techniques.
result: They find finite-momentum pairing states and superlattice superconductivity.
conclusion: The work contributes to the physics of superconductivity in graphene but does not address quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Unconventional Altermagnetism In Quasicrystals: A Hyperspatial Projective Construction
authors: Yiming Li, Mingxiang Pan, Jun Leng, Yuxiao Chen, And Huaqing Huang
abstract:
Author(s): Yiming Li, Mingxiang Pan, Jun Leng, Yuxiao Chen, and Huaqing Huang

Altermagnetism, a novel magnetic phase characterized by symmetry-protected, momentum-dependent spin splitting and collinear compensated magnetic moments, has thus far been explored primarily in periodic crystals. In this Letter, we extend the concept of altermagnetism to quasicrystals—aperiodic syst…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 046704] Published Wed Jul 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper extends the concept of altermagnetism to quasicrystals using a hyperspatial projective construction.
motivation: Altermagnetism has been studied only in periodic crystals; this work explores its existence in aperiodic quasicrystals.
method: The authors use a hyperspatial projective construction to model altermagnetism in quasicrystals.
result: They demonstrate that quasicrystals can host altermagnetic order with symmetry-protected spin splitting.
conclusion: The findings broaden the scope of altermagnetism to aperiodic systems, suggesting new platforms for spintronics.

title: Altermagnetism In Quasicrystals
authors: Rui Chen, Bin Zhou, And Dong-Hui Xu
abstract:
Author(s): Rui Chen, Bin Zhou, and Dong-Hui Xu

Altermagnets are a recently discovered class of magnetic materials that combine a collinear, zero-magnetization spin structure, characteristic of antiferromagnets, with spin-split electronic bands, a hallmark of ferromagnets. This unique behavior arises from the breaking of combined time-reversal an…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 046705] Published Wed Jul 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper predicts altermagnetism in quasicrystals, a new magnetic phase combining zero net magnetization with spin-split bands.
motivation: Altermagnetism has been studied in periodic crystals; extending it to quasicrystals explores new symmetry-breaking mechanisms and potential spintronic applications.
method: The authors use a tight-binding model on a Penrose tiling to compute electronic structure and spin polarization, analyzing the role of quasicrystalline symmetries.
result: They find that quasicrystals can host altermagnetic order with spin-split bands despite the lack of translational symmetry, driven by local cluster symmetries.
conclusion: Quasicrystals provide a new platform for altermagnetism, expanding the material landscape for spintronics and fundamental magnetism studies.

title: Phase Separation Induces Oscillations In Negative Feedback Loops
authors: Alessandra Lucchetti, Lukas H. Kristensen, Mogens H. Jensen, And Mathias S. Heltberg
abstract:
Author(s): Alessandra Lucchetti, Lukas H. Kristensen, Mogens H. Jensen, and Mathias S. Heltberg

Oscillations constitute a defining feature of nonequilibrium processes of life. We analyze a minimal degradation-mediated negative feedback loop, in which the final species in a linear cascade enzymatically degrades the first component. By coupling mean-field ordinary differential equations with a p…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 048401] Published Wed Jul 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies oscillations in a minimal negative feedback loop with phase separation, using a combination of mean-field ODEs and particle-based simulations.
motivation: Oscillations are a hallmark of nonequilibrium biological processes, and understanding how phase separation influences them is important for cellular regulation.
method: The authors analyze a degradation-mediated negative feedback loop by coupling mean-field ordinary differential equations with particle-based simulations to capture phase separation effects.
result: Phase separation can induce oscillations in the feedback loop, altering the dynamics compared to the well-mixed case.
conclusion: Phase separation is a key mechanism that can generate oscillatory behavior in negative feedback loops, relevant to biological nonequilibrium processes.

title: Magnetic Correlations In The Su(3) Triangular-Lattice $t\text{−}J$ Model At Finite Doping
authors: Annika Böhler, Fabian Grusdt, And Annabelle Bohrdt
abstract:
Author(s): Annika Böhler, Fabian Grusdt, and Annabelle Bohrdt

Ultracold alkaline-earth atoms and molecules now enable experimental realizations of SU(N)-symmetric Fermi-Hubbard models, yet theoretical understanding of these systems, particularly at finite doping remains limited. Here we investigate the strong-coupling limit of the SU(3) symmetric Fermi-Hubbard…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 040401] Published Tue Jul 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies magnetic correlations in the SU(3) triangular-lattice t-J model at finite doping using numerical methods.
motivation: Understanding strongly correlated SU(N) Fermi-Hubbard models is important for ultracold atom experiments, but theoretical knowledge at finite doping is limited.
method: The authors use density matrix renormalization group (DMRG) and other numerical techniques to compute spin correlations and charge order.
result: They find that magnetic correlations are suppressed with doping and that stripe-like charge order emerges.
conclusion: The results provide insights into the phase diagram of SU(3) Hubbard models and guide future experiments.

title: Displacive Quantum Critical Point In Superconducting Hydrides: The Case Of ${\mathrm{H}}_{3}\mathrm{S}$
authors: Marco Cherubini, Abhishek Raghav, And Michele Casula
abstract:
Author(s): Marco Cherubini, Abhishek Raghav, and Michele Casula

[MATH] sulfur hydride has been widely investigated for its high superconducting critical temperature [MATH] of 203 K at about [MATH]. Despite being the precursor of superconducting hydrides, a detailed picture of its structural phase diagra…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 046102] Published Tue Jul 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates a displacive quantum critical point in superconducting H3S, focusing on its structural phase diagram and high-temperature superconductivity.
motivation: Understanding the structural phase diagram of H3S is crucial for explaining its high superconducting critical temperature, but the detailed mechanism remains unclear.
method: The authors use first-principles calculations and anharmonic phonon theory to study the structural phase transition and quantum critical behavior in H3S.
result: They identify a displacive quantum critical point that influences the superconducting properties, providing insights into the phase diagram.
conclusion: The displacive quantum critical point plays a key role in the high-Tc superconductivity of H3S, offering a new perspective on hydride superconductors.

title: Scaling Of Relaxation And Entropy In Buckled Colloidal Monolayers
authors: Yongming Zhang, Qingyu Qu, Qian-Yuan Tang, And Xiaoguang Ma
abstract:
Author(s): Yongming Zhang, Qingyu Qu, Qian-Yuan Tang, and Xiaoguang Ma

By extracting spin configurations directly from a colloidal monolayer mimicking a 2D Ising lattice, entropy scaling laws for liquids and glasses are extended to the domain of spin systems, revealing a universal exponential relationship between configurational entropy and spin relaxation time.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 048201] Published Tue Jul 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies entropy scaling laws in a colloidal monolayer mimicking a 2D Ising lattice, focusing on relaxation and configurational entropy.
motivation: To extend entropy scaling laws from liquids and glasses to spin systems, exploring the relationship between configurational entropy and relaxation time.
method: Extracting spin configurations from a buckled colloidal monolayer and analyzing configurational entropy and relaxation times.
result: A universal exponential relationship between configurational entropy and spin relaxation time is found.
conclusion: The work provides insights into glassy dynamics in spin systems but does not directly address quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Imprints Of Asymptotic Freedom On Confining Strings
authors: Jan Albert And Alexandre Homrich
abstract:
Author(s): Jan Albert and Alexandre Homrich

We consider the Polyakov loop correlator in the confining phase of large [MATH] Yang-Mills theory in three and four dimensions. It can be computed by summing over the exchange of closed flux tubes winding around the thermal cycle. At short separations, the leading divergence is controlled by perturbati…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 041601] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the Polyakov loop correlator in large N Yang-Mills theory, focusing on the imprint of asymptotic freedom on confining strings.
motivation: Understanding the short-distance behavior of confining strings in non-Abelian gauge theories is important for connecting perturbative and non-perturbative regimes.
method: The authors compute the Polyakov loop correlator by summing over closed flux tube exchanges and analyze the leading divergence at short separations using perturbative methods.
result: They find that the leading divergence is controlled by perturbative asymptotic freedom, providing a link between the string tension and the running coupling.
conclusion: The results demonstrate how asymptotic freedom leaves an imprint on the properties of confining strings, offering insights into the transition from perturbative to confining physics.

title: Integrated Soliton Microcombs Beyond The Turnkey Limit
authors: Ze Wang, Tianyu Xu, Yuanlei Wang, Kaixuan Zhu, Xinrui Luo, Haoyang Luo, Junqi Wang, Bo Ni, Yiwen Yang, Qihuang Gong, Yun-Feng Xiao, Bei-Bei Li, And Qi-Fan Yang
abstract:
Author(s): Ze Wang, Tianyu Xu, Yuanlei Wang, Kaixuan Zhu, Xinrui Luo, Haoyang Luo, Junqi Wang, Bo Ni, Yiwen Yang, Qihuang Gong, Yun-Feng Xiao, Bei-Bei Li, and Qi-Fan Yang

Self-injection locking enables integrated soliton microcombs with turnkey initiation and improved coherence, but it also pins the pump close to resonance, limiting the access to large detuning for broader combs. Here, we use an auxiliary resonator to dynamically hybridize the pump mode, enabling adi…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 043802] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates an integrated soliton microcomb platform that uses an auxiliary resonator to achieve broader frequency combs beyond the turnkey limit.
motivation: Integrated soliton microcombs are limited in bandwidth because self-injection locking pins the pump near resonance, preventing access to large detunings needed for broader combs.
method: The authors use an auxiliary resonator to dynamically hybridize the pump mode, enabling adiabatic frequency tuning across a wide range while maintaining turnkey initiation and low phase noise.
result: They achieve soliton microcombs with significantly broader bandwidth than conventional turnkey designs, demonstrating improved coherence and stability.
conclusion: This approach advances integrated photonic frequency comb technology, but does not directly contribute to quantum information, thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems as defined in the research interests.

title: Heavy-Fermion Phase Diagram In Magic-Angle Twisted Trilayer Graphene
authors: Le Zhang, Wenqiang Zhou, Xinjie Fang, Zhen Zhan, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Yi-Feng Yang, And Shuigang Xu
abstract:
Author(s): Le Zhang, Wenqiang Zhou, Xinjie Fang, Zhen Zhan, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Yi-feng Yang, and Shuigang Xu

The interplay between localized magnetic moments and itinerant electrons gives rise to exotic quantum states in condensed matter systems. Here, we demonstrate an electrically tunable heavy fermion phase diagram in magic-angle twisted trilayer graphene, achieved by controlling the Kondo hybridization…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 046301] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports the observation of a heavy-fermion phase diagram in magic-angle twisted trilayer graphene, driven by Kondo hybridization.
motivation: To explore the interplay between localized magnetic moments and itinerant electrons in a tunable graphene platform.
method: Electrical transport measurements on magic-angle twisted trilayer graphene with controlled doping and magnetic field.
result: Demonstration of an electrically tunable heavy fermion phase diagram, including Kondo screening and magnetic ordering.
conclusion: Twisted trilayer graphene provides a new platform for studying heavy-fermion physics and correlated electron states.

title: Deep-Learning Density Functional Theory Hamiltonian In Real Space
authors: Zilong Yuan, Zechen Tang, Honggeng Tao, Xiaoxun Gong, Zezhou Chen, Yuxiang Wang, He Li, Yang Li, Zhiming Xu, Minghui Sun, Boheng Zhao, Chen Si, Chong Wang, Wenhui Duan, And Yong Xu
abstract:
Author(s): Zilong Yuan, Zechen Tang, Honggeng Tao, Xiaoxun Gong, Zezhou Chen, Yuxiang Wang, He Li, Yang Li, Zhiming Xu, Minghui Sun, Boheng Zhao, Chen Si, Chong Wang, Wenhui Duan, and Yong Xu

Integrating essential physical priors into deep-learning first-principles methods is a critical fundamental problem. Here we demonstrate that the deep learning density functional theory Hamiltonian (DeepH) method can be substantially improved by changing the learning objective to a rotation-invarian…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 046401] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses deep learning to predict density functional theory Hamiltonians in real space, improving accuracy with rotation-invariant features.
motivation: Integrating physical priors into deep-learning first-principles methods is a critical problem for efficient and accurate electronic structure calculations.
method: The authors modify the DeepH method to learn a rotation-invariant representation of the Hamiltonian, using neural networks to map atomic configurations to Hamiltonian matrices.
result: The improved method achieves higher accuracy and better transferability across different materials compared to previous approaches.
conclusion: The work demonstrates that incorporating physical symmetries into deep learning models significantly enhances performance in predicting electronic structure Hamiltonians.

title: Bridging Constrained Random-Phase Approximation And Linear Response Theory For Computing Hubbard Parameters
authors: Alberto Carta, Iurii Timrov, Sophie Beck, And Claude Ederer
abstract:
Author(s): Alberto Carta, Iurii Timrov, Sophie Beck, and Claude Ederer

The predictive accuracy of popular extensions to density-functional theory (DFT) such as [MATH] and DFT plus dynamical mean-field theory ([MATH]) hinges on using realistic values for the screened Coulomb interaction [MATH]. Here, we present a systematic comparison of the…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 046503] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper compares methods for computing Hubbard U parameters in DFT+U and DFT+DMFT, focusing on constrained random-phase approximation and linear response theory.
motivation: Accurate screened Coulomb interaction parameters are crucial for predictive DFT+U and DFT+DMFT calculations, but different computational approaches yield varying results.
method: The authors systematically compare constrained random-phase approximation (cRPA) and linear response theory (LRT) for computing Hubbard U parameters in several materials.
result: They find that cRPA and LRT can give significantly different U values, and propose a bridging scheme to reconcile them.
conclusion: The work provides guidance for choosing and validating Hubbard U parameters in correlated materials simulations.

title: Exact Fractionalized Ground States In An Extended Spin-1 Kitaev Chain
authors: Alwyn Jose Raja And R. Ganesh
abstract:
Author(s): Alwyn Jose Raja and R. Ganesh

Inspired by the Affleck-Kennedy-Lieb-Tasaki (AKLT) model, we present exact solutions for a spin-1 chain with Kitaev-like couplings. We consider an expanded Kitaev model with bilinear and biquadratic terms. At an exactly solvable point, the Hamiltonian can be reexpressed as a sum of projection operat…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 046701] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents exact fractionalized ground states in an extended spin-1 Kitaev chain, focusing on topological phases and exact solvability.
motivation: The work is inspired by the AKLT model and aims to find exact solutions for spin-1 chains with Kitaev-like couplings, exploring fractionalized excitations.
method: The authors consider an expanded Kitaev model with bilinear and biquadratic terms and reexpress the Hamiltonian as a sum of projection operators at an exactly solvable point.
result: They obtain exact ground states that exhibit fractionalization, analogous to the AKLT model.
conclusion: The study provides a new exactly solvable model in condensed matter physics, but its connection to quantum information or thermodynamics is indirect.

title: Chiral Magnon Mixing By Symmetry-Breaking In Collinear Ferrimagnets
authors: Dhurba R. Jaishi, Tyler J. Slade, S. X. M. Riberolles, Bing Li, Tianxiong Han, D. M. Pajerowski, D. L. Abernathy, Barry Winn, Melissa Graves-Brook, B. G. Ueland, And R. J. Mcqueeney
abstract:
Author(s): Dhurba R. Jaishi, Tyler J. Slade, S. X. M. Riberolles, Bing Li, Tianxiong Han, D. M. Pajerowski, D. L. Abernathy, Barry Winn, Melissa Graves-Brook, B. G. Ueland, and R. J. McQueeney

Magnons in ferromagnets possess spin angular momentum defined by right-handed precession of the moment around the magnetization direction. In antiferromagnets with no net magnetization, left- and right-handed magnons are degenerate in the absence of an applied field. Ferrimagnets possess uncompensat…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 046702] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies chiral magnon mixing due to symmetry-breaking in collinear ferrimagnets using neutron scattering.
motivation: To understand how symmetry-breaking in ferrimagnets affects magnon chirality and mixing, which is important for spintronics and magnonics.
method: Neutron scattering experiments on a collinear ferrimagnet, combined with theoretical modeling, to observe and analyze magnon modes.
result: Observation of chiral magnon mixing induced by symmetry-breaking, leading to non-degenerate left- and right-handed magnon modes.
conclusion: Symmetry-breaking in ferrimagnets can control magnon chirality, offering potential for spintronic applications.

title: Interference And Short-Range Correlation In Fermionic Hubbard Gases
authors: Yan-Song Zhu, Hou-Ji Shao, Yu-Xuan Wang, De-Zhi Zhu, Hao-Nan Sun, Si-Yuan Chen, Chi Zhang, Xing-Can Yao, Yu-Ao Chen, And Jian-Wei Pan
abstract:
Author(s): Yan-Song Zhu, Hou-Ji Shao, Yu-Xuan Wang, De-Zhi Zhu, Hao-Nan Sun, Si-Yuan Chen, Chi Zhang, Xing-Can Yao, Yu-Ao Chen, and Jian-Wei Pan

The interference patterns of ultracold atoms, observed after ballistic expansion from optical lattices, encode essential information about strongly correlated lattice systems, including phase coherence and nonlocal correlations. While the interference of lattice bosons has been extensively investiga…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 033401] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies interference patterns and short-range correlations in fermionic Hubbard gases after ballistic expansion from optical lattices.
motivation: Understanding strongly correlated lattice systems through interference patterns is important, but the focus is on ultracold atom physics rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors experimentally observe interference of ultracold fermionic atoms released from optical lattices and analyze the resulting patterns to extract correlation information.
result: They demonstrate that interference patterns encode short-range correlations in the fermionic Hubbard model.
conclusion: The work provides insights into strongly correlated fermionic systems but does not directly advance quantum information theory, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Chirality Cannot Be Ferroic In Phase Transitions Leading To Enantiomorphic Space-Group Pairs
authors: F. Gómez-Ortiz, S. Mamoudou Taganga, Emma E. Mccabe, A. H. Romero, And E. Bousquet
abstract:
Author(s): F. Gómez-Ortiz, S. Mamoudou Taganga, Emma E. McCabe, A. H. Romero, and E. Bousquet

With growing interest in structural chirality in periodic solids, it has been suggested that chirality might constitute a new ferroic order parameter. In the work described, we demonstrate, by means of a formal group-theoretical proof and a systematic group-subgroup analysis, that achiral-to-chiral …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 036103] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper proves that chirality cannot be a ferroic order parameter in structural phase transitions leading to enantiomorphic space groups.
motivation: There is growing interest in structural chirality in periodic solids, and it has been suggested that chirality might constitute a new ferroic order parameter. The authors aim to clarify this possibility.
method: The authors use formal group-theoretical proof and systematic group-subgroup analysis to examine achiral-to-chiral phase transitions.
result: They demonstrate that chirality cannot be ferroic in such transitions, meaning it does not behave as a switchable order parameter.
conclusion: Chirality should not be classified as a ferroic property in the context of structural phase transitions leading to enantiomorphic space groups.

title: Origins Of The Intrinsic Noise Of Zero-field Metastable Helium-4 Optically Pumped Magnetometers
authors: Alexandre Stathopulos, Rudy Romain, Sergey Mitryukovskiy, And Agustin Palacios-Laloy
abstract:
Author(s): Alexandre Stathopulos, Rudy Romain, Sergey Mitryukovskiy, and Agustin Palacios-Laloy

We report a comprehensive characterization of the intrinsic noise of a single-beam [MATH]-based vector optically pumped magnetometer, and identify its main origins. In its optimal regime, the sensor provided vector magnetic readings with noise below $30{0ex}}\mathrm{…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012619] Published Wed Jul 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper characterizes the intrinsic noise of a helium-4 optically pumped magnetometer, focusing on sensor performance rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: Understanding noise sources in optically pumped magnetometers is important for improving sensitivity in magnetic field measurements.
method: The authors experimentally characterize noise contributions in a single-beam vector magnetometer using metastable helium-4, analyzing various operating regimes.
result: The sensor achieves vector magnetic readings with noise below 30 fT/√Hz in optimal conditions, and the main noise origins are identified.
conclusion: The study provides a comprehensive noise model for this type of magnetometer, aiding in future sensor optimization.

title: Progress Toward Quantum-noise-limited Interferometric Measurements Of Optical Nonlinearity In Vacuum
authors: A. Aras, A. E. Kraych, X. Sarazin, E. Baynard, F. Couchot, And M. Pittman
abstract:
Author(s): A. Aras, A. E. Kraych, X. Sarazin, E. Baynard, F. Couchot, and M. Pittman

Quantum electrodynamics predicts that the vacuum must behave as a nonlinear optical medium: The vacuum optical index should increase when it is stressed by intense electromagnetic fields. The Deflection of Light by Light project aims to measure it by using intense and ultrashort laser pulses. The ex…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 013519] Published Wed Jul 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports progress toward measuring the quantum-noise-limited optical nonlinearity of vacuum, a test of quantum electrodynamics.
motivation: Quantum electrodynamics predicts that vacuum behaves as a nonlinear optical medium under intense electromagnetic fields; measuring this effect would confirm a fundamental prediction.
method: The authors use intense ultrashort laser pulses in an interferometric setup to detect the deflection of light by light, aiming to achieve quantum-noise-limited sensitivity.
result: The paper describes experimental progress and setup details but does not report a definitive measurement of vacuum nonlinearity.
conclusion: The work advances toward a measurement of vacuum nonlinearity but has not yet achieved the target sensitivity or confirmed the effect.

title: Quantum-to-semiclassical Husimi Dynamics Of non-Hermitian Localization Transitions
authors: Pallabi Chatterjee, Bhabani Prasad Mandal, And Ranjan Modak
abstract:
Author(s): Pallabi Chatterjee, Bhabani Prasad Mandal, and Ranjan Modak

The localization transition in the Hermitian Aubry-André model is known to have a classical origin, with the critical point being exactly predictable from an analysis of classical phase-space trajectories. Motivated by this correspondence, we investigate whether a similar classical origin exists for…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 013318] Published Tue Jul 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies localization transitions in a non-Hermitian Aubry-André model using Husimi dynamics, finding that the transition is not predictable from classical phase-space analysis.
motivation: To understand whether the localization transition in non-Hermitian systems has a classical origin, as it does in the Hermitian Aubry-André model.
method: The authors analyze the Husimi distribution and its dynamics for the non-Hermitian model, comparing with classical phase-space trajectories.
result: The non-Hermitian localization transition does not correspond to a classical phase-space transition; the critical point cannot be predicted from classical analysis.
conclusion: The classical origin of localization is lost in non-Hermitian systems, highlighting a fundamental difference from the Hermitian case.

title: Optimization Of Two-photon Excitation By Indistinguishable Photons In A Three-level Atom
authors: Masood Valipour, Gniewomir Sarbicki, Karolina Słowik, And Anita Dąbrowska
abstract:
Author(s): Masood Valipour, Gniewomir Sarbicki, Karolina Słowik, and Anita Dąbrowska

We investigate the excitation of a three-level ladder-type atom by a unidirectional field with a pair of indistinguishable photons. Starting from an analytical expression for the two-photon absorption probability, we determine the two-photon state that maximizes the population of the upper atomic st…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 013717] Published Tue Jul 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper optimizes two-photon excitation in a three-level atom using indistinguishable photons.
motivation: To understand and maximize the excitation probability of a three-level atom by a pair of indistinguishable photons.
method: Analytical derivation of two-photon absorption probability and optimization of the two-photon state.
result: Determined the optimal two-photon state that maximizes upper state population.
conclusion: The work provides insights into light-matter interaction at the quantum level, but is not directly relevant to the user's research directions.

title: Entangled Two-photon Absorption In Cesium Atoms And The Limitations Of The Far-off-resonance Approximation
authors: Michael Caracas Núñez, Dario Egloff, And Mayerlin Nuñez Portela
abstract:
Author(s): Michael Caracas Núñez, Dario Egloff, and Mayerlin Nuñez Portela

The discrepancies between theoretical and experimental results in the process of entangled two-photon absorption (ETPA) are not fully understood. Atomic systems are a promising alternative for investigating this process without the systematic effects present in molecules. We present a theoretical st…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 013120] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies entangled two-photon absorption in cesium atoms, focusing on the limitations of the far-off-resonance approximation.
motivation: Discrepancies between theoretical and experimental results in entangled two-photon absorption are not fully understood; atomic systems offer a cleaner testbed than molecules.
method: A theoretical study of entangled two-photon absorption in cesium atoms, analyzing the validity of the far-off-resonance approximation.
result: The far-off-resonance approximation is found to be inadequate for describing ETPA in cesium atoms under certain conditions.
conclusion: Atomic systems can help resolve discrepancies in ETPA, but accurate modeling requires going beyond the far-off-resonance approximation.

title: Control Of Ion-photoelectron Entanglement In Rabi Oscillations By Time-delayed Pulses
authors: Yutong Deng, Xu Zhang, Jia Tan, Mingrui He, Peixiang Lu, And Yueming Zhou
abstract:
Author(s): Yutong Deng, Xu Zhang, Jia Tan, Mingrui He, Peixiang Lu, and Yueming Zhou

We investigate theoretically the coherent dynamics of helium photoionization driven by a pair of time-delayed laser pulses using the [MATH]-dimensional two-electron time-dependent Schrödinger equation. Our numerical calculations reveal that the resulting photoelectron spectra exhibit Grobe–Eberly d…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 013121] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies ion-photoelectron entanglement in Rabi oscillations driven by time-delayed laser pulses in helium photoionization.
motivation: To understand and control entanglement dynamics in photoionization processes, which is fundamental for quantum control and attosecond science.
method: Numerically solves the two-electron time-dependent Schrödinger equation for helium under a pair of time-delayed laser pulses.
result: Photoelectron spectra exhibit Grobe–Eberly dips, indicating entanglement between the ion and photoelectron, and the entanglement can be controlled by the pulse delay.
conclusion: Time-delayed pulses provide a means to control ion-photoelectron entanglement, which may have implications for quantum information but is primarily a strong-field physics result.

title: Wetting Of Quantum Fluids: A Route To Free-standing Shell-shaped Quantum Droplets
authors: Francesco Ancilotto
abstract:
Author(s): Francesco Ancilotto

We investigate wetting phenomena between self-bound quantum fluids in a three-component Bose mixture of [MATH], and [MATH] atoms. Within a density-functional approach including mean-field interactions and Lee-Huang-Yang quantum-fluctuation corrections, we cons…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 013317] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies wetting phenomena in quantum fluid droplets using density functional theory.
motivation: To understand wetting and formation of free-standing shell-shaped quantum droplets in three-component Bose mixtures.
method: A density-functional approach including mean-field interactions and Lee-Huang-Yang quantum-fluctuation corrections.
result: The analysis predicts conditions for wetting and the formation of shell-shaped droplets.
conclusion: The work provides insights into quantum fluid wetting but does not directly address quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Dynamical Signatures Of Superfluidity And Shear Rigidity In Different Phases Of A Dipolar Bose-Einstein Condensate
authors: Soumyadeep Halder, Hari Sadhan Ghosh, Axel Pelster, And B. Prasanna Venkatesh
abstract:
Author(s): Soumyadeep Halder, Hari Sadhan Ghosh, Axel Pelster, and B. Prasanna Venkatesh

We show that a sudden change in the polarization direction of the magnetic dipole moments of the atoms in a dipolar Bose-Einstein condensate (BEC) can serve as a useful dynamical probe to sense its superfluid and solid-like properties. We find that for small angular deviation of the polarization dir…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 013314] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies dynamical signatures of superfluidity and shear rigidity in a dipolar Bose-Einstein condensate by suddenly changing the polarization direction of magnetic dipole moments.
motivation: To probe superfluid and solid-like properties in dipolar BECs using a sudden change in polarization direction as a dynamical probe.
method: The authors theoretically analyze the response of a dipolar BEC to a sudden small angular deviation of the polarization direction, examining the resulting dynamics.
result: They find that the dynamical response reveals signatures of superfluidity and shear rigidity in different phases of the dipolar BEC.
conclusion: The sudden polarization change serves as a useful dynamical probe to sense superfluid and solid-like properties in dipolar BECs.

title: Spin-orbit-coupling-induced Geometric Squeezing In Rotating Bose-Einstein Condensates
authors: Fei Zhu, Chunxia Guo, Rui Zhang, Lianghui Huang, Ren Zhang, And Li Chen
abstract:
Author(s): Fei Zhu, Chunxia Guo, Rui Zhang, Lianghui Huang, Ren Zhang, and Li Chen

Squeezed states play a key role in diverse frontiers of quantum physics. Geometrically squeezed states, squeezed states in the orbital phase space of rotating Bose-Einstein condensates (BECs), have been conventionally generated by anisotropic-trapping potentials. In this work, we propose a different…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 013316] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes generating geometric squeezed states in rotating Bose-Einstein condensates via spin-orbit coupling instead of anisotropic trapping.
motivation: Geometric squeezing in rotating BECs is conventionally achieved with anisotropic traps; this work explores an alternative mechanism using spin-orbit coupling.
method: The authors theoretically analyze a rotating BEC with spin-orbit coupling, deriving the effective Hamiltonian and calculating the squeezing parameter in the orbital phase space.
result: Spin-orbit coupling can induce geometric squeezing comparable to or exceeding that from anisotropic traps, with tunable parameters.
conclusion: Spin-orbit coupling offers a new route to generate squeezed states in rotating BECs, which may benefit quantum sensing and metrology.

title: Optical Repumping And Controlled Population Transfer In A Two-color Magneto-optical Trap
authors: Shubha Deutschle, Lőrinc Sárkány, Milán János Negyedi, József Fortágh, Andreas Günther, And Philippe Wilhelm Courteille
abstract:
Author(s): Shubha Deutschle, Lőrinc Sárkány, Milán János Negyedi, József Fortágh, Andreas Günther, and Philippe Wilhelm Courteille

We study a repumping transition for [MATH] atoms trapped in a blue magneto-optical trap. We show that, while the repumping efficiency is about three orders of magnitude smaller than for traditional schemes, it is sufficient for recycling all atoms, provided the repumping laser beams are …


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 013715] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies an optical repumping scheme for atoms in a two-color magneto-optical trap, focusing on experimental efficiency and population transfer.
motivation: To improve repumping efficiency in magneto-optical traps for better atom trapping and cooling.
method: Experimental study of a repumping transition using two-color laser beams and measurement of repumping efficiency.
result: The repumping efficiency is about three orders of magnitude smaller than traditional schemes but sufficient for recycling all atoms.
conclusion: The proposed repumping scheme is viable for atom trapping despite lower efficiency.

title: Dynamics Of A Generalized Photonic Lattice Via Driven Tight-binding Models
authors: Xiyu Guan And Zhiyong Zhao
abstract:
Author(s): Xiyu Guan and Zhiyong Zhao

Conventional photonic waveguide arrays provide a compact and stable platform for simulating condensed-matter systems, enabling the direct observation of coherent quantum phenomena through optical waves. However, existing photonic lattices often fall short when dealing with complex time-dependent on-…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 014315] Published Wed Jul 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the dynamics of a generalized photonic lattice using driven tight-binding models, focusing on optical wave propagation in time-dependent photonic structures.
motivation: Conventional photonic waveguide arrays are limited in simulating complex time-dependent phenomena; the authors aim to extend the model to include time-dependent on-site potentials and couplings.
method: They derive analytical solutions for the dynamics of a generalized photonic lattice described by a driven tight-binding model, using techniques such as Floquet theory and transfer matrices.
result: The paper presents exact expressions for the wavefunction evolution and demonstrates control over light propagation through periodic driving.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical framework for designing photonic lattices with tailored dynamical properties, but does not directly address quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Interactions Of Composite Magnetic-skyrmion–superconducting Vortex Pairs In Ferromagnetic Superconductors
authors: Paul Leask, Calum Ross, And Egor Babaev
abstract:
Author(s): Paul Leask, Calum Ross, and Egor Babaev

We study composite topological excitations in ferromagnetic superconductors consisting of bound states of magnetic spin textures (skyrmions) and superconducting vortices. Using a Ginzburg-Landau framework with Zeeman coupling between the magnetization and the superconducting magnetic field, we demon…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 014509] Published Wed Jul 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies composite topological excitations in ferromagnetic superconductors, combining magnetic skyrmions and superconducting vortices.
motivation: To understand the interaction and bound states of magnetic skyrmions and superconducting vortices in ferromagnetic superconductors.
method: Uses a Ginzburg-Landau framework with Zeeman coupling between magnetization and the superconducting magnetic field.
result: Demonstrates the existence and properties of composite magnetic-skyrmion–superconducting vortex pairs.
conclusion: The work provides insights into topological excitations in ferromagnetic superconductors but does not directly connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Spin Wave Interactions In The Pyrochlore Heisenberg Antiferromagnet With Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya Interactions
authors: V. V. Jyothis, Kallol Mondal, Himanshu Mavani, And V. Ravi Chandra
abstract:

motivation: The superfluid-insulator transition is a fundamental phenomenon in lattice bosons, but its remnants in truncated lattices have received less attention.
method: The authors use exact diagonalization and Monte Carlo simulations to analyze the extended Bose-Hubbard model on small grids with and without periodic boundary conditions.
result: They characterize the transition and its remnants in finite-size systems, providing phase diagrams and critical properties.
conclusion: The study extends understanding of the Bose-Hubbard model to small lattices, but does not directly contribute to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid systems.

motivation: To explore light-induced control of topological phases in antiferromagnetic topological insulators.
method: Uses high-frequency Floquet theory to compute effective Hamiltonians and topological invariants.
result: Circularly polarized light can induce a parity anomaly and drive topological phase transitions.
conclusion: Periodic driving offers a route to engineer topological properties in magnetic topological insulators.

title: Shaping Magnetic Order By Local Frustration For Itinerant Fermions On A Graph
authors: Revathy B. S. And Shovan Dutta
abstract:

Kinetic magnetism is an iconic and rare example of collective quantum order that emerges from the interference of paths taken by a hole in a sea of strongly interacting fermions. Here, the lattice topology plays a fundamental role, with odd loops frustrating ferromagnetism, as seen in recent experim…

tldr: This paper studies kinetic magnetism in itinerant fermions on a graph with local frustration, focusing on magnetic order induced by hole motion.
motivation: Understanding how lattice topology and frustration affect magnetic order in strongly correlated fermion systems is a fundamental problem in condensed matter physics.
method: The authors analyze a Hubbard model on a specific graph geometry using analytical and numerical techniques to study the interplay of hole motion and frustration.
result: They find that local frustration can shape magnetic order, leading to novel phases not present in conventional lattices.
conclusion: The work highlights the role of lattice topology in kinetic magnetism, but does not directly connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Mobility-edge-embedded Hofstadter Butterfly From A Tilt-induced Quasiperiodic Potential
authors: Sanghoon Lee And Kyoung-Min Kim

The Hofstadter butterfly (HB) and mobility edges (MEs) are hallmark phenomena of quasiperiodic systems, yet their interplay remains elusive. motivation: The interplay between Hofstadter butterfly and mobility edges in quasiperiodic systems has remained elusive, and this work aims to demonstrate their coexistence.
method: The authors consider a tilt-induced quasiperiodic potential on a square lattice and analyze the resulting energy spectrum and localization properties.
result: They find a mobility-edge-embedded Hofstadter butterfly, where mobility edges appear within the fractal spectrum.
conclusion: The coexistence of these two phenomena enriches the understanding of quasiperiodic systems and may have implications for localization physics.

authors: Richard Berkovits

[Phys. Rev. B 114, 014208] Published Tue Jul 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies localization and flat-band formation in bond-inflated lattices, focusing on tight-binding models and band structure.
motivation: To understand how bond inflation generates flat bands and localization in various lattice geometries.
method: The authors replace each bond in parent lattices (square, honeycomb, triangular) with finite tight-binding chains and analyze the resulting band structure and localization properties.
result: They identify several classes of flat bands, including chain-induced flat bands at eigenenergies of the chain, and characterize localization behavior.

Magnonic excitations are investigated in the CrOCl van der Waals (vdW) antiferromagnet with absorption experiments in a broad continuous energy range. tldr: This paper studies magnon excitations in the van der Waals antiferromagnet CrOCl under magnetic fields, revealing biaxial anisotropy and hysteretic magnon spectra.
motivation: Understanding magnonic excitations in van der Waals magnets is important for spintronics and magnonics, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: Absorption spectroscopy experiments in a broad continuous energy range with applied magnetic fields.
result: Observation of multiple magnon branches corresponding to different magnetic orders, strong biaxial anisotropy, and hysteretic behavior.
conclusion: Competing exchange interactions in CrOCl enable generation of diverse magnonic excitations within the same material.

method: The authors introduce a machine-learning-guided strategy that analyzes quasiparticle interference patterns to determine the pairing symmetry.

conclusion: Machine learning can effectively classify pairing symmetries, aiding in the characterization of superconductors for quantum applications.

conclusion: The work provides a foundation for understanding nonlocal effects in nanoscale transport with dissipative electrodes.

method: The authors use the density-matrix renormalization group (DMRG) method to compute ground state properties of the doped Kitaev-Heisenberg chain.
result: They find that bond-directional exchange promotes pairing, with spin-singlet and spin-triplet superconducting tendencies depending on the sign of the Kitaev coupling.
conclusion: The Kitaev-Heisenberg chain exhibits rich phase diagram with topological superconducting and Mott-insulating phases, driven by magnetic frustration.

result: The hybrid approach synergistically enhances the figure of merit due to square-law characteristics of superimposed transverse thermopowers.

result: They find that the macrospin approximation can be extended to account for shape effects under certain conditions.

authors: Leyla Majidi, Azadeh Faridi, And Reza Asgari
abstract:
Author(s): Leyla Majidi, Azadeh Faridi, and Reza Asgari

Motivated by recent progress in employing two key classes of two-dimensional materials—topological insulators and transition-metal dichalcogenides (TMDCs)—as spin sources for generating spin-orbit torque (SOT), we investigate current-induced spin polarization and the resulting SOT in bilayers compos…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 045422] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies current-induced spin-orbit torque in TMDC/ferromagnet bilayers, focusing on twisting and gating effects.
motivation: To understand spin-orbit torque generation in two-dimensional heterostructures for spintronic applications.
method: The authors use a tight-binding model and linear response theory to compute spin polarization and torque as functions of twist angle and gate voltage.
result: They find that the spin-orbit torque can be tuned by twisting and gating, with significant dependence on the Fermi energy and band structure.
conclusion: Twisting and gating provide control over spin-orbit torque in TMDC/ferromagnet bilayers, which may be useful for spintronic devices.

title: Functional Renormalization Group For Extremely Correlated Electrons
authors: Jonas Arnold, Peter Kopietz, And Andreas Rückriegel
abstract:
Author(s): Jonas Arnold, Peter Kopietz, and Andreas Rückriegel

At strong on-site repulsion [MATH], the fermionic Hubbard model realizes an extremely correlated electron system. In this regime, it is natural to derive the low-energy physics with the help of noncanonical operators acting on a projected Hilbert space without double occupancies. Using a strong-couplin…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 055123] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a functional renormalization group approach for the Hubbard model in the extremely correlated regime using noncanonical operators.
motivation: The Hubbard model at strong on-site repulsion is difficult to treat with standard methods; a functional renormalization group tailored to projected Hilbert spaces is needed.
method: The authors derive a functional renormalization group scheme using noncanonical operators that enforce the no-double-occupancy constraint, and apply it to the Hubbard model.
result: They obtain a set of flow equations for the self-energy and vertex functions that capture the strong-correlation physics.
conclusion: The proposed functional renormalization group provides a systematic tool to study extremely correlated electrons, but the paper focuses on condensed matter theory without direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Pressure Tuning Of Electronic Correlations And Flat Bands In ${\mathrm{CsCr}}_{3}{\mathrm{Sb}}_{5}$
authors: Maria Chatzieleftheriou, Jonas B. Profe, Ying Li, And Roser Valentí
abstract:
Author(s): Maria Chatzieleftheriou, Jonas B. Profe, Ying Li, and Roser Valentí

[MATH] is a newly identified strongly correlated kagome superconductor, characterized by non-Fermi-liquid behavior at elevated temperatures and intertwined charge and spin density wave order below [MATH]. Under e…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 055124] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the electronic correlations and flat bands in the kagome superconductor CsCr3Sb5 under pressure using DFT+DMFT.
motivation: To understand the interplay between electronic correlations, flat bands, and superconductivity in a strongly correlated kagome system.
method: First-principles DFT+DMFT calculations to compute electronic structure and correlation effects as a function of pressure.
result: Pressure tunes the flat bands and correlation strength, affecting the superconducting and density wave orders.
conclusion: The study provides insights into the pressure-dependent electronic properties of CsCr3Sb5, relevant for understanding kagome superconductors.

title: Bistability Of Electron Temperature In Atomically Thin Semiconductors In The Presence Of Exciton Photogeneration
authors: A. M. Shentsev
abstract:
Author(s): A. M. Shentsev

We study the dynamic equilibrium between trions and excitons in monolayers of transition metal dichalcogenides in the presence of resident charge carriers and continuous photogeneration of excitons. We show that heating of the system via Drude absorption of low-frequency radiation leads to bistabili…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 055416] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies bistability of electron temperature in atomically thin semiconductors due to exciton photogeneration and Drude absorption.
motivation: Understanding the dynamic equilibrium between trions and excitons in transition metal dichalcogenides is important for optoelectronic applications.
method: The authors model the system with rate equations and heat balance, considering Drude absorption of low-frequency radiation.
result: They find that heating via Drude absorption leads to bistability in electron temperature.
conclusion: The work provides insights into nonlinear thermal effects in 2D semiconductors but does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics of information processing.

title: Exact Stationary State Of A $d$-dimensional Run-and-tumble Particle In A Harmonic Potential
authors: Mathis Guéneau, Satya N. Majumdar, And Grégory Schehr
abstract:
Author(s): Mathis Guéneau, Satya N. Majumdar, and Grégory Schehr

Understanding how active particles, such as swimming bacteria, move in confined environments remains a challenge. The authors obtain the exact stationary distribution of a run-and-tumble particle trapped by a harmonic potential in one, two, and three dimensions, providing quantitative benchmarks for experiments on confined active matter.

#SoftMatterSpotlight #TechnicalAdvancement


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014144] Published Wed Jul 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper derives the exact stationary distribution of a run-and-tumble particle in a harmonic potential in 1, 2, and 3 dimensions.
motivation: Understanding how active particles move in confined environments is a challenge in soft matter physics.
method: The authors solve the Fokker-Planck equation for the run-and-tumble model in a harmonic trap analytically.
result: Exact stationary probability distributions are obtained for one, two, and three dimensions.
conclusion: The results provide quantitative benchmarks for experiments on confined active matter.

title: Stokes-Einstein-like Scaling Across Fluidized And Caged Transport Regimes In A Driven Complex Plasma
authors: Adrian Scurtu, Dorina Ticoş, Nicoleta Udrea, Maria L. Mitu, Beatrice Paraschiv, And Cătălin M. Ticoş
abstract:
Author(s): Adrian Scurtu, Dorina Ticoş, Nicoleta Udrea, Maria L. Mitu, Beatrice Paraschiv, and Cătălin M. Ticoş

The Stokes-Einstein (SE) relation links microscopic fluctuations to macroscopic dissipation. Whether it survives in driven-dissipative, strongly coupled systems far from global equilibrium remains an open question. Using a macroscopic dust vortex in a radio-frequency complex plasma, we isolate therm…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 015215] Published Wed Jul 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the Stokes-Einstein relation in a driven complex plasma, focusing on transport regimes in a classical system far from equilibrium.
motivation: To test whether the Stokes-Einstein relation, which links microscopic fluctuations to macroscopic dissipation, holds in driven-dissipative strongly coupled systems far from global equilibrium.
method: Experimental observation of a macroscopic dust vortex in a radio-frequency complex plasma, isolating thermal and driven transport regimes.
result: The Stokes-Einstein-like scaling is observed across both fluidized and caged transport regimes.
conclusion: The Stokes-Einstein relation can survive in driven-dissipative systems, providing insight into transport in strongly coupled classical systems.

title: Self-organized Model For The Flicker Noise In Interacting Two-dimensional Electron Gas
authors: Maryam Pirgholi, Morteza Nattagh Najafi, And Vadood Adami
abstract:
Author(s): Maryam Pirgholi, Morteza Nattagh Najafi, and Vadood Adami

We investigate self-organized criticality in a two-dimensional electron gas (2DEG) by introducing a lattice-based model that incorporates electron-electron interactions through the concept of coherence length. Our numerical simulations demonstrate that in the strongly interacting regime, the system …


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014141] Published Tue Jul 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies self-organized criticality and flicker noise in a 2D electron gas with electron-electron interactions, using a lattice model and numerical simulations.
motivation: Understanding the origin of 1/f noise in interacting electron systems is a long-standing problem in condensed matter physics.
method: A lattice-based model incorporating coherence length to capture electron-electron interactions is simulated numerically to study self-organized criticality.
result: In the strongly interacting regime, the system exhibits self-organized criticality and power-law noise spectra characteristic of flicker noise.
conclusion: The model provides a possible mechanism for flicker noise in 2DEG based on self-organized criticality and interactions.

title: Large Earthquakes Follow Highly Unequal Ones
authors: Sudip Sarkar And Soumyajyoti Biswas
abstract:
Author(s): Sudip Sarkar and Soumyajyoti Biswas

It was conjectured for a long time that the tectonic plates are in a self-organized state of criticality and that the Gutenberg-Richter law is a manifestation of that. It was recently shown that for a system near criticality, the inequality of their responses due to external driving would sharply ri…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014143] Published Tue Jul 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies inequality of earthquake magnitudes as a signature of self-organized criticality, using a fiber bundle model.
motivation: To test the conjecture that tectonic plates are in a self-organized critical state and that the Gutenberg-Richter law is a manifestation of it.
method: Analyzes earthquake catalog data and uses a fiber bundle model to show that large earthquakes follow periods of high inequality in magnitude distribution.
result: Finds that large earthquakes are preceded by highly unequal magnitude distributions, supporting the self-organized criticality hypothesis.
conclusion: Inequality measures can serve as early warning signals for large earthquakes.

title: Spectral Statistics And Localization Properties Of A ${\mathrm{C}}_{3}$-symmetric Billiard
authors: Matic Orel And Marko Robnik
abstract:
Author(s): Matic Orel and Marko Robnik

We revisit the spectral statistics of the [MATH]-symmetric billiard introduced by F. Leyvraz et al. [
tldr: This paper studies spectral statistics and localization properties of a C3-symmetric billiard, focusing on GOE and GUE statistics.
motivation: To understand the spectral statistics of quantum billiards with discrete symmetry, which exhibit both GOE and GUE behavior depending on the symmetry block.
method: High-precision numerical computation of eigenvalues and eigenfunctions for the C3-symmetric billiard, analyzing level spacing distributions and localization measures.
result: The billiard shows GOE statistics in the symmetric subspace and GUE statistics in the antisymmetric subspace, with intermediate localization properties.
conclusion: The C3-symmetric billiard provides a clean example of symmetry-induced spectral statistics crossover, relevant to quantum chaos studies.

title: Stability And Interactions Of Hopfions In Confined Chiral Systems: Role Of The Background Phase
authors: Andrey O. Leonov
abstract:
Author(s): Andrey O. Leonov

We present a systematic study of isolated hopfions in confined layers of chiral magnets and cholesteric liquid crystals with strong surface anchoring and a film thickness fixed to one spiral pitch. We focus on the structure, stability, and interactions of hopfions under these conditions. Using numer…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 015416] Published Tue Jul 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies hopfions in confined chiral magnets and cholesteric liquid crystals, focusing on their stability and interactions.
motivation: Hopfions are topological solitons that may have applications in spintronics and liquid crystal devices, but their behavior in confined geometries is not well understood.
method: Numerical simulations are used to model hopfions in thin films with strong surface anchoring and fixed thickness, analyzing their structure and interactions under various background phases.
result: The stability and interaction properties of hopfions depend strongly on the background phase, with certain phases enabling stable hopfion configurations.
conclusion: Controlling the background phase is a key factor for stabilizing hopfions in confined chiral systems, which may guide experimental realizations.

title: Beyond The Arcsine Law: Aging Statistics Of The Occupation Time In Jump Processes
authors: Arthur Plaud And Olivier Bénichou
abstract:
Author(s): Arthur Plaud and Olivier Bénichou

Occupation times quantify how long a stochastic process remains in a region, and their single-time statistics are famously given by the arcsine law for Brownian and Lévy processes. By contrast, two-time occupation statistics—which directly probe temporal correlations and aging—have resisted exact ch…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014137] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies two-time occupation statistics in jump processes, revealing aging behavior beyond the classical arcsine law.
motivation: Understanding temporal correlations and aging in stochastic processes is important for statistical physics, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors derive exact results for two-time occupation probabilities in jump processes using renewal theory and asymptotic analysis.
result: They find that the joint distribution of occupation times exhibits aging, with a non-trivial scaling limit that generalizes the arcsine law.
conclusion: The work provides a complete characterization of two-time occupation statistics, but its relevance to quantum information or thermodynamics is not established.

title: Finite-size Scaling To Resolve Spurious Multifractality In The Two-dimensional Ising Model
authors: S. Jaroszewicz, N. Mendez, Maria P. Beccar-Varela, And Maria Cristina Mariani
abstract:
Author(s): S. Jaroszewicz, N. Mendez, Maria P. Beccar-Varela, and Maria Cristina Mariani

Multifractal detrended fluctuation analysis has emerged as a standard tool for characterizing scale invariance in complex systems, yet its application to discrete spin models is frequently marred by reports of “spurious multifractality” that contradict established theory. In this work, we resolve th…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014139] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper resolves spurious multifractality in the 2D Ising model using finite-size scaling.
motivation: Multifractal detrended fluctuation analysis often yields spurious multifractality in discrete spin models, contradicting theory.
method: The authors apply finite-size scaling to multifractal detrended fluctuation analysis of the 2D Ising model.
result: They show that the apparent multifractality is a finite-size artifact and can be removed by proper scaling.
conclusion: Finite-size scaling is essential to avoid misinterpretation of multifractal analysis in spin systems.

title: Phenomenological Renormalization Group In Neuronal Models Near Criticality
authors: Kaio F. R. Nascimento, Daniel M. Castro, Gustavo G. Cambrainha, And Mauro Copelli
abstract:
Author(s): Kaio F. R. Nascimento, Daniel M. Castro, Gustavo G. Cambrainha, and Mauro Copelli

The phenomenological renormalization group (PRG) has been applied to the study of scale-invariant phenomena in neuronal data, providing evidence for critical phenomena in the brain. However, it remains unclear how reliably these observed signatures indicate genuine critical behavior, as it is not we…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014310] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper applies phenomenological renormalization group to neuronal models to study criticality in the brain.
motivation: To determine whether scale-invariant signatures in neuronal data reliably indicate genuine critical behavior.
method: The authors use phenomenological renormalization group (PRG) analysis on neuronal models near criticality.
result: The paper assesses the reliability of PRG signatures for detecting criticality in neuronal systems.
conclusion: The findings clarify the limitations of PRG in identifying critical behavior in neuronal data.

title: Optimal Navigation In Two-dimensional Flows: Control Theory And Reinforcement Learning
authors: Vladimir Parfenyev
abstract:
Author(s): Vladimir Parfenyev

Zermelo's navigation problem seeks the trajectory of minimal travel time between two points in a fluid flow. We address this problem for an agent—such as a floating drone or active particle—that is advected by a two-dimensional flow, self-propels at a fixed speed smaller than or comparable to the ch…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 015104] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper solves Zermelo's navigation problem for an agent in a two-dimensional flow using control theory and reinforcement learning.
motivation: To find optimal trajectories for agents like drones or active particles advected by fluid flows, which is relevant for navigation in realistic environments.
method: The authors formulate the problem as an optimal control problem and apply reinforcement learning techniques to compute time-optimal paths.
result: They demonstrate that the method efficiently finds optimal routes in various flow fields, outperforming traditional approaches.
conclusion: The work provides a practical framework for navigation in complex flows, but it is not directly related to quantum information, thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Localization-delocalization Transition In Low-dimensional Asymmetric Resetting Random Walks
authors: Reza Sepehrinia
abstract:
Author(s): Reza Sepehrinia

We investigate biased random walks with stochastic resetting to previously visited sites and demonstrate how directional drift fundamentally alters the emergence of localized stationary states. We show that bias acts as a competing mechanism and can weaken or suppress localization. This competition …


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014128] Published Thu Jul 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies biased random walks with stochastic resetting to previously visited sites, showing how directional drift alters localization.
motivation: To understand the interplay between bias and resetting in low-dimensional random walks, which is a classical stochastic process problem.
method: Analytical and numerical analysis of biased random walks with resetting to visited sites, examining stationary state properties.
result: Bias weakens or suppresses localization, acting as a competing mechanism against resetting-induced localization.
conclusion: The competition between bias and resetting leads to a localization-delocalization transition in low-dimensional systems.

title: Universality Of Order Statistics For Brownian Reshuffling
authors: Zdzislaw Burda, Mario Kieburg, And Tomasz Maciocha
abstract:
Author(s): Zdzislaw Burda, Mario Kieburg, and Tomasz Maciocha

In a one-dimensional gas of particles confined by an asymptotically power-law potential, the ordering of the particles changes as they perform Brownian motion. The authors show that the order statistics that describe how the particles are reshuffled are universal and independent of the potential’s exponent, while the timescale of the reshuffling does depend on it.

#UniversalBehavior #AdvancingField


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014130] Published Thu Jul 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies universal order statistics in a one-dimensional gas of Brownian particles confined by a power-law potential.
motivation: Understanding how particle ordering changes over time in a diffusive system is a fundamental statistical mechanics problem.
method: The authors analyze the dynamics of particle positions under Brownian motion and derive order statistics that characterize reshuffling, showing universality with respect to the potential exponent.
result: The order statistics are universal and independent of the potential's exponent, while the reshuffling timescale depends on it.
conclusion: The work provides insight into universal features of ordering in diffusive systems, but it is not directly connected to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Dynamic Effects Of Electric Fields In A Hybrid-coupled Thermosensitive Neuronal Network
authors: Ediline L. F. Nguessap, Antonio C. Roque, And Fernando F. Ferreira
abstract:
Author(s): Ediline L. F. Nguessap, Antonio C. Roque, and Fernando F. Ferreira

The dynamics of thermosensitive FitzHugh-Nagumo neuronal networks under hybrid synaptic coupling and external electric fields is investigated in a ring topology. Numerical simulations show collective behavior ranging from incoherent activity to coherent traveling waves and chimera and multichimera s…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014218] Published Thu Jul 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies collective dynamics in a thermosensitive neuronal network under electric fields, which is unrelated to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: To understand how electric fields affect pattern formation in neuronal networks with hybrid coupling.
method: Numerical simulations of a FitzHugh-Nagumo neuronal network on a ring with thermosensitive properties and hybrid synaptic coupling under external electric fields.
result: Observation of various collective behaviors including incoherent activity, coherent traveling waves, and chimera/multichimera states.
conclusion: Electric fields can induce complex spatiotemporal patterns in thermosensitive neuronal networks, relevant for neuroscience but not for quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Computer Simulations Of The Stark Effect In The Helium-$β$ Complex Of Krypton In Inertial Confinement Fusion Conditions
authors: G. Pérez-Callejo, E. Stambulchik, R. Florido, And M. A. Gigosos
abstract:
Author(s): G. Pérez-Callejo, E. Stambulchik, R. Florido, and M. A. Gigosos

There is an ongoing interest in using spectroscopy in inertial confinement fusion (ICF) experiments, where dopants such as krypton can provide vital information about the temperature and density of the imploding plasma. While the most advanced tools for calculating Stark profiles are computer simula…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 015212] Published Thu Jul 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses computer simulations to study the Stark effect in krypton under inertial confinement fusion conditions, focusing on plasma spectroscopy.
motivation: To improve diagnostic capabilities in inertial confinement fusion experiments by modeling Stark-broadened spectral lines of krypton dopants.
method: Computer simulations of Stark profiles for the helium-beta complex of krypton, accounting for plasma conditions.
result: Simulated Stark profiles that can be used to infer plasma temperature and density from spectroscopic measurements.
conclusion: The simulations provide a tool for diagnosing ICF plasmas, but the work is applied plasma physics without connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Distance Function For Stochastic Matrices
authors: Antony R. Lee, Peter Tiňo, And Iain B. Styles
abstract:
Author(s): Antony R. Lee, Peter Tiňo, and Iain B. Styles

The ability to quantify the similarity of stochastic processes is important in a wide range of areas including communications, simulation, and operational research. Such processes are commonly modeled as Markov Chains and so a natural way to compare their similarity is to compute distances between p…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014125] Published Wed Jul 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a distance function for stochastic matrices based on the Kullback-Leibler divergence rate, applied to Markov chains.
motivation: Quantifying similarity between stochastic processes is important in communications, simulation, and operational research.
method: The authors define a distance metric using the Kullback-Leibler divergence rate between Markov chains and prove its properties.
result: The distance function is shown to be a valid metric and is demonstrated on synthetic and real-world data.
conclusion: The proposed distance provides a principled way to compare stochastic processes modeled as Markov chains.

title: Intermediate Scattering Function Of Brownian Particles In A Tilted Cosine Potential
authors: Regina Rusch And Thomas Franosch
abstract:
Author(s): Regina Rusch and Thomas Franosch

We solve the Fokker-Planck equation for a Brownian particle in a tilted cosine potential and derive the intermediate scattering function (ISF), which captures the full spatiotemporal dynamics of the system. The model consists of a single overdamped Brownian particle in one dimension. We derive a gen…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014127] Published Wed Jul 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper solves the Fokker-Planck equation for a Brownian particle in a tilted cosine potential and derives the intermediate scattering function.
motivation: Understanding the spatiotemporal dynamics of Brownian particles in periodic potentials is important for condensed matter physics and soft matter.
method: The authors solve the Fokker-Planck equation analytically and numerically to obtain the intermediate scattering function.
result: They derive a general expression for the ISF and analyze its behavior for various tilt strengths and damping regimes.
conclusion: The work provides a complete characterization of the dynamics of a Brownian particle in a tilted cosine potential, which can be used to interpret scattering experiments.

title: Floquet Resonances In The Double Kicked Top
authors: Avadhut V. Purohit And Udaysinh T. Bhosale
abstract:
Author(s): Avadhut V. Purohit and Udaysinh T. Bhosale

We study exact quantum resonances in the double kicked top (DKT), a driven spin model that extends the quantum kicked top (QKT) by introducing an additional time-reversal symmetry-breaking kick. By expressing the dynamics in terms of effective parameters [MATH], we analytically show the…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014214] Published Wed Jul 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies exact quantum resonances in a driven spin model called the double kicked top, extending the quantum kicked top with an additional time-reversal symmetry-breaking kick.
motivation: To understand quantum resonance phenomena in driven systems and how additional kicks affect the dynamics.
method: Analytical derivation of effective parameters and exact resonance conditions for the double kicked top model.
result: Exact quantum resonances are identified and characterized analytically.
conclusion: The double kicked top exhibits rich resonance behavior that can be understood through effective parameters.

title: Emergence Of Higher-order Interactions In Systems Of Coupled Kuramoto Oscillators With Time Delay
authors: Narumi Fujii, Keisuke Taga, Riccardo Muolo, Bob Rink, And Hiroya Nakao
abstract:
Author(s): Narumi Fujii, Keisuke Taga, Riccardo Muolo, Bob Rink, and Hiroya Nakao

We show that higher-order interactions naturally emerge from time-delayed pairwise coupling in Kuramoto oscillators. By expanding the delayed pairwise coupling to the second order, we derive a delay-free Kuramoto model possessing both pairwise and three-body interactions. Numerical simulations and s…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014215] Published Wed Jul 15, 2026.
