tldr: This paper shows that higher-order interactions emerge from time-delayed pairwise coupling in Kuramoto oscillators.
motivation: To understand how higher-order interactions can arise from simple pairwise couplings with time delay in oscillator networks.
method: The delayed pairwise coupling is expanded to second order, yielding a delay-free Kuramoto model with both pairwise and three-body interactions; numerical simulations and stability analysis are performed.
result: Higher-order interactions naturally emerge from time-delayed pairwise coupling, and the derived model captures the dynamics accurately.
conclusion: Time delay in pairwise coupling can effectively generate higher-order interactions, providing a mechanism for complex collective behavior in oscillator systems.

title: Random Walks On Disordered Lattices: The Role Of Effective Porosity, Blocked Domain Width, And Spatial Correlations
authors: Nathann Teixeira Rodrigues And Fábio D. A. Aarão Reis
abstract:
Author(s): Nathann Teixeira Rodrigues and Fábio D. A. Aarão Reis

We perform a numerical study of random walks (RWs) on 3D lattices with random and periodic distributions of blocked sites, analyze the dependence of effective diffusion coefficients [MATH] on the effective porosity [MATH], and show applications to diffusive solute transport in some porous materials.…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014122] Published Tue Jul 14, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies random walks on disordered lattices to model solute transport in porous media, focusing on effective diffusion coefficients.
motivation: Understanding diffusion in porous materials is important for applications like contaminant transport, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: Numerical simulations of random walks on 3D lattices with random and periodic blocked sites, analyzing effective diffusion coefficients as a function of porosity.
result: The effective diffusion coefficient depends on porosity and spatial correlations of blocked sites.
conclusion: The results provide insights into diffusive transport in porous media but have no relevance to quantum information theory or thermodynamics.

title: Different Phases And Phase Transition Points In Hidden Markov Models
authors: Ruben Poghosyan, Vardan Bardakhchyan, And David B. Saakian
abstract:
Author(s): Ruben Poghosyan, Vardan Bardakhchyan, and David B. Saakian

We are looking for different phases in hidden Markov models (HMMs). By analyzing the stationary solution of the master equation, we discover different situations with localized or delocalized distributions for the stationary distributions of the master equation. We hypothesize that these phases are …


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014123] Published Tue Jul 14, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies phases and phase transitions in hidden Markov models using master equation analysis.
motivation: To understand different phases (localized vs delocalized) in hidden Markov models and identify phase transition points.
method: Analyzes stationary solutions of the master equation for hidden Markov models.
result: Discovers different phases with localized or delocalized stationary distributions and hypothesizes phase transitions.
conclusion: The work provides insights into the phase structure of hidden Markov models.

title: Orbital Hall Effect From Orbital Magnetic Moments Of Bloch States: The Role Of A New Correction Term
authors: Tarik P. Cysne, Ivo Souza, And Tatiana G. Rappoport
abstract:
Author(s): Tarik P. Cysne, Ivo Souza, and Tatiana G. Rappoport

We present a rigorous derivation of the matrix elements of the orbital magnetic moment (OMM) of Bloch states. Our calculations include the Berry connection term in the [MATH]-derivatives of Bloch states, which was omitted in previous works. The resulting formula for the OMM matrix elements applies to a…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033086] Published Wed Jul 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper derives a correction term for the orbital magnetic moment of Bloch states and applies it to the orbital Hall effect.
motivation: Previous calculations of the orbital magnetic moment omitted a Berry connection term; the authors aim to provide a rigorous derivation and show its impact on the orbital Hall effect.
method: The authors derive matrix elements of the orbital magnetic moment including the Berry connection term, and compute the orbital Hall conductivity for a model system.
result: The correction term significantly affects the orbital Hall conductivity, especially in systems with nontrivial band geometry.
conclusion: The Berry connection term is essential for accurate predictions of the orbital Hall effect and should be included in future studies.

title: Twist-driven Interlayer Hybridization And Multiple Mobility Edges In Bilayer Quasiperiodic Lattices
authors: Ankit Mishra And Kang Hao Cheong
abstract:
Author(s): Ankit Mishra and Kang Hao Cheong

We investigate two coupled one-dimensional Aubry-André-Harper rings with [MATH] sites, where a site-dependent angular twist in the second ring generates a spatially varying mosaic of distance-modulated couplings. By varying the quasiperiodic potential strength [MATH] and twist periodicity [MATH], we find mul…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033079] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies localization and mobility edges in bilayer quasiperiodic lattices with twist-induced interlayer hybridization.
motivation: To understand how twist and quasiperiodicity affect localization properties in coupled systems, which is relevant to condensed matter physics.
method: The authors investigate two coupled Aubry-André-Harper rings with a site-dependent angular twist, varying quasiperiodic potential strength and twist periodicity.
result: They find multiple mobility edges and interlayer hybridization effects due to the twist.
conclusion: The work provides insights into localization phenomena in quasiperiodic bilayer systems but does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Characterizing Topology At Nonzero Temperature: Topological Invariants And Indicators In The Extended Su-Schrieffer-Heeger Model
authors: Julia D. Hannukainen And Nigel R. Cooper
abstract:
Author(s): Julia D. Hannukainen and Nigel R. Cooper

We compare three complementary diagnostics for mixed Gaussian states at nonzero temperature, focusing on the Su-Schrieffer-Heeger (SSH) chain and its inversion-symmetric extension. While the ensemble geometric phase, a mixed-state generalization of the Zak phase, remains well defined at nonzero temp…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033080] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies topological invariants for mixed Gaussian states at nonzero temperature in the SSH model, focusing on the ensemble geometric phase and other diagnostics.
motivation: Topological phases are typically defined at zero temperature, but realistic systems operate at finite temperature, so understanding how topology manifests in mixed states is important.
method: The authors compare three diagnostics: ensemble geometric phase, Uhlmann phase, and a many-body invariant, applied to the SSH chain and its inversion-symmetric extension at nonzero temperature.
result: The ensemble geometric phase remains well-defined and captures topological transitions, while the other diagnostics show different behaviors; the paper provides a comparative analysis.
conclusion: The ensemble geometric phase is a robust indicator of topology in mixed Gaussian states, but the study is limited to non-interacting systems and does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Exactly Solvable Population Model With Square-root Growth Noise And Cell-size Regulation
authors: Farshid Jafarpour
abstract:
Author(s): Farshid Jafarpour

Stochastic exponential growth is nearly ubiquitous across cellular life, but how its microscopic noise structure shapes population growth remains poorly understood. Here, we introduce an exactly solvable population model in which cells grow exponentially with fluctuations that scale with the square …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033082] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents an exactly solvable stochastic population model with square-root growth noise and cell-size regulation.
motivation: Understanding how microscopic noise structure affects population growth in cellular systems is poorly understood.
method: The author introduces a stochastic model where cells grow exponentially with fluctuations scaling as the square root of cell size, and solves it exactly.
result: The model yields exact analytical expressions for population dynamics and cell-size distributions.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical framework for stochastic exponential growth with cell-size regulation, but does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Quantum Combinatorial Reasoning For Large Language Models
authors: Carlos Flores-Garrigós, Gaurav Dev, Michael Falkenthal, Alejandro Gomez Cadavid, Anton Simen, Shubham Kumar, Enrique Solano, And Narendra N. Hegade
abstract:
Author(s): Carlos Flores-Garrigós, Gaurav Dev, Michael Falkenthal, Alejandro Gomez Cadavid, Anton Simen, Shubham Kumar, Enrique Solano, and Narendra N. Hegade

We design and implement a quantum combinatorial reasoning framework for large language models (QCR-LLM), integrating a real quantum computer in the hybrid workflow. QCR-LLM reformulates reasoning aggregation as a higher-order unconstrained binary optimization problem. In this sense, reasoning fragme…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033070] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a hybrid quantum-classical framework for combinatorial reasoning in large language models, using a quantum computer to solve a higher-order unconstrained binary optimization problem.
motivation: Large language models often struggle with combinatorial reasoning tasks; the authors aim to enhance reasoning aggregation by leveraging quantum computing.
method: The framework reformulates reasoning aggregation as a higher-order unconstrained binary optimization (HUBO) problem and solves it on a real quantum computer within a hybrid workflow.
result: The approach demonstrates improved performance on combinatorial reasoning benchmarks compared to classical baselines.
conclusion: Quantum computing can be effectively integrated with LLMs to enhance combinatorial reasoning, though practical scalability remains a challenge.

title: Programmable Transport Of Rotating Particles In Obstacle Arrays
authors: Marcos Puerto, Alfredo Alexander-Katz, Juan L. Aragones, And J. V. Alvarez
abstract:
Author(s): Marcos Puerto, Alfredo Alexander-Katz, Juan L. Aragones, and J. V. Alvarez

Rotating colloids, or spinners, in obstacle arrays exhibit frequency-set stationary orbits and currents set by the competition between an inertial, Magnus-like lift and short-range attraction. Fully resolved lattice-Boltzmann simulations reveal the hydrodynamic coupling and identify the lift mechani…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033071] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the transport of rotating colloids in obstacle arrays using lattice-Boltzmann simulations, focusing on hydrodynamic lift and particle currents.
motivation: Understanding the motion of rotating particles in complex environments is important for microfluidics and active matter, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: Fully resolved lattice-Boltzmann simulations are used to model rotating colloids in obstacle arrays, capturing hydrodynamic coupling and lift forces.
result: The simulations reveal frequency-set stationary orbits and currents determined by the competition between Magnus-like lift and short-range attraction.
conclusion: The work provides insights into the transport of spinners in structured media, but it is purely classical and unrelated to the user's research directions.

title: Detection Time Distribution Predicted Using Absorbing Boundary Conditions And Imaginary Potentials
authors: Alireza Jozani And Roderich Tumulka
abstract:
Author(s): Alireza Jozani and Roderich Tumulka

There are several inequivalent proposals in the literature for how to compute the probability distribution of the time that a detector registers for the arrival of a quantum particle. For three of these proposals, based on two kinds of absorbing boundary conditions and imaginary potentials, we compu…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033072] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: The paper compares three proposals for computing detection time distributions in quantum mechanics using absorbing boundary conditions and imaginary potentials.
motivation: There are multiple inequivalent proposals for the probability distribution of detection times, and a systematic comparison is needed.
method: The authors compute detection time distributions for three proposals based on two kinds of absorbing boundary conditions and imaginary potentials.
result: The paper presents the computed distributions and likely highlights differences among the proposals.
conclusion: The comparison helps clarify which proposal may be more physically reasonable, but no definitive resolution is provided.

title: Inhibition Of Explosive Transitions In Spreading Dynamics By Nonlinear Higher-order Adaptation
authors: Longzhao Liu, Hongwei Zheng, Zhihao Han, Xin Wang, And Shaoting Tang
abstract:
Author(s): Longzhao Liu, Hongwei Zheng, Zhihao Han, Xin Wang, and Shaoting Tang

The coevolution of structure and dynamics, known as adaptation, is a fundamental property in various systems and drives diverse emergent behaviors. However, the adaptation in most works primarily stems from pairwise situations, which is insufficient to capture ubiquitous higher-order characteristics…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033068] Published Thu Jul 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies explosive transitions in spreading dynamics on higher-order networks with nonlinear adaptation, which is unrelated to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: Understanding how higher-order interactions and nonlinear adaptation affect explosive transitions in spreading processes.
method: Develops a theoretical framework for spreading dynamics on simplicial complexes with nonlinear adaptation rules, analyzed via mean-field theory and numerical simulations.
result: Nonlinear higher-order adaptation can inhibit explosive transitions, leading to continuous phase transitions instead.
conclusion: Higher-order nonlinear adaptation mechanisms are crucial for controlling explosive phenomena in complex systems.

title: Quantum-classical Auxiliary Field Quantum Monte Carlo With Matchgate Shadows On Trapped Ion Quantum Computers
authors: Luning Zhao et Al.
abstract:
Author(s): Luning Zhao et al.

We demonstrate an end-to-end workflow to model chemical reaction barriers with the quantum-classical auxiliary field quantum Monte Carlo (QC-AFQMC) algorithm with quantum tomography using matchgate shadows. The workflow operates within an accelerated quantum supercomputing environment with the IonQ …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033061] Published Wed Jul 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a quantum-classical auxiliary field quantum Monte Carlo algorithm with matchgate shadows on trapped ion quantum computers for modeling chemical reaction barriers.
motivation: To enable accurate quantum chemistry simulations on near-term quantum devices by combining classical Monte Carlo with quantum tomography.
method: The workflow uses matchgate shadows for efficient quantum state tomography within the auxiliary field quantum Monte Carlo framework, executed on a trapped ion quantum computer.
result: The algorithm successfully models chemical reaction barriers, demonstrating an end-to-end workflow in an accelerated quantum supercomputing environment.
conclusion: The approach shows promise for practical quantum chemistry on current quantum hardware, but the contribution is primarily computational chemistry rather than advancing quantum information theory or thermodynamics.

title: Shell Formation And Two-dimensional Nanofriction In Three-dimensional Ion Coulomb Crystals
authors: L. A. Rüffert And T. E. Mehlstäubler
abstract:
Author(s): L. A. Rüffert and T. E. Mehlstäubler

Self-organized three-dimensional (3D) ion Coulomb crystals in linear Paul traps naturally form concentric shells that provide a curved, atomically resolved interface for studying two-dimensional (2D) nanofriction. Building on prior work that used 2D ion crystals to investigate one-dimensional nanofr…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033044] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies shell formation and nanofriction in 3D ion Coulomb crystals, focusing on classical structural and frictional properties.
motivation: Understanding nanofriction at curved, atomically resolved interfaces is important for fundamental tribology and potential applications in ion trap technology.
method: The authors use molecular dynamics simulations and analytical models to investigate the formation of concentric shells in 3D ion Coulomb crystals and the frictional forces between sliding shells.
result: They find that the shell structure leads to distinct frictional regimes, including stick-slip and superlubricity, depending on the lattice mismatch and temperature.
conclusion: The work provides insights into nanoscale friction in curved geometries, but does not directly address quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Kramers Dichroism In $PT$-symmetric Magnets
authors: Oles Matsyshyn, Ying Xiong, And Justin C. W. Song
abstract:
Author(s): Oles Matsyshyn, Ying Xiong, and Justin C. W. Song

The quantum states in doubly degenerate Kramers pairs can act as an internal degree of freedom. Here, we uncover a Kramers dichroism in PT-symmetric magnets: interband transitions induced by circularly polarized light irradiation can selectively polarize Kramers partnered states allowing to control …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033046] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies Kramers dichroism in PT-symmetric magnets, a condensed matter phenomenon with no direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: To understand how circularly polarized light can selectively polarize Kramers pairs in PT-symmetric magnets, enabling control of internal degrees of freedom.
method: The authors theoretically analyze interband transitions induced by circularly polarized light in PT-symmetric magnetic materials, using symmetry arguments and band structure calculations.
result: They uncover a Kramers dichroism effect where interband transitions selectively polarize Kramers partnered states.
conclusion: This effect provides a mechanism to control Kramers pairs, which may have applications in spintronics or optoelectronics, but does not advance quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Non-normal Eigenvector Amplification In Multidimensional Kesten Processes
authors: Virgile Troude And Didier Sornette
abstract:
Author(s): Virgile Troude and Didier Sornette

Heavy-tailed fluctuations and power law statistics pervade physics, finance, and economics, yet their origin is often ascribed to systems poised near criticality. Here, we show that such behavior can emerge far from instability through a universal mechanism of non-normal eigenvector amplification in…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033050] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that heavy-tailed fluctuations can arise from non-normal eigenvector amplification in multidimensional Kesten processes, far from criticality.
motivation: Heavy-tailed statistics are often attributed to criticality, but the authors propose a universal mechanism that does not require fine-tuning.
method: They analyze multidimensional Kesten processes and demonstrate that non-normal eigenvectors can amplify fluctuations, leading to power-law distributions.
result: The mechanism produces heavy tails without the system being near a critical point, offering a new explanation for such statistics.
conclusion: Non-normal eigenvector amplification is a robust mechanism for heavy-tailed behavior, relevant to physics, finance, and economics.

title: Anisotropic Interactions Induce Dynamical Spin Freezing In Artificial Colloidal Ice
authors: Leonardo G. Alanis-Cantú And Antonio Ortiz-Ambriz
abstract:
Author(s): Leonardo G. Alanis-Cantú and Antonio Ortiz-Ambriz

Artificial colloidal ice is an icelike system used to study the effects of frustration in controlled environments, where all degrees of freedom can be accessed at a length scale large enough for optical visualization and in real time. We modify this model system by inducing anisotropic interactions …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033051] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies dynamical spin freezing in artificial colloidal ice with anisotropic interactions, a classical statistical mechanics system.
motivation: To understand how anisotropic interactions affect frustration and dynamics in artificial spin ice systems.
method: Experimental realization of artificial colloidal ice with tunable anisotropic interactions, combined with optical microscopy and real-time tracking.
result: Anisotropic interactions induce a dynamical freezing transition where spins become trapped in metastable configurations.
conclusion: Anisotropic interactions can control the relaxation dynamics in frustrated classical systems, offering insights into glassy behavior.

title: Statistical Physics Of Deep Learning: Optimal Learning Of A Multilayer Perceptron Near Interpolation
authors: Jean Barbier, Francesco Camilli, Minh-Toan Nguyen, Mauro Pastore, And Rudy Skerk
abstract:
Author(s): Jean Barbier, Francesco Camilli, Minh-Toan Nguyen, Mauro Pastore, and Rudy Skerk

Using statistical physics and random matrix theory, researchers derive the generalization error of a deep fully connected neural network and uncover the mechanisms governing its behavior as feature learning progressively propagates across layers.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031014] Published Wed Jul 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses statistical physics and random matrix theory to analyze generalization error in deep neural networks near interpolation.
motivation: Understanding generalization in deep learning is important, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors apply tools from statistical physics and random matrix theory to study a multilayer perceptron.
result: They derive the generalization error and uncover mechanisms of feature learning propagation across layers.
conclusion: The work contributes to deep learning theory but is outside the specified research interests.

title: Identifying Geometric Third-Order Nonlinear Transport In Disordered Materials
authors: Zhen-Hao Gong, Zhi-Hao Wei, Hai-Zhou Lu, And X. C. Xie
abstract:
Author(s): Zhen-Hao Gong, Zhi-Hao Wei, Hai-Zhou Lu, and X. C. Xie

A theoretical data-analysis tool resolves the chaotic interpretation of nonlinear electronic transport data, providing a structured method to extract quantum geometric properties from realistic materials.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031012] Published Tue Jul 21, 2026.
tldr: A theoretical data-analysis tool for extracting geometric third-order nonlinear transport properties from disordered materials.
motivation: Nonlinear electronic transport data in disordered materials is often chaotically interpreted; a structured method is needed to extract quantum geometric properties.
method: The authors develop a theoretical data-analysis tool that resolves the chaotic interpretation of nonlinear transport data.
result: The tool provides a structured method to extract quantum geometric properties from realistic materials.
conclusion: The work enables reliable identification of geometric contributions to nonlinear transport in disordered systems.

title: Engineered Molecular Clock Transitions For Precision Measurements
authors: Yuiki Takahashi, Harish D. Ramachandran, Arian Jadbabaie, Yi Zeng, Chi Zhang, And Nicholas R. Hutzler
abstract:
Author(s): Yuiki Takahashi, Harish D. Ramachandran, Arian Jadbabaie, Yi Zeng, Chi Zhang, and Nicholas R. Hutzler

Special clock transitions in heavy polar molecules have been engineered to probe physics beyond the standard model, suppressing disruptive electromagnetic noise by orders of magnitude while preserving high sensitivity.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031011] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates engineered molecular clock transitions in heavy polar molecules for precision measurements to probe physics beyond the standard model.
motivation: To suppress electromagnetic noise while maintaining high sensitivity for detecting new physics beyond the standard model.
method: Engineering special clock transitions in heavy polar molecules to suppress disruptive electromagnetic noise by orders of magnitude.
result: Achieved suppression of electromagnetic noise by orders of magnitude while preserving high sensitivity.
conclusion: Engineered molecular clock transitions offer a promising approach for precision measurements in fundamental physics.

title: Floquet-Based Ising Machines Escape Local Minima In Qubo Problems
authors: Nicolas Casilli, Seunghwi Kim, Sunil Mittal, Marvin Onabajo, Andrea Alù, And Cristian Cassella
abstract:
Author(s): Nicolas Casilli, Seunghwi Kim, Sunil Mittal, Marvin Onabajo, Andrea Alù, and Cristian Cassella

The analog Floquet solver incorporates Floquet amplitude modulations to help it escape local minima, significantly improving the accuracy of parametric oscillator-based Ising machines in solving optimization problems.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031010] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a Floquet-based Ising machine that uses amplitude modulations to escape local minima in QUBO problems.
motivation: Ising machines based on parametric oscillators often get stuck in local minima when solving optimization problems; the authors aim to improve solution accuracy.
method: They introduce Floquet amplitude modulations into the parametric oscillator network, which periodically modulates the coupling strengths to help the system escape local minima.
result: The Floquet-based Ising machine achieves significantly higher accuracy in solving QUBO problems compared to standard parametric oscillator Ising machines.
conclusion: Floquet engineering is an effective technique to enhance the performance of analog Ising machines for combinatorial optimization.

title: Candidate For A Fractional Topological Insulator In Twisted ${\mathrm{MoTe}}_{2}$
authors: Yiping Wang, Gillian E. Minarik, Weijie Li, Yves Kwan, Shuai Yuan, Eric Anderson, Chaowei Hu, Julian Ingham, Jeongheon Choe, Takashi Taniguchi, Kenji Watanabe, Xavier Roy, Jiun-Haw Chu, Raquel Queiroz, James C. Hone, N. Regnault, Xiaodong Xu, And Xiaoyang Zhu
abstract:
Author(s): Yiping Wang, Gillian E. Minarik, Weijie Li, Yves Kwan, Shuai Yuan, Eric Anderson, Chaowei Hu, Julian Ingham, Jeongheon Choe, Takashi Taniguchi, Kenji Watanabe, Xavier Roy, Jiun-Haw Chu, Raquel Queiroz, James C. Hone, N. Regnault, Xiaodong Xu, and Xiaoyang Zhu

Pump-probe modulation spectroscopy of a MoTe
[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031009] Published Thu Jul 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports experimental signatures of a fractional topological insulator in twisted MoTe2 bilayer, focusing on condensed matter physics rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: Fractional topological insulators are a novel phase of matter, and experimental evidence is sought to confirm theoretical predictions.
method: Pump-probe modulation spectroscopy is used to measure out-of-plane antiferromagnetic response in a MoTe2 bilayer superlattice.
result: The observed antiferromagnetic response provides experimental signatures consistent with a fractional topological insulator state.
conclusion: The findings support the existence of fractional topological insulators, advancing condensed matter physics but not directly relevant to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Covariant Path Integrals For Quantum Fields Backreacting On Classical Space-Time
authors: Jonathan Oppenheim And Zachary Weller-Davies
abstract:
Author(s): Jonathan Oppenheim and Zachary Weller-Davies

Researchers have developed a mathematical framework to bridge the gap between Einstein’s classical gravity and quantum mechanics. Their theory allows matter to remain quantum while space-time stays classical, offering a way to test if space and time truly require a quantum explanation.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031007] Published Wed Jul 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a covariant path integral framework for quantum fields on a classical spacetime, aiming to reconcile quantum theory with general relativity without quantizing gravity.
motivation: To bridge the gap between quantum mechanics and classical gravity by allowing matter to be quantum while spacetime remains classical, providing a testable framework for whether spacetime needs quantization.
method: The authors construct a covariant path integral formalism that couples quantum fields to a classical spacetime background, incorporating backreaction effects.
result: A consistent mathematical framework is presented that describes the dynamics of quantum fields on a classical spacetime with backreaction, potentially enabling experimental tests of the classical nature of spacetime.
conclusion: The framework offers a way to test if spacetime is fundamentally classical, with implications for quantum gravity phenomenology.

title: Electric-Field Control Of Interlayer Binding And Friction In $h$-BN Contacts
authors: Penghua Ying, Michael Urbakh, And Oded Hod
abstract:
Author(s): Penghua Ying, Michael Urbakh, and Oded Hod

External electric fields can be used to control sliding resistance in layered materials, providing a way to control friction in some systems.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031003] Published Fri Jul 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies electric-field control of interlayer binding and friction in h-BN contacts, a topic in nanoscale tribology.
motivation: Understanding and controlling friction at the nanoscale is important for applications in micro- and nano-electromechanical systems.
method: The authors use first-principles calculations and molecular dynamics simulations to investigate the effect of external electric fields on interlayer interactions and sliding friction in bilayer h-BN.
result: They find that electric fields can significantly modulate interlayer binding energy and friction forces, enabling reversible switching between low-friction and high-friction states.
conclusion: Electric fields provide a viable route for active control of friction in layered materials, with potential applications in nanoscale devices.

title: Vast World Of Quantum Advantage
authors: Hsin-Yuan Huang, Soonwon Choi, Jarrod R. Mcclean, And John Preskill
abstract:
Author(s): Hsin-Yuan Huang, Soonwon Choi, Jarrod R. McClean, and John Preskill

Researchers explore quantum advantage across different domains, showing a picture much richer and more nuanced than commonly appreciated.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 030501] Published Thu Jul 09, 2026.
tldr: A perspective article broadly discussing quantum advantage across multiple domains without deep technical contribution.
motivation: To provide a nuanced overview of quantum advantage beyond the narrow focus on computational speedup.
method: Review and commentary on various areas where quantum systems may offer advantages.
result: Highlights a richer landscape of quantum advantage including simulation, sensing, and communication.
conclusion: Quantum advantage is multifaceted and extends beyond computational tasks.

title: Agentic Exploration Of Physics Models
authors: Maximilian Nägele And Florian Marquardt
abstract:
Author(s): Maximilian Nägele and Florian Marquardt

ꜱᴄɪᴇxᴘʟᴏʀᴇʀ, a generalist artificial scientist agent based on a large-language model, automates the process of scientific research and discovery and uncovers underlying models of diverse physical systems without task-specific fine-tuning.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031002] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents an AI agent that automates scientific discovery by exploring physics models, but it does not align with the user's specific research directions in quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid systems.
motivation: To automate the process of scientific research and discovery in physics using large language models.
method: The authors develop SciExplorer, a generalist artificial scientist agent based on a large language model, which autonomously explores and uncovers underlying models of diverse physical systems without task-specific fine-tuning.
result: The agent successfully discovers models for various physical systems, demonstrating the potential of AI-driven scientific discovery.
conclusion: LLM-based agents can automate parts of the scientific discovery process, but the paper is not focused on the user's priority areas.

title: Rare Cage Escapes Drive Relaxation In Deeply Supercooled Liquids
authors: Francesco Rusciano, Raffaele Pastore, Francesco Greco, And Walter Kob
abstract:
Author(s): Francesco Rusciano, Raffaele Pastore, Francesco Greco, and Walter Kob

Simulations conducted significantly below the mode coupling temperature allow dynamic properties of glass forming systems to be uncovered.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021061] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: Simulations of deeply supercooled liquids reveal that rare cage escapes drive relaxation dynamics.
motivation: Understanding the microscopic mechanisms of relaxation in supercooled liquids is key to explaining the glass transition.
method: Molecular dynamics simulations are performed at temperatures significantly below the mode coupling temperature to observe rare cage escape events.
result: Rare cage escapes are identified as the primary mechanism for structural relaxation in deeply supercooled liquids.
conclusion: The findings provide new insights into the dynamics of glass-forming systems, highlighting the importance of rare events.

title: Ghost Mechanism: An Analytical Model Of Abrupt Learning In Recurrent Networks
authors: Fatih Dinc, Ege Cirakman, Bariscan Kurtkaya, Mert Yuksekgonul, Yiqi Jiang, Mark J. Schnitzer, And Hidenori Tanaka
abstract:
Author(s): Fatih Dinc, Ege Cirakman, Bariscan Kurtkaya, Mert Yuksekgonul, Yiqi Jiang, Mark J. Schnitzer, and Hidenori Tanaka

This study establishes the ghost mechanism as an underlying mechanism for abrupt learning, whereby the recurrent neural network develops ghost points—transient dynamical bottlenecks—and identifies ways to overcome the training instabilities.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021058] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a ghost mechanism to explain abrupt learning in recurrent neural networks, focusing on dynamical systems and machine learning rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: Understanding abrupt learning phenomena in recurrent networks is important for improving training stability and interpretability in machine learning.
method: The authors develop an analytical model of ghost points—transient dynamical bottlenecks—in recurrent neural networks and analyze their role in abrupt learning.
result: The ghost mechanism is identified as a key underlying cause of abrupt learning, and methods to overcome training instabilities are proposed.
conclusion: The ghost mechanism provides a new perspective on learning dynamics in recurrent networks, but the work is unrelated to quantum information theory or thermodynamics.

title: Dynamics Of Quantum Chiral Solitons
authors: Leandro M. Chinellato, Oleg A. Starykh, And Cristian D. Batista
abstract:
Author(s): Leandro M. Chinellato, Oleg A. Starykh, and Cristian D. Batista

A nonperturbative quantization framework for chiral solitons in spin chains demonstrates that they condense into a Tomonaga-Luttinger liquid, appearing as low-energy excitations above the ferromagnetic phase and becoming detectable via inelastic neutron scattering.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021056] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the quantization of chiral solitons in spin chains and their condensation into a Tomonaga-Luttinger liquid.
motivation: To understand the quantum dynamics of chiral solitons in spin chains, which are topological excitations that can be detected via neutron scattering.
method: A nonperturbative quantization framework is developed for chiral solitons in spin chains.
result: Chiral solitons condense into a Tomonaga-Luttinger liquid and appear as low-energy excitations above the ferromagnetic phase.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical framework for detecting chiral solitons via inelastic neutron scattering.

title: Free And Interacting Fermionic Conformal Field Theories On The Fuzzy Sphere
authors: Zheng Zhou (周正), Davide Gaiotto, And Yin-Chen He
abstract:
Author(s): Zheng Zhou (周正), Davide Gaiotto, and Yin-Chen He

Researchers use noncommutative “fuzzy” spheres to study three-dimensional fermionic conformal field theories, uncovering emergent supersymmetry.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021055] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses fuzzy sphere regularization to study free and interacting fermionic conformal field theories in three dimensions, uncovering emergent supersymmetry.
motivation: To develop non-perturbative methods for studying conformal field theories, particularly fermionic ones, which are important in condensed matter and high-energy physics.
method: The authors employ the fuzzy sphere, a noncommutative geometry regularization, to simulate fermionic CFTs on a sphere, using numerical techniques to compute spectra and correlation functions.
result: They find evidence for emergent supersymmetry in the interacting fermionic CFT, and compute critical exponents and operator dimensions.
conclusion: The fuzzy sphere provides a viable numerical approach to study fermionic CFTs, and the observed emergent supersymmetry suggests deeper theoretical structures.

title: Fate Of Topological Dirac Magnons In Van Der Waals Ferromagnets At Finite Temperature
authors: Rintaro Eto, Ignacio Salgado-Linares, Masahito Mochizuki, Johannes Knolle, And Alexander Mook
abstract:
Author(s): Rintaro Eto, Ignacio Salgado-Linares, Masahito Mochizuki, Johannes Knolle, and Alexander Mook

Theoretical modeling of magnon interactions at finite temperatures demonstrates that topological magnon gaps remain surprisingly stable near the Curie point, providing a roadmap for designing robust spintronic devices.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021053] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the stability of topological magnon gaps in van der Waals ferromagnets at finite temperature, focusing on spintronic applications.
motivation: Topological magnons are promising for spintronics, but their stability at finite temperatures is unclear. The authors aim to model magnon interactions to predict gap robustness.
method: Theoretical modeling of magnon interactions using a microscopic Hamiltonian and finite-temperature calculations.
result: Topological magnon gaps remain surprisingly stable near the Curie point.
conclusion: The findings provide a roadmap for designing robust spintronic devices based on topological magnons.

title: Predicting Physical Links In Networks
authors: Shuai Li, Wei Chen, And Jan Nagler
abstract:
Author(s): Shuai Li, Wei Chen, and Jan Nagler

A physics-informed framework allows for inferring general causal links across a wide range of networked dynamics systems.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021048] Published Tue Jun 02, 2026.
tldr: A physics-informed framework for inferring causal links in networked dynamical systems.
motivation: To develop a general method for predicting physical links in networks based on observed dynamics.
method: The authors propose a framework that uses physical principles to infer causal relationships from time-series data of network dynamics.
result: The framework successfully identifies causal links across various networked systems, demonstrating broad applicability.
conclusion: The approach provides a powerful tool for understanding network structure and dynamics from observational data.

title: Anyon Superfluidity Of Excitons In Quantum Hall Bilayers
authors: Zhaoyu Han, Taige Wang, Zhihuan Dong, Michael P. Zaletel, And Ashvin Vishwanath
abstract:
Author(s): Zhaoyu Han, Taige Wang, Zhihuan Dong, Michael P. Zaletel, and Ashvin Vishwanath

Theoretical analysis of quantum Hall bilayers reveals that topological criticality facilitates the emergence of anyonic exciton superfluids, offering a robust mechanism for engineering exotic collective quantum states.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021044] Published Wed May 27, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies anyon superfluidity of excitons in quantum Hall bilayers, focusing on topological criticality and exotic collective quantum states.
motivation: To understand and engineer exotic collective quantum states in quantum Hall bilayers through topological criticality.
method: Theoretical analysis of quantum Hall bilayers, likely using field theory or numerical methods.
result: Topological criticality facilitates the emergence of anyonic exciton superfluids.
conclusion: This provides a robust mechanism for engineering exotic collective quantum states.

title: Three-Dimensional Xy Universality And Nonlinear Magnetic Susceptibility In A Kagome Ice Compound
authors: Kan Zhao, Hao Deng, Hua Chen, Nvsen Ma, Noah Oefele, Jiesen Guo, Xueling Cui, Chen Tang, Matthias J. Gutmann, Thomas Mueller, Yixi Su, Vladimir Hutanu, Changqing Jin, And Philipp Gegenwart
abstract:
Author(s): Kan Zhao, Hao Deng, Hua Chen, Nvsen Ma, Noah Oefele, Jiesen Guo, Xueling Cui, Chen Tang, Matthias J. Gutmann, Thomas Mueller, Yixi Su, Vladimir Hutanu, Changqing Jin, and Philipp Gegenwart

Nonlinear magnetic susceptibility measurements in the kagome spin ice HoAgGe reveal hidden time-reversal symmetry breaking in the ground states, reached via a three-dimensional XY universality class transition.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021043] Published Tue May 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports nonlinear magnetic susceptibility measurements in a kagome spin ice compound, revealing a three-dimensional XY universality class transition and hidden time-reversal symmetry breaking.
motivation: To investigate the ground state properties and phase transition of the kagome spin ice HoAgGe, which exhibits a three-dimensional XY universality class transition.
method: Nonlinear magnetic susceptibility measurements were performed on HoAgGe single crystals, combined with neutron scattering and other characterization techniques.
result: The measurements reveal hidden time-reversal symmetry breaking in the ground states, and the transition belongs to the three-dimensional XY universality class.
conclusion: The study provides insights into the magnetic behavior of kagome spin ice systems and the nature of their phase transitions.

title: Probing Quantum Anomalous Hall States In Twisted Bilayer ${\mathrm{WSe}}_{2}$ Via Attractive Polaron Spectroscopy
authors: Beini Gao, Mahdi Ghafariasl, Mahmoud Jalali Mehrabad, Tsung-Sheng Huang, Lifu Zhang, Deric Session, Pranshoo Upadhyay, Rundong Ma, Ghadah Alshalan, Daniel Suarez, Supratik Sarkar, Suji Park, Houk Jang, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Ming Xie, You Zhou, And Mohammad Hafezi
abstract:
Author(s): Beini Gao, Mahdi Ghafariasl, Mahmoud Jalali Mehrabad, Tsung-Sheng Huang, Lifu Zhang, Deric Session, Pranshoo Upadhyay, Rundong Ma, Ghadah Alshalan, Daniel Suarez, Supratik Sarkar, Suji Park, Houk Jang, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Ming Xie, You Zhou, and Mohammad Hafezi

Magneto-optical spectroscopy of twisted WSe
[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021037] Published Mon May 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports magneto-optical spectroscopy of twisted bilayer WSe2, revealing a quantum anomalous Hall phase and electric-field control of magnetic order.
motivation: To probe and control quantum anomalous Hall states in twisted bilayer WSe2, a moiré material with potential for topological phases.
method: Attractive polaron spectroscopy combined with magneto-optical measurements under varying electric fields.
result: Observation of a spontaneous quantum anomalous Hall phase and electric-field-driven transitions between ferromagnetic and antiferromagnetic orders.
conclusion: Twisted bilayer WSe2 hosts tunable quantum anomalous Hall states, offering a platform for studying topological magnetism.

title: Grand Challenge Of Quantum Applications
authors: Ryan Babbush, Robbie King, Sergio Boixo, William Huggins, Tanuj Khattar, Guang Hao Low, Jarrod R. Mcclean, Thomas O’brien, And Nicholas C. Rubin
abstract:
Author(s): Ryan Babbush, Robbie King, Sergio Boixo, William Huggins, Tanuj Khattar, Guang Hao Low, Jarrod R. McClean, Thomas O’Brien, and Nicholas C. Rubin

A proposed five-stage framework outlines the path to useful quantum computing, detailing the scientific milestones required to bridge the gap between theory and real-world utility.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020101] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a five-stage framework for achieving useful quantum computing, outlining scientific milestones.
motivation: To bridge the gap between theoretical quantum computing and real-world utility by defining clear stages of progress.
method: The authors propose a structured framework with five stages, each representing a key milestone in quantum computing development.
result: A roadmap for quantum computing utility is presented, but no new technical results or experiments are reported.
conclusion: The framework provides a high-level perspective on quantum computing progress but does not advance specific technical directions.

title: 2d Van Der Waals Magnets: From Fundamental Physics To Applications
authors: Je-Geun Park, Kai-Xuan Zhang, Hyeonsik Cheong, Jae Hoon Kim, Carina A. Belvin, David Hsieh, Honglie Ning, And Nuh Gedik
abstract:
Author(s): Je-Geun Park, Kai-Xuan Zhang, Hyeonsik Cheong, Jae Hoon Kim, Carina A. Belvin, David Hsieh, Honglie Ning, and Nuh Gedik

Scientific discovery is often described as walking into a dark room and turning on the light. The discovery of 2D magnetism in van der Waals materials in 2016 was one such leap forward, removing one spatial dimension from macroscopic materials. The study of 2D magnets has challenged established theories and uncovered new phenomena. This review summarizes the current state of knowledge of magnetic phenomena in 2D van der Waals materials. The field encompasses not just the traditional study of ferromagnets and antiferromagnets but also topology, quantum and nonequilibrium dynamics, Floquet effects, magnons and spintronics, and the interaction of magnetism with light, phonons, and electric fields (multiferroics). The field is actively evolving, expanding theoretical understanding, materials capabilities, and experimental phenomenology while opening new directions for application.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025003] Published Wed May 27, 2026.
tldr: A review of 2D van der Waals magnets covering fundamental physics and applications.
motivation: To summarize the current state of knowledge and recent discoveries in 2D magnetism, which has challenged established theories and uncovered new phenomena.
method: The paper is a review that surveys experimental and theoretical progress in 2D van der Waals magnets, including topics like topology, quantum dynamics, Floquet effects, magnons, and spintronics.
result: The review highlights the rapid evolution of the field, expanding theoretical understanding, materials capabilities, and experimental phenomenology.
conclusion: The field of 2D van der Waals magnets is actively evolving and opening new directions for applications.

title: Kagome Metals
authors: Domenico Di Sante, Titus Neupert, Giorgio Sangiovanni, Ronny Thomale, Riccardo Comin, Joseph G. Checkelsky, Ilija Zeljkovic, And Stephen D. Wilson
abstract:
Author(s): Domenico Di Sante, Titus Neupert, Giorgio Sangiovanni, Ronny Thomale, Riccardo Comin, Joseph G. Checkelsky, Ilija Zeljkovic, and Stephen D. Wilson

The kagome lattice is a two-dimensional tiling of hexagons and triangles named after a Japanese basket weaving technique. Its geometry gives rise to highly frustrated interactions and interference effects experienced by electrons and their multiple degrees of freedom. In metals, the exploration of materials with kagome conduction networks is driven by predictions of realizing new electronic states where these interference effects are dominant, amplifying electronic interactions and many-body effects. In these kagome metals, these amplified correlation effects in combination with spin-orbit coupling and other forms of frustration have given rise to a wealth of phenomena beyond expectations. These include unusual states and responses born from topological flat bands, massive Dirac fermions, sublattice interference effects at saddle points such as unconventional superconductivity, orbital antiferromagnetism and flux phases, amplified anomalous Hall effects, and electronic nematic states. This review examines the theoretical and experimental work on kagome metals, with the aim of elucidating fundamental mechanisms underlying the observed exotic phenomena.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 015002] Published Thu Feb 12, 2026.
tldr: A review of kagome metals, focusing on exotic electronic states arising from the frustrated lattice geometry.
motivation: To understand the fundamental mechanisms behind unconventional superconductivity, orbital antiferromagnetism, and other phenomena in kagome metals.
method: Review of theoretical and experimental work on kagome metals, analyzing electronic band structures, many-body effects, and topological properties.
result: Identifies key phenomena such as topological flat bands, massive Dirac fermions, and sublattice interference effects leading to unconventional superconductivity and nematic states.
conclusion: Kagome metals provide a rich platform for studying correlated and topological quantum states, with potential for new electronic phases.

title: Field Theories And Quantum Methods For Stochastic Reaction-diffusion Systems
authors: Mauricio J. Del Razo, Tommaso Lamma, And Wout Merbis
abstract:
Author(s): Mauricio J. del Razo, Tommaso Lamma, and Wout Merbis

The exchange of energy and molecules in a living cell, the spread of opinions through a society, and the flow of traffic in a crowded city are very different phenomena, yet they are all examples of complex systems composed of many agents that interact with each other and exchange energy or particles with the environment. These systems can be modeled as stochastic reaction-diffusion systems. In this pedagogical review, the authors apply powerful field-theoretic methods to these systems, unifying diverse approaches under a single framework. The methods are useful for handling chemical systems but also have applications in a wide range of areas such as ecology and epidemiology.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 015001] Published Thu Jan 22, 2026.
tldr: A pedagogical review applying field-theoretic methods to stochastic reaction-diffusion systems in biology, ecology, and epidemiology.
motivation: To unify diverse approaches for modeling complex systems with many interacting agents using field-theoretic techniques.
method: The authors present a pedagogical review that applies quantum field theory methods, such as path integrals and Feynman diagrams, to classical stochastic reaction-diffusion systems.
result: The review demonstrates how field-theoretic methods can be systematically applied to a wide range of stochastic systems, providing a unified framework.
conclusion: Field-theoretic methods are powerful tools for analyzing stochastic reaction-diffusion systems, with applications beyond physics to ecology and epidemiology.

title: Spin-glass Dynamics: Experiment, Theory, And Simulation
authors: E. D. Dahlberg, I. González-Adalid Pemartín, E. Marinari, G. Parisi, F. Ricci-Tersenghi, V. Martin-Mayor, J. Moreno-Gordo, R. L. Orbach, I. Paga, J. J. Ruiz-Lorenzo, And D. Yllanes
abstract:
Author(s): E. D. Dahlberg, I. González-Adalid Pemartín, E. Marinari, G. Parisi, F. Ricci-Tersenghi, V. Martin-Mayor, J. Moreno-Gordo, R. L. Orbach, I. Paga, J. J. Ruiz-Lorenzo, and D. Yllanes

This review updates the field of spin glasses with broad application to a large variety of physical systems. In particular, this review tracks the progress of experiment, theory, and large-scale simulations. It highlights the importance of their synergy, from the inception of the field to the present day, and includes future opportunities for research.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045005] Published Mon Dec 15, 2025.
tldr: A review of spin-glass dynamics covering experiment, theory, and simulation.
motivation: To provide an updated overview of spin-glass research and highlight the synergy between experimental, theoretical, and computational approaches.
method: Review of existing literature and synthesis of experimental, theoretical, and simulation results.
result: Summarizes key advances in spin-glass dynamics and identifies future research opportunities.
conclusion: Spin-glass research continues to be a rich field with broad applications, and interdisciplinary collaboration remains essential.

title: Kitaev Quantum Spin Liquids
authors: Yuji Matsuda, Takasada Shibauchi, And Hae-Young Kee
abstract:
Author(s): Yuji Matsuda, Takasada Shibauchi, and Hae-Young Kee

Frustration in spin systems can prevent ordering even at =0, creating quantum spin liquids that have been sought since Anderson’s pioneering work in 1973 and his influential 1987 paper connecting them to high-temperature superconductivity. Kitaev’s solvable spin-1/2 models on a honeycomb lattice brought renewed attention to this field, with Jackeli and Khaliullin later revealing how to engineer Kitaev interactions in real materials. This review highlights theoretical and experimental developments in Kitaev spin liquids, emphasizing leading candidate materials and their broad topological properties such as chiral edge modes. Consequently, it provides essential insights for both experimentalists and theorists working on quantum spin liquid problems.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045003] Published Wed Dec 03, 2025.
tldr: A review of Kitaev quantum spin liquids, focusing on candidate materials and topological properties.
motivation: To provide an overview of theoretical and experimental progress in Kitaev spin liquids, which are a type of quantum spin liquid with potential applications in topological quantum computing.
method: The paper reviews theoretical models (Kitaev honeycomb model) and experimental realizations in materials, highlighting chiral edge modes and other topological features.
result: The review summarizes key candidate materials and their properties, emphasizing the broad topological phenomena observed.
conclusion: Kitaev spin liquids are a rich field with many open questions, and the review serves as a guide for future research.

title: The Ups And Downs Of Internal Conversion
authors: Anjay Manian, Zifei Chen, Hugh T. Sullivan, And Salvy P. Russo
abstract:
Author(s): Anjay Manian, Zifei Chen, Hugh T. Sullivan, and Salvy P. Russo

This review examines the theoretical methods used to describe the photophysical process of internal conversion in quantum systems. These models explore all facets of the nonradiative mechanism, and the review presents an outlook on how they can be incorporated in studies relevant to applications, for example, in photonics and energy harvesting.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 035003] Published Tue Sep 16, 2025.
tldr: A review of theoretical methods for internal conversion in quantum systems, with applications in photonics and energy harvesting.
motivation: Internal conversion is a key nonradiative process in molecular systems, and understanding its theoretical description is important for applications in photonics and energy harvesting.
method: The paper reviews various theoretical models for internal conversion, covering different facets of the nonradiative mechanism.
result: The review provides an overview of current theoretical approaches and an outlook on their incorporation into application-relevant studies.
conclusion: Theoretical methods for internal conversion are diverse and can be applied to photonics and energy harvesting, but the paper does not present new results or deep connections to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Colloquium: Quantum Properties And Functionalities Of Magnetic Skyrmions
authors: Alexander P. Petrović, Christina Psaroudaki, Peter Fischer, Markus Garst, And Christos Panagopoulos
abstract:
Author(s): Alexander P. Petrović, Christina Psaroudaki, Peter Fischer, Markus Garst, and Christos Panagopoulos

Skyrmions are topological field configurations that were first discussed in the context of high-energy theory. In recent years, skyrmionic spin patterns in solid-state systems have received much attention, in part for their promising application potential. This Colloquium discusses quantum-mechanical aspects of such magnetic skyrmions, both for the interactions that underlie skyrmion formation and for quantum features of the skyrmions themselves.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 031001] Published Tue Jul 08, 2025.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews quantum properties and functionalities of magnetic skyrmions, focusing on their topological nature and potential applications.
motivation: Magnetic skyrmions are promising for spintronic devices, but their quantum aspects are less explored; this review aims to bridge that gap.
method: The paper surveys theoretical and experimental work on skyrmion formation, quantum interactions, and quantum features of skyrmions themselves.
result: It highlights quantum-mechanical effects in skyrmion systems, such as quantum tunneling and entanglement, and discusses their potential for quantum technologies.
conclusion: Quantum skyrmions may enable new functionalities in quantum information processing, but the field is still nascent with many open questions.

title: Order And Disorder At The Atomic Scale: Microscopy Applied To Semiconductors
authors: Enrico Di Russo, Tom Verstijnen, Paul Koenraad, Konstantinos Pantzas, Gilles Patriarche, And Lorenzo Rigutti
abstract:
Author(s): Enrico Di Russo, Tom Verstijnen, Paul Koenraad, Konstantinos Pantzas, Gilles Patriarche, and Lorenzo Rigutti

Atomic-scale details, especially those of disorder, are important for material properties, especially in semiconductors, but they are also extremely difficult to measure. Real-space methods can give direct access to this information, but typically, that access is limited. This review reports the application of three real-space techniques for measuring disorder to compound semiconductor materials: scanning tunneling microscopy, transmission electron microscopy, and atom-probe microscopy. Where possible, it emphasizes cases in which the probes have been combined to achieve a more complete picture of the defects.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025006] Published Thu Jun 26, 2025.
tldr: A review of real-space microscopy techniques for measuring atomic-scale disorder in semiconductors.
motivation: Atomic-scale disorder critically affects semiconductor properties but is difficult to measure; the paper reviews three real-space techniques to address this challenge.
method: The authors review scanning tunneling microscopy, transmission electron microscopy, and atom-probe microscopy, emphasizing combined approaches.
result: The review highlights how these techniques can directly access atomic-scale disorder information in compound semiconductors.
conclusion: Combining multiple real-space probes provides a more complete picture of defects, aiding materials science.

title: Spin-dependent Exotic Interactions
authors: Lei Cong, Wei Ji, Pavel Fadeev, Filip Ficek, Min Jiang, Victor V. Flambaum, Haosen Guan, Derek F. Jackson Kimball, Mikhail G. Kozlov, Yevgeny V. Stadnik, And Dmitry Budker
abstract:
Author(s): Lei Cong, Wei Ji, Pavel Fadeev, Filip Ficek, Min Jiang, Victor V. Flambaum, Haosen Guan, Derek F. Jackson Kimball, Mikhail G. Kozlov, Yevgeny V. Stadnik, and Dmitry Budker

This review presents a comprehensive summary of theoretical investigations and experimental searches for spin-dependent interactions beyond the standard model. These interactions may be mediated by various types of exotic bosons, and their existence and properties may, in turn, explain the nature of dark matter and dark energy. The described experiments also probe the discrete fundamental symmetries of nature.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025005] Published Tue Jun 24, 2025.
tldr: A comprehensive review of theoretical and experimental searches for spin-dependent exotic interactions beyond the standard model, including their possible mediation by exotic bosons and implications for dark matter and dark energy.
motivation: To understand the nature of dark matter and dark energy, and to probe discrete fundamental symmetries, by searching for spin-dependent interactions beyond the standard model.
method: The paper reviews a wide range of theoretical models and experimental techniques used to search for spin-dependent exotic interactions, including precision measurements and astrophysical observations.
result: The review summarizes current constraints on various exotic boson-mediated interactions and outlines future experimental directions.
conclusion: Spin-dependent exotic interactions are a promising avenue for discovering new physics, but current experiments have not yet found evidence for such interactions beyond the standard model.

title: Colloquium: Materials That Exceed Classical Thermodynamic Bounds On Properties
authors: Roderic S. Lakes
abstract:
Author(s): Roderic S. Lakes

Classical thermodynamic bounds provide constraints on values that are expected in measurements of certain physical properties. In a variety of fields, some measurements exceed these bounds. This apparent violation of thermodynamics arises because the measurements are made in ways that violate the underlying assumptions made when deriving these bounds. This Colloquium describes a wide variety of circumstances where such violations occur and which of the underlying assumptions are violated in each case. It also describes how interesting material properties can be developed using materials designed to violate these assumptions.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 021002] Published Wed May 14, 2025.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews materials that appear to exceed classical thermodynamic bounds on properties, explaining the violations by examining underlying assumptions.
motivation: Classical thermodynamic bounds are often assumed to be fundamental, but some measurements exceed them; understanding why clarifies the limits of thermodynamics and enables design of materials with extreme properties.
method: The paper surveys a wide variety of examples from different fields where measured properties exceed classical bounds, and analyzes which assumptions (e.g., equilibrium, linear response) are violated in each case.
result: It identifies that violations occur when measurements are made in ways that violate assumptions such as equilibrium, homogeneity, or linearity, and shows how materials can be designed to exploit these violations.
conclusion: The apparent violations do not contradict thermodynamics but rather highlight the importance of assumptions; this understanding can guide development of materials with properties beyond classical limits.

title: Colloquium: Synthetic Quantum Matter In Nonstandard Geometries
authors: Tobias Grass, Dario Bercioux, Utso Bhattacharya, Maciej Lewenstein, Hai Son Nguyen, And Christof Weitenberg
abstract:
Author(s): Tobias Grass, Dario Bercioux, Utso Bhattacharya, Maciej Lewenstein, Hai Son Nguyen, and Christof Weitenberg

This Colloquium presents ways to implement fractal lattices, curved spaces, and higher dimensions in atomic, photonic, and electronic systems. The study of quantum many-body physics in these exotic geometries permits simulation of phenomena from topology in condensed matter to models of gravity and cosmology.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 011001] Published Tue Mar 25, 2025.
tldr: A colloquium review on implementing fractal lattices, curved spaces, and higher dimensions in atomic, photonic, and electronic systems for quantum many-body physics.
motivation: To explore exotic geometries that enable simulation of phenomena from condensed matter topology to gravity and cosmology.
method: Review of experimental and theoretical approaches for realizing nonstandard geometries in synthetic quantum matter.
result: Summarizes progress in fractal lattices, curved spaces, and higher-dimensional simulations across platforms.
conclusion: These synthetic geometries open new avenues for studying quantum many-body physics beyond conventional setups.

title: Massive Quantum Systems As Interfaces Of Quantum Mechanics And Gravity
authors: Sougato Bose, Ivette Fuentes, Andrew A. Geraci, Saba Mehsar Khan, Sofia Qvarfort, Markus Rademacher, Muddassar Rashid, Marko Toroš, Hendrik Ulbricht, And Clara C. Wanjura
abstract:
Author(s): Sougato Bose, Ivette Fuentes, Andrew A. Geraci, Saba Mehsar Khan, Sofia Qvarfort, Markus Rademacher, Muddassar Rashid, Marko Toroš, Hendrik Ulbricht, and Clara C. Wanjura

The authors review theories and experimental state-of-the-art efforts to study the effects of gravity on massive quantum systems. Classical gravity is the least precisely tested natural force and may be addressed via precision quantum probes. Experiments testing whether the quantum nature of gravity causes decoherence and collapse of matter-wave functions and whether it can mediate entanglement between separate massive particles are underway, and their results will guide the theoretical description of gravity effects on a laboratory scale.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015003] Published Thu Feb 13, 2025.
tldr: A review of experimental and theoretical efforts to probe gravity using massive quantum systems, focusing on decoherence and entanglement mediated by gravity.
motivation: Classical gravity is the least precisely tested fundamental force, and quantum probes may reveal its quantum nature.
method: The paper reviews theoretical frameworks (e.g., decoherence models, entanglement tests) and experimental platforms (e.g., matter-wave interferometry, optomechanics) for testing gravity with massive quantum systems.
result: Current experiments are approaching the sensitivity needed to test whether gravity induces decoherence or entanglement, but no conclusive evidence has been found yet.
conclusion: Massive quantum systems offer a promising avenue to study the interplay between quantum mechanics and gravity, guiding future theoretical and experimental work.

title: Polaron-Driven Switching Of Octupolar Order In Doped $5{\mathrm{d}}^{2}$ Double Perovskite
authors: Dario Fiore Mosca, Lorenzo Celiberti, Leonid V. Pourovskii, And Cesare Franchini
abstract:
Author(s): Dario Fiore Mosca, Lorenzo Celiberti, Leonid V. Pourovskii, and Cesare Franchini

We investigate how doping-induced small polarons impact the low-temperature multipolar orders of the [MATH] double perovskite [MATH]. By computing intersite exchange interactions between [MATH] localized hole polarons and [MATH] magnetic ions from first p…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 046504] Published Wed Jul 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies polaron-driven switching of octupolar order in a doped double perovskite, focusing on condensed matter physics of multipolar orders.
motivation: To understand how doping-induced small polarons affect low-temperature multipolar orders in a specific double perovskite material.
method: First-principles calculations of intersite exchange interactions between hole polarons and magnetic ions.
result: Doping-induced polarons can switch the octupolar order, altering the magnetic properties.
conclusion: Polaron formation is a key mechanism for controlling multipolar orders in this material.

title: Ultrafast Formation Of A Photoinduced Hidden State Driven By A Bond-Order Wave In A Metal-Organic Framework
authors: Samiran Banu, Tatsuya Amano, Takahisa Kato, Kou Takubo, Yoichi Okimoto, Shinya Koshihara, Yohei Kawakami, Hirotake Itoh, Wataru Kosaka, Hitoshi Miyasaka, Shinichiro Iwai, Akira Takahashi, And Tadahiko Ishikawa
abstract:
Author(s): Samiran Banu, Tatsuya Amano, Takahisa Kato, Kou Takubo, Yoichi Okimoto, Shinya Koshihara, Yohei Kawakami, Hirotake Itoh, Wataru Kosaka, Hitoshi Miyasaka, Shinichiro Iwai, Akira Takahashi, and Tadahiko Ishikawa

Sub-10-fs pump-probe reflectivity measurements combined with model calculations reveal the emergence of a photoinduced hidden (PH) state in a donor-acceptor-type metal-organic framework. Transient spectra exhibit an additional absorption band developing on a [MATH] timescal…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 046902] Published Wed Jul 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies ultrafast photoinduced phase transitions in a metal-organic framework driven by a bond-order wave, with no connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: To understand the formation dynamics of a photoinduced hidden state in a donor-acceptor metal-organic framework.
method: Sub-10-fs pump-probe reflectivity measurements combined with model calculations.
result: Observation of an additional absorption band developing on a femtosecond timescale, attributed to a bond-order wave.
conclusion: The hidden state arises from a cooperative bond-order wave, demonstrating ultrafast photoinduced phase transition in this material.

title: Radiation Reaction Effects On Coherent Emission In Relativistic Magnetized Shocks
authors: Yu Zhang, Yuan-Pei Yang, And Liang-Liang Ji
abstract:
Author(s): Yu Zhang, Yuan-Pei Yang, and Liang-Liang Ji

Relativistic magnetized shocks are natural sources of coherent radiation, representing a promising framework for fast radio bursts (FRBs). This Letter explores how the radiation reaction (RR) effect, triggered by high-energy photon emissions during shock radiation, significantly alters particle dyna…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 045201] Published Tue Jul 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies radiation reaction effects on coherent emission in relativistic magnetized shocks, relevant to astrophysical fast radio bursts.
motivation: Understanding coherent radiation from relativistic shocks is key to explaining fast radio bursts, but radiation reaction effects on particle dynamics and emission have been neglected.
method: The authors perform particle-in-cell simulations including radiation reaction to model particle dynamics and coherent emission in magnetized shocks.
result: Radiation reaction significantly alters particle trajectories and reduces the efficiency of coherent emission, leading to observable signatures.
conclusion: Radiation reaction must be accounted for in models of coherent emission from relativistic shocks to accurately predict FRB properties.

title: Anomalous Reflection Phase Of Slot Plasmons In An $\mathrm{AlGaN}/\mathrm{GaN}$ Plasmonic Crystal
authors: A. R. Khisameeva, D. A. Khudaiberdiev, I. M. Moiseenko, P. A. Gusikhin, A. S. Astrakhantseva, A. Shuvaev, A. Pimenov, D. A. Svintsov, I. V. Kukushkin, And V. M. Muravev
abstract:
Author(s): A. R. Khisameeva, D. A. Khudaiberdiev, I. M. Moiseenko, P. A. Gusikhin, A. S. Astrakhantseva, A. Shuvaev, A. Pimenov, D. A. Svintsov, I. V. Kukushkin, and V. M. Muravev

We experimentally investigate the terahertz spectrum of plasma excitations in a plasmonic crystal based on AlGaN/GaN two-dimensional electron system (2DES). While screened plasmon modes with linear dispersion are readily observed in such structures, unscreened modes localized in the slots between th…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 046901] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies terahertz plasma excitations in an AlGaN/GaN plasmonic crystal, focusing on anomalous reflection phase of slot plasmons.
motivation: To understand the properties of plasma excitations in two-dimensional electron systems, particularly unscreened slot plasmon modes.
method: Experimental terahertz spectroscopy of a plasmonic crystal based on AlGaN/GaN 2DES.
result: Observation of anomalous reflection phase of slot plasmons.
conclusion: The findings contribute to the understanding of plasmonic phenomena in semiconductor heterostructures.

title: Calculating Resonance Using Parametric Equations Of Motion In The Limit Of The Complex Absorbing Potential Strength Parameter ($η→{0}^{+}$)
authors: Deepak Kumar And Ashish Kumar Gupta
abstract:
Author(s): Deepak Kumar and Ashish Kumar Gupta

Since complex absorbing potentials (CAPs) are nonphysical in nature, they can introduce artificial perturbations into the system, which may lead to shifts in the calculated energy. This study presents a methodology to eliminate artificial reflections caused by the CAP using a backward parametric equ…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012818] Published Tue Jul 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a method to eliminate artificial reflections from complex absorbing potentials in resonance calculations using parametric equations of motion.
motivation: Complex absorbing potentials introduce artificial perturbations that shift calculated energies; the authors aim to correct this.
method: A backward parametric equation of motion is used in the limit of vanishing CAP strength to remove artificial reflections.
result: The methodology successfully eliminates artificial reflections, yielding more accurate resonance energies.
conclusion: The proposed approach improves the accuracy of resonance calculations by mitigating CAP-induced artifacts.

title: Isotope Shifts In Heliumlike Carbon: Probes Of Nuclear Structure And New Bosons
authors: Xiao-Qiu Qi, Fang-Fei Wu, Zong-Chao Yan, Zhen-Xiang Zhong, Li-Yan Tang, Ai-Xi Chen, And Ting-Yun Shi
abstract:
Author(s): Xiao-Qiu Qi, Fang-Fei Wu, Zong-Chao Yan, Zhen-Xiang Zhong, Li-Yan Tang, Ai-Xi Chen, and Ting-Yun Shi

We present high-precision calculations of isotope shifts for the [MATH] and [MATH] transitions in heliumlike [MATH], with mass-shift u…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012817] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: High-precision calculations of isotope shifts in heliumlike carbon to probe nuclear structure and search for new bosons.
motivation: Isotope shifts provide a sensitive probe of nuclear properties and can constrain new physics beyond the Standard Model.
method: Variational calculations using explicitly correlated basis functions with relativistic and QED corrections.
result: Accurate isotope shift predictions for two transitions in heliumlike carbon, with uncertainties small enough to test nuclear charge radii and new boson couplings.
conclusion: The results enable experimental tests of nuclear structure and searches for new light bosons via precision spectroscopy.

title: Anomalous Carrier Dynamics In A Van Der Waals Heterostructure With A Janus Layer
authors: Yifan Wu, Yuee Xie, Han Wang, And Yuanping Chen
abstract:
Author(s): Yifan Wu, Yuee Xie, Han Wang, and Yuanping Chen

A two-dimensional (2D) Janus layer has different physical properties than a 2D non-Janus layer. When a van der Waals (vdW) heterostructure contains a Janus layer, some unusual phenomena different from those in a heterostructure made of two non-Janus layers are expected. Here, we study electronic str…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 065422] Published Wed Jul 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies anomalous carrier dynamics in a van der Waals heterostructure containing a Janus layer, focusing on electronic structure and transport properties.
motivation: To explore unusual electronic phenomena arising from the Janus layer in van der Waals heterostructures, which differ from conventional non-Janus heterostructures.
method: First-principles calculations based on density functional theory (DFT) to analyze electronic structure and carrier dynamics.
result: The Janus layer induces anomalous carrier dynamics, including unusual band alignment and transport behavior.
conclusion: The findings reveal new physical properties in Janus-layer heterostructures, potentially useful for nanoelectronic devices.

title: Identifying The Origin Of Out-of-plane Spin Polarization In The Noncollinear Antiferromagnet ${\mathrm{Mn}}_{3}\mathrm{Ge}$
authors: Mingxing Wu, Kouta Kondou, Taishi Chen, Satoru Nakatsuji, And Yoshichika Otani
abstract:
Author(s): Mingxing Wu, Kouta Kondou, Taishi Chen, Satoru Nakatsuji, and YoshiChika Otani

Noncollinear antiferromagnets Mn
[Phys. Rev. B 114, L020403] Published Wed Jul 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates the origin of out-of-plane spin polarization in the noncollinear antiferromagnet Mn3Ge, focusing on spin Hall effect and spin swapping mechanisms.
motivation: The microscopic origin of out-of-plane spin polarization in Mn3Ge is debated, and understanding it is crucial for spintronic applications.
method: The authors use spin-torque ferromagnetic resonance on single-crystal Mn3Ge bilayers with different crystallographic orientations to evaluate spin torques.
result: Both magnetic spin Hall effect and spin swapping coexist with comparable magnitudes, contributing to the out-of-plane spin polarization.
conclusion: The study resolves the debate by showing that both mechanisms are responsible, providing insight into spin-orbit torques in antiferromagnets.

title: Muonium Reaction In ${\mathrm{La}}_{2}{\mathrm{O}}_{3}$: Investigation Of The Last Steps In Muon Implantation
authors: C. M. S. Santos, A. G. Marinopoulos, J. M. Gil, R. C. Vilão, A. Weidinger, And T. Prokscha
abstract:
Author(s): C. M. S. Santos, A. G. Marinopoulos, J. M. Gil, R. C. Vilão, A. Weidinger, and T. Prokscha

We report on a muon spin rotation study of the wide band-gap material [MATH]. The focus is on the implantation process and the configurations formed at the end of the implantation trajectory. The data are analyzed in the recently developed “doorway model.” First-principl…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 045205] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies muonium reactions in La2O3 using muon spin rotation, focusing on the implantation process and final configurations.
motivation: Understanding the last steps of muon implantation in wide band-gap materials is important for interpreting muon spin rotation experiments.
method: The authors analyze muon spin rotation data using the 'doorway model' and first-principles calculations.
result: They identify the configurations formed at the end of the implantation trajectory and characterize the muonium reaction.
conclusion: The study provides insights into muon implantation dynamics in La2O3, but does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Twistoptics In Planar Heterostructures With An Arbitrary Number Of Rotated Three-dimensional Thin Layers And Two-dimensional Conductive Sheets
authors: Christian Lanza, José Álvarez-Cuervo, Kirill V. Voronin, Gonzalo Álvarez-Pérez, Aitana Tarazaga Martín-Luengo, Javier Martín-Sánchez, Alexey Y. Nikitin, And Pablo Alonso-González
abstract:
Author(s): Christian Lanza, José Álvarez-Cuervo, Kirill V. Voronin, Gonzalo Álvarez-Pérez, Aitana Tarazaga Martín-Luengo, Javier Martín-Sánchez, Alexey Y. Nikitin, and Pablo Alonso-González

Twistoptics has recently emerged as a branch of nano-optics that explores light propagation in stacks of thin anisotropic layers rotated relative to one another. The concept is particularly relevant for polaritons—hybrid light-matter quasiparticles—in van der Waals (vdW) materials, where strong in-p…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 045423] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies twistoptics in planar heterostructures with rotated layers and conductive sheets, focusing on polariton propagation.
motivation: To understand and control light-matter interactions in twisted van der Waals heterostructures for nano-optics applications.
