method: The authors develop a theoretical framework to describe electromagnetic modes in stacks of anisotropic layers and 2D sheets with arbitrary rotations.
result: They derive general dispersion relations and demonstrate tunable polariton properties via twist angles.
conclusion: Twistoptics provides a versatile platform for engineering polaritons in layered materials, with potential applications in nanophotonics.

title: Dynamics-induced Activity Patterns Of Active-inactive Clusters In Complex Networks
authors: Anil Kumar, V. K. Chandrasekar, And D. V. Senthilkumar
abstract:
Author(s): Anil Kumar, V. K. Chandrasekar, and D. V. Senthilkumar

Synchrony patterns describe network states in which nodes of a coupled dynamical system are grouped into clusters based on synchronization between nodes. Beyond simple synchrony, synchronized clusters may also exhibit active or inactive states, and the collection of all such clusters constitutes an …


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014219] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies synchrony patterns in complex networks, focusing on active-inactive cluster dynamics, which is unrelated to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: Understanding synchronization patterns in complex networks is important for network science, but the paper does not connect to quantum information theory or thermodynamics.
method: The authors analyze coupled dynamical systems on complex networks to identify conditions for active-inactive cluster formation.
result: They derive conditions for the emergence of such clusters and characterize their dynamics.
conclusion: The work contributes to nonlinear dynamics and network science, but has no relevance to the specified research interests.

title: First-passage Times For The Space-fractional Fokker-Planck Equation
authors: Christopher N. Angstmann, Daniel S. Han, Bruce I. Henry, And Boris Z. Huang
abstract:
Author(s): Christopher N. Angstmann, Daniel S. Han, Bruce I. Henry, and Boris Z. Huang

We extend the random walk framework to include compounded steps, providing first-passage time (FPT) properties for a class of superdiffusive processes which are governed by the space-fractional spectral Fokker-Planck equation. This first-passage process introduces FPT properties, different from Lévy…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014136] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies first-passage times for superdiffusive processes governed by the space-fractional Fokker-Planck equation.
motivation: Understanding first-passage times in anomalous diffusion is important for various physical systems, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors extend the random walk framework to include compounded steps and derive first-passage time properties for space-fractional Fokker-Planck dynamics.
result: They obtain first-passage time distributions that differ from those of Lévy flights, highlighting the role of the fractional derivative order.
conclusion: The work provides analytical results for first-passage times in a class of superdiffusive processes, but its relevance to quantum information theory or information thermodynamics is minimal.

title: Continuous-time Random Walks With Asymmetric Waiting-time And Jump-length Distributions As A Model Of Biased Anomalous Transport
authors: Guohua Li, Andrey G. Cherstvy, Hong Zhang, Zeyu Tu, And Ralf Metzler
abstract:
Author(s): Guohua Li, Andrey G. Cherstvy, Hong Zhang, Zeyu Tu, and Ralf Metzler

Continuous-time random walks (CTRWs) are highly appreciated as a model of anomalous diffusion (AD) in complex media such as structured and heterogeneous environments. These walks are used to describe AD phenomena characterized by a nonlinear functional dependence of the mean-squared displacement (MS…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014129] Published Thu Jul 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies continuous-time random walks with asymmetric waiting-time and jump-length distributions as a model of biased anomalous transport.
motivation: Anomalous diffusion is common in complex media, and biased transport (e.g., in biological cells) requires models that capture asymmetry in both waiting times and jump lengths.
method: The authors develop a CTRW model with coupled asymmetric waiting-time and jump-length distributions, and analyze the mean-squared displacement and other transport properties.
result: They derive conditions for subdiffusive, superdiffusive, and normal diffusion regimes, and show how asymmetry affects the transport exponent and diffusion coefficient.
conclusion: The model provides a flexible framework for describing biased anomalous transport in heterogeneous systems, but does not directly address quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Realizable Entropic Lattice Boltzmann Method For high-Péclet Scalar Transport
authors: Jingsen Feng, Yang Liu, And Xu Chu
abstract:
Author(s): Jingsen Feng, Yang Liu, and Xu Chu

We present a realizable entropic lattice Boltzmann method (RELBM) for scalar transport at high Péclet (Pe) number. The method combines an ADE-tailored entropic relaxation with a nonorthogonality correction to ghost-mode damping and a strictly conservative population-space realizability limiter activ…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, L013301] Published Thu Jul 16, 2026.
tldr: A realizable entropic lattice Boltzmann method for high-Péclet scalar transport in fluid dynamics.
motivation: To improve numerical stability and accuracy of lattice Boltzmann simulations for scalar transport at high Péclet numbers.
method: Combines an ADE-tailored entropic relaxation with nonorthogonality correction to ghost-mode damping and a conservative realizability limiter.
result: The method achieves stable and accurate simulations for high-Péclet scalar transport.
conclusion: The proposed RELBM is effective for high-Péclet scalar transport problems.

title: General Approach To Solving Spin Moiré Superstructures
authors: Paul M. Neves, Takashi Kurumaji, Joshua P. Wakefield, Arno Hiess, Paul Steffens, Navid Qureshi, Robert Cubitt, Lisa M. Debeer-Schmitt, Johanna C. Palmstrom, Satoru Hayami, Marek Bartkowiak, Markus Zolliker, Jonathan S. White, And Joseph G. Checkelsky

Mapping of spin textures in EuAg
[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021054] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a general approach to solving spin moiré superstructures in EuAg4Sb2, revealing three distinct magnetic phases and establishing a design framework for spin-based vortex lattices.
motivation: The study aims to understand and control spin textures in moiré superstructures, which are of interest for manipulating information via spin-based vortex lattices.
method: The authors use neutron scattering and other experimental techniques to map spin textures in EuAg4Sb2, combined with theoretical modeling to identify three tunable magnetic phases.
result: Three distinct magnetic phases are discovered, each with unique spin textures, and a design framework for spin moiré superstructures is established.
conclusion: The work provides a general approach to engineering spin moiré superstructures, potentially enabling new ways to manipulate information through spin-based vortex lattices.

title: Are Neural Networks Collision Resistant?
authors: Marco Benedetti, Andrej Bogdanov, Enrico M. Malatesta, Marc Mézard, Gianmarco Perrupato, Alon Rosen, Nikolaj I. Schwartzbach, And Riccardo Zecchina
abstract:
Author(s): Marco Benedetti, Andrej Bogdanov, Enrico M. Malatesta, Marc Mézard, Gianmarco Perrupato, Alon Rosen, Nikolaj I. Schwartzbach, and Riccardo Zecchina

A study of the computational complexity of finding collisions in a simple one-layer neural network shows that efficient algorithms fail to find collisions, a result of direct relevance for the definition of new cryptographic protocols based on machine-learning models.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021051] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the computational complexity of finding collisions in a simple one-layer neural network, showing that efficient algorithms fail to find collisions.
motivation: To explore whether neural networks can serve as collision-resistant hash functions for cryptographic protocols.
method: The authors analyze the computational complexity of collision finding in a one-layer neural network using theoretical and algorithmic approaches.
result: Efficient algorithms are shown to fail in finding collisions, suggesting that such neural networks may be collision resistant.
conclusion: The findings are relevant for defining new cryptographic protocols based on machine-learning models.

title: Robust Orbital-Selective Flat Bands In Layered Transition-Metal Oxyhalides At Room Temperature
authors: Xiangyu Luo, Ludovica Zullo, Sahaj Patel, Dongjin Oh, Willa Mihalyi-Koch, Emma Lian, Jiaruo Li, Qian Song, Asish K. Kundu, Anil Rajapitamahuni, Elio Vescovo, Natalia Olszowska, Rafał Kurleto, Dawid Wutke, Xavier Roy, Giorgio Sangiovanni, And Riccardo Comin
abstract:

Angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy of layered transition-metal oxyhalides reveals intrinsic flat bands that remain stable at room temperature, providing a tunable platform for investigating strongly correlated electron states.

tldr: This paper reports the observation of robust orbital-selective flat bands in layered transition-metal oxyhalides at room temperature using angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy.
motivation: Flat bands in strongly correlated materials can host exotic quantum phases, but most known flat bands require cryogenic temperatures. The authors aim to find a room-temperature stable platform.
method: Angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES) was performed on layered transition-metal oxyhalides to map the electronic band structure.
result: Intrinsic flat bands were observed that remain stable at room temperature, with orbital selectivity and tunability via material composition.
conclusion: These materials provide a tunable platform for investigating strongly correlated electron states at room temperature, potentially enabling new quantum phenomena.

title: Colloquium: What Do We Mean By ‘active Matter’?
authors: Michael Te Vrugt, Benno Liebchen, And Michael E. Cates
abstract:
Author(s): Michael te Vrugt, Benno Liebchen, and Michael E. Cates

Active matter has become a lively topic in recent years, but what exactly is meant by the term ‘active matter’ is often unclear. This Colloquium discusses the scientific and semantic issues underlying this ambiguity, as well as the history of the field, and offers a definition of active matter as a well-defined subset of nonequilibrium systems. It then surveys recent developments including nonreciprocal interactions, intracellular phase separation, and quantum active matter.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 031001] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This Colloquium discusses the definition, history, and recent developments of active matter, including nonreciprocal interactions, intracellular phase separation, and quantum active matter.
motivation: The term 'active matter' is often used ambiguously; the paper aims to clarify its meaning and scope.
method: The authors review the history of the field, propose a definition of active matter as a subset of nonequilibrium systems, and survey recent developments.
result: They offer a clear definition and highlight emerging topics such as quantum active matter.
conclusion: Active matter is a well-defined subset of nonequilibrium systems, and the field is expanding into new areas including quantum systems.

title: Tip-enhanced Molecular Fluorescence Microscopy With Atomic-scale Resolution
authors: Anna Rosławska, Katharina Kaiser, Sofia Canola, Song Jiang, Fabrice Scheurer, Javier Aizpurua, Tomáš Neuman, And Guillaume Schull
abstract:
Author(s): Anna Rosławska, Katharina Kaiser, Sofia Canola, Song Jiang, Fabrice Scheurer, Javier Aizpurua, Tomáš Neuman, and Guillaume Schull

Scanning probe techniques have transformed our ability to study materials at the atomic scale, providing atom-by-atom views of surfaces. Tip-enhanced molecular fluorescence microscopy combines scanning probes with optical fluorescence. Such optical techniques normally have spatial resolution limited by the wavelength of the light used. However, using the scanning tip itself as a nanoscale optical antenna confines the electromagnetic field to the tip apex, achieving superresolution down to the atomic scale. Fluorescence is a fundamental probe of materials that reveals electronic structure and vibronic properties by exciting electrons to higher levels and observing the photons emitted when they relax. These capabilities are of particular interest for studying and identifying molecules, submolecular structures, and their reactions. This review discusses the techniques of tip-enhanced molecular fluorescence microscopy and the new insights they have revealed.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025007] Published Tue Jun 30, 2026.
tldr: This review discusses tip-enhanced molecular fluorescence microscopy achieving atomic-scale resolution using scanning probe techniques.
motivation: To overcome the diffraction limit in optical microscopy and achieve atomic-scale spatial resolution for studying molecular electronic and vibronic properties.
method: Combines scanning probe microscopy with a nanoscale optical antenna at the tip apex to confine the electromagnetic field, enabling super-resolution fluorescence imaging.
result: Demonstrates atomic-scale resolution in fluorescence microscopy, allowing visualization of individual molecules and submolecular structures.
conclusion: Tip-enhanced fluorescence microscopy provides a powerful tool for nanoscale optical characterization of molecular systems.

title: Neutron Stars And The Dense Matter Equation Of State
authors: Katerina Chatziioannou, H. Thankful Cromartie, Stefano Gandolfi, Ingo Tews, David Radice, Andrew W. Steiner, And Anna L. Watts
abstract:
Author(s): Katerina Chatziioannou, H. Thankful Cromartie, Stefano Gandolfi, Ingo Tews, David Radice, Andrew W. Steiner, and Anna L. Watts

Neutron stars, the remnants of supernova explosions, are the densest objects in the Universe. A typical neutron star has a mass between one and two solar masses, and a radius of around 12 km. The density at the center of the star is higher than that in atomic nuclei. As a result, the properties of neutron stars provide important information about the behavior of ordinary matter under extreme compression. In recent years, new information about neutron stars has emerged from two sources. The first is the observation of the gravitational-wave signal from the final inspiral of a coalescing binary neutron star. The second is a careful measurement of the x-ray pulse profile of a spinning neutron star. This review discusses these measurements and summarizes how they constrain masses, radii, and central densities. The results are compared to predictions based on calculations of the nuclear equation of state at densities comparable to that in atomic nuclei, which are then extrapolated to higher density. The review ends with an outlook on future observational opportunities.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045007] Published Wed Dec 24, 2025.
tldr: This review discusses neutron star observations and constraints on the dense matter equation of state.
motivation: Neutron stars are the densest objects in the Universe, and their properties provide information about matter under extreme compression.
method: The review summarizes constraints from gravitational-wave signals of binary neutron star mergers and X-ray pulse profile measurements.
result: The measurements constrain masses, radii, and central densities, which are compared to nuclear equation of state predictions.
conclusion: Future observations will further refine our understanding of dense matter.

title: Fitness-Driven Scaling Laws Between mRNA And Protein Levels
authors: Yichen Yan (颜逸辰) And Jie Lin
abstract:
Author(s): Yichen Yan (颜逸辰) and Jie Lin (林杰)

The relationship between protein and messenger RNA (mRNA) levels is a key aspect of gene expression. Although a strong mRNA-protein correlation is widely observed, the evolutionary force driving the correlation remains poorly understood, undermining the reliability of using mRNA abundance as a proxy…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 048402] Published Wed Jul 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the scaling relationship between mRNA and protein levels from an evolutionary fitness perspective.
motivation: Understanding the evolutionary forces driving the correlation between mRNA and protein levels is crucial for reliable gene expression inference.
method: The authors develop a theoretical model incorporating fitness effects to derive scaling laws between mRNA and protein abundances.
result: They find that the scaling exponent depends on the fitness landscape and mutation rates, explaining observed correlations.
conclusion: The work provides an evolutionary basis for mRNA-protein correlations, but is unrelated to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: High Temperature Ferromagnetism In Epitaxial Monolayers Of Co-Doped ${\mathrm{Fe}}_{5}{\mathrm{GeTe}}_{2}$
authors: Jules Courtin, Fatima Ibrahim, Davide Benettin, Djordje Dosenovic, Roberto Sant, Pâmella Vasconcelos Borges Pinho, Vincent Polewczyk, Alain Marty, Isabelle Gomes de Moraes, Matthieu Jamet, Denis Jalabert, Fadi Choueikani, Philippe Ohresser, Nicholas B. motivation: To overcome the challenge of producing atomically thin magnetic films that maintain long-range magnetic order above 150 K.
method: Epitaxial growth of Co-doped Fe5GeTe2 monolayers and characterization using X-ray magnetic circular dichroism and other techniques.
result: The Co-doped monolayers exhibit ferromagnetism with a Curie temperature above room temperature.

title: Essay: Pushing The Frontiers Of High Energy Density Science Toward Unexplored States Of Matter
authors: Federica Coppari
abstract:
Author(s): Federica Coppari

In this forward-looking PRL Essay, Federica Coppari presents a compelling perspective on high-energy-density science, centering on the remarkable behavior of matter under extreme conditions—such as very high pressures and a wide range of temperatures—like those found deep inside planets, stars, and fusion reactions.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 040001] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: This essay discusses high-energy-density science, focusing on matter under extreme pressures and temperatures relevant to planetary interiors and fusion.
motivation: To explore the frontiers of high-energy-density physics and understand material behavior under extreme conditions.
method: Perspective article summarizing current knowledge and future directions in high-energy-density science.
result: Highlights the need for new experimental and theoretical approaches to study matter at extreme conditions.
conclusion: Advancing high-energy-density science will require interdisciplinary efforts and novel facilities.

title: Superfluidity In The Second Layer Of $^{4}\mathrm{He}$ On Graphite
authors: Jun Usami And Hiroshi Fukuyama
abstract:
Author(s): Jun Usami and Hiroshi Fukuyama

Evidence for a new type of superfluid phase in second-layer [MATH] on graphite has been obtained from simultaneous measurements of torsional-oscillator response and heat capacity on exactly the same sample down to 30 mK, which resolve substrate-related uncertainties in the previous studie…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 046001] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports experimental evidence for a new superfluid phase in the second layer of 4He on graphite.
motivation: Previous studies of second-layer 4He on graphite were inconclusive due to substrate-related uncertainties; this work aims to resolve those uncertainties.
method: Simultaneous torsional-oscillator and heat capacity measurements were performed on the same sample down to 30 mK.
result: Evidence for a new type of superfluid phase in the second layer was obtained.
conclusion: The findings clarify the phase diagram of 4He films on graphite and reveal a novel superfluid state.

title: Nmr Evidence For Spontaneous Electronic Chiral Order In URhSn
authors: Y. Tokunaga, T. Ishitobi, H. Sakai, S. Kambe, H. Harima, A. Nakamura, A. Maurya, D. Li, Y. Homma, F. Honda, D. Aoki, And Y. Shimizu
abstract:
Author(s): Y. Tokunaga, T. Ishitobi, H. Sakai, S. Kambe, H. Harima, A. Nakamura, A. Maurya, D. Li, Y. Homma, F. Honda, D. Aoki, and Y. Shimizu

The first direct evidence of spontaneous electronic chiral order in URhSn, a strongly correlated material without an inherently chiral lattice structure, fundamentally challenges the prevailing notion that electronic chirality requires a chiral crystal framework.

tldr: This paper reports NMR evidence for spontaneous electronic chiral order in URhSn, a strongly correlated material without a chiral lattice.
motivation: To challenge the prevailing notion that electronic chirality requires a chiral crystal framework by finding direct evidence in a non-chiral lattice.
method: Nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) measurements on URhSn single crystals.
result: Observation of spontaneous electronic chiral order in URhSn, providing the first direct evidence of such order in a material without an inherently chiral lattice.
conclusion: Electronic chirality can emerge in non-chiral lattices, fundamentally changing the understanding of chiral order in strongly correlated materials.

In this work, we calculate the hyperfine-structure constants of the [MATH] ion using a relativistic hybrid approach that combines configuration-interaction and coupled-cluster singles and doubles methods. Magnetic-dipole and electric-quadrupole hyperfine-structure constants are deter…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012816] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper calculates hyperfine-structure constants and nuclear quadrupole moment of Sc II using relativistic hybrid methods.
motivation: Accurate hyperfine constants are needed for atomic spectroscopy and nuclear structure studies.
method: A relativistic hybrid approach combining configuration-interaction and coupled-cluster singles and doubles methods is used.
result: Magnetic-dipole and electric-quadrupole hyperfine-structure constants are determined, and the nuclear quadrupole moment is extracted.
conclusion: The calculated values provide improved atomic data for Sc II, useful for astrophysical and nuclear physics applications.

title: Spatiotemporal-kinetic Coupling In The Fluorescence Dynamics Of Femtosecond-laser-induced Nitrogen Plasma At Low Pressures
authors: Hongqiang Xie, Ziyuan Zuo, Weikang Lei, Shibo Song, Jintao Luo, Runbin Chen, Mingzheng Wei, Wei Luo, Long Zou, Zhiming Chen, Yazi Luo, And Guihua Li
abstract:

tldr: This paper studies the spatiotemporal-kinetic coupling in fluorescence dynamics of femtosecond-laser-induced nitrogen plasma at low pressures.
motivation: Understanding the microscopic excited-state dynamics initiated by macroscopic propagation of femtosecond laser pulses in gas mixtures is important for applications in remote sensing and plasma physics.

result: The study reveals how spatiotemporal dynamics of the laser pulse affect the fluorescence emission from nitrogen plasma under low-pressure conditions.
conclusion: The findings provide insights into the complex interplay between laser propagation and plasma kinetics, which can inform the design of laser-induced plasma experiments.

motivation: To study atomic parity violation as a probe of nuclear properties, specifically neutron skin effects, in highly charged ions.
method: Relativistic many-body calculations of parity-violating E1 amplitudes for specific transitions in H- and Li-like ions of Ca and Pb, including nuclear uncertainties.

conclusion: The calculations can be used to extract nuclear information from future experiments on atomic parity violation in highly charged ions.

title: Raman Spectroscopy Of The Van Der Waals Topological Magnet GdGaI
authors: Nan Jiang, Yijin Zhang, Yujie Xia, Tomo Higashihara, Ryutaro Okuma, Jun-Ichi Yamaura, Yoshinori Okada, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Tiantian Zhang, Tomoki Machida, And Yasuhiro Niimi
abstract:

method: Polarization-resolved Raman spectroscopy combined with symmetry analysis and density functional theory calculations.
result: Six Raman-active phonons were identified, and the spectra matched expectations from symmetry analysis.
conclusion: The study provides a detailed phonon characterization of GdGaI, relevant for understanding its excitonic insulator properties.

title: Mie Voids As Broadband Directional Light Sources
authors: Benjamin Reichel, Adrià Canós Valero, Mario Hentschel, Harald Giessen, And Thomas Weiss

The Kerker effect arises from the interference between electric and magnetic multipoles, enabling directional light scattering in nanophotonics. However, conventional dielectric and plasmonic nanoparticles can only act as Kerker sources in narrow spectral regions, limiting their applicability. Here,…

tldr: This paper demonstrates that Mie voids can act as broadband directional light sources via the Kerker effect.
motivation: Conventional dielectric and plasmonic nanoparticles only achieve directional scattering in narrow spectral regions, limiting their applicability.
method: The authors theoretically and experimentally investigate Mie voids (air holes in a dielectric medium) to achieve broadband Kerker-type directional scattering.
result: Mie voids exhibit broadband directional light emission due to the overlap of electric and magnetic dipole resonances over a wide wavelength range.
conclusion: Mie voids provide a simple and robust platform for broadband directional light sources, with potential applications in nanophotonics.

result: Observation of H-linear magnetoresistance in the T^2 resistivity regime, indicating a possible quantum critical or scattering mechanism.
conclusion: The findings provide insights into the electronic properties of nickelates, but the paper focuses on condensed matter physics without direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Room-temperature Antiferromagnetic Resonance In NaMnAs
authors: Jan Dzian, Stáňa Tázlarů, Ivan Mohelský, Florian Le Mardelé, Filip Chudoba, Jiří Volný, Jan Wyzula, Amit Pawbake, Simone Ritarossi, Riccardo Mazzarello, Philipp Ritzinger, Jakub Železný, Karel Výborný, Klára Uhlířová, Benoît Grémaud, Andrés Saúl, Clément Faugeras, Martin Veis, And Milan Orlita

We report on antiferromagnetic resonance experiments in bulk tetragonal NaMnAs—a room-temperature antiferromagnetic semiconductor. Our results corroborate previous ab initio studies which propose that NaMnAs is an easy-axis antiferromagnet with the Néel vector oriented along the tetragonal axis. At …


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 034420] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports antiferromagnetic resonance experiments in the room-temperature antiferromagnetic semiconductor NaMnAs.
motivation: To experimentally confirm the magnetic properties of NaMnAs predicted by ab initio studies, specifically its easy-axis antiferromagnetic ordering.
method: Antiferromagnetic resonance (AFMR) spectroscopy was performed on bulk tetragonal NaMnAs samples.
result: The AFMR data corroborate that NaMnAs is an easy-axis antiferromagnet with the Néel vector along the tetragonal axis.
conclusion: NaMnAs is confirmed as a room-temperature antiferromagnetic semiconductor, which may be relevant for spintronics applications.

title: Short-term Plasticity-based Working Memory Spiking Model Is Resilient To Synaptic Heterogeneity
authors: Gianmarco Tiddia, Luca Sergi, Simone Rubiu, Antonio Incollu, And Bruno Golosio
abstract:
Author(s): Gianmarco Tiddia, Luca Sergi, Simone Rubiu, Antonio Incollu, and Bruno Golosio

The presence of activity-silent working memory has been increasingly supported by experimental observation, and short-term synaptic facilitation is suggested to underlie this phenomenon. Originally proposed in the early 2000s, the synaptic theory of working memory was supported by a relatively simpl…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014409] Published Wed Jul 22, 2026.
tldr: A spiking neural network model for working memory based on short-term plasticity is shown to be resilient to synaptic heterogeneity.
motivation: To understand how activity-silent working memory can be robustly maintained in neural circuits despite biological variability.
method: The authors develop a spiking neural network model with short-term synaptic facilitation and simulate its dynamics under varying levels of synaptic heterogeneity.
result: The model maintains working memory performance even with significant heterogeneity in synaptic parameters.
conclusion: Short-term plasticity provides a robust mechanism for working memory that is resilient to biological noise.

title: Absence Of O(2) Symmetry In The Vicsek Model
authors: Yushin Takahashi, Kota Mitsui, Tsuyoshi Mizohata, And Hideyuki Miyahara
abstract:
Author(s): Yushin Takahashi, Kota Mitsui, Tsuyoshi Mizohata, and Hideyuki Miyahara

The phase transition in the Vicsek model is widely believed to be associated with spontaneous symmetry breaking of the two-dimensional rotational symmetry [MATH]. In this paper, we revisit the original model introduced by Vicsek et al. [
tldr: This paper demonstrates that the Vicsek model does not exhibit O(2) symmetry breaking, contrary to common belief.
motivation: The Vicsek model is a paradigmatic model for collective motion, and its phase transition is often attributed to spontaneous breaking of O(2) symmetry. The authors aim to correct this misconception.
method: The authors revisit the original Vicsek model, analyze its symmetries, and perform numerical simulations to show the absence of O(2) symmetry breaking.
result: They find that the model's order parameter does not correspond to a broken continuous symmetry, and the phase transition is not associated with O(2) symmetry breaking.
conclusion: The widely held belief about O(2) symmetry breaking in the Vicsek model is incorrect; the model's transition is of a different nature.

title: Quantum Diffusion Of Molecular Hydrogen In Liquid $\mathrm{Ne}+{\mathrm{H}}_{2}$ Mixtures: A Quasielastic Neutron Scattering Study
authors: Daniele Colognesi, Ubaldo Bafile, Milva Celli, Leonardo Del Rosso, Franz Demmel, And Martin Neumann
abstract:

This study presents an analysis of the diffusional dynamics of [MATH] impurities in liquid Ne using quasielastic neutron scattering (QENS) and quantum dynamical simulations. By applying a Lorentzian fitting procedure, we identify two key spectral features: peak width ([MATH]) and i…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 015413] Published Thu Jul 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the diffusion of molecular hydrogen in liquid neon using neutron scattering and simulations, with no connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: To understand the diffusional dynamics of H2 impurities in liquid Ne, which is relevant for condensed matter physics but not for the user's research interests.
method: Quasielastic neutron scattering (QENS) experiments and quantum dynamical simulations, with Lorentzian fitting to extract spectral features.
result: Two spectral features (peak width and intensity) were identified, characterizing the diffusion process.
conclusion: The study provides insights into hydrogen diffusion in cryogenic liquids, but has no relevance to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: THz Dynamics Of Hydrogen Sulfide: Search For Collective Modes Of A Non-hydrogen-bonded Analog Of Water
authors: Ferdinando Formisano, Alessio de Francesco, Francesco Sacchetti, Caterina Petrillo, And Eleonora Guarini
abstract:
Author(s): Ferdinando Formisano, Alessio De Francesco, Francesco Sacchetti, Caterina Petrillo, and Eleonora Guarini

Using neutron inelastic scattering, the authors investigate the dynamics of liquid hydrogen sulfide, which is similar to water but lacks the hydrogen-bond network. While fast sound is preserved, the secondary weakly dispersive mode typical of hydrogen-bonded liquids is not detected.

#WellStructured #ClearMotivation #SoftMatterSpotlight


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 015412] Published Wed Jul 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the THz dynamics of liquid hydrogen sulfide using neutron scattering, focusing on collective modes in a non-hydrogen-bonded analog of water.
motivation: To understand the role of hydrogen bonding in the dynamics of liquids by comparing water with its non-hydrogen-bonded analog, hydrogen sulfide.
method: Neutron inelastic scattering experiments on liquid hydrogen sulfide to measure its dynamic structure factor and identify collective modes.
result: Fast sound is preserved in hydrogen sulfide, but the secondary weakly dispersive mode characteristic of hydrogen-bonded liquids is absent.
conclusion: The absence of the secondary mode confirms its association with hydrogen-bond networks, highlighting the unique dynamics of hydrogen-bonded liquids.

title: Rheology Of Dense Vibrated Granular Flows: Nonmonotonic Response Controlled By Granular Temperature
authors: A. Plati, G. Petrillo, L. de Arcangelis, A. Gnoli, A. Puglisi, A. Sarracino, And E. Lippiello
abstract:
Author(s): A. Plati, G. Petrillo, L. de Arcangelis, A. Gnoli, A. Puglisi, A. Sarracino, and E. Lippiello

When subjected to vibrations, the effective viscosity of a granular medium depends heavily on both confining pressure and vibration parameters. In this work, experimentally calibrated discrete element simulations of a vane rheometer are used to provide a unified framework that reconciles experimental observations. The results show that confining pressure directly dictates the rheological response, while vibration effects are mediated by the granular temperature, which results from a balance between energy input and internal dissipation.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L032010] Published Tue Jul 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the rheology of dense vibrated granular flows, focusing on the nonmonotonic response controlled by granular temperature.
motivation: Understanding the effective viscosity of granular media under vibrations is important for industrial processes and geophysics, but a unified framework reconciling experimental observations is lacking.
method: The authors use experimentally calibrated discrete element simulations of a vane rheometer to model dense vibrated granular flows.
result: Confining pressure directly dictates the rheological response, while vibration effects are mediated by granular temperature, which results from a balance between energy input and internal dissipation.
conclusion: The study provides a unified framework that reconciles experimental observations of granular rheology under vibrations.

title: Mie-tronics Supermodes And Symmetry Breaking In Nonlocal Metasurfaces
authors: Thanh Xuan Hoang, Ayan Nussupbekov, Jie Ji, Daniel Leykam, Jaime Gómez Rivas, And Yuri Kivshar
abstract:
Author(s): Thanh Xuan Hoang, Ayan Nussupbekov, Jie Ji, Daniel Leykam, Jaime Gómez Rivas, and Yuri Kivshar

It is usually believed that symmetry breaking in photonic systems leads to weaker confinement, such as in the case of metasurfaces when bound states in the continuum are replaced by quasibound states with lower quality [MATH] factors. Here, in contrast, we reveal that symmetry breaking can instead en…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033076] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies symmetry breaking in nonlocal metasurfaces, revealing that it can enhance light confinement and Q-factors, contrary to conventional wisdom.
motivation: Understanding symmetry breaking in photonic systems is important for controlling light-matter interactions, but its effect on confinement in nonlocal metasurfaces was unclear.
method: The authors theoretically and numerically analyze Mie-tronics supermodes in nonlocal metasurfaces, examining how symmetry breaking alters mode confinement and Q-factors.
result: They find that symmetry breaking can lead to stronger confinement and higher Q-factors, enabling new regimes of light-matter interaction.
conclusion: This work challenges the common belief that symmetry breaking always weakens confinement, offering new design principles for high-Q metasurfaces.

title: Multiphoton Ionization With Three-dimensional Light Fields
authors: D. Köhnke, H.-C. Ahlswede, T. Bayer, And M. Wollenhaupt
abstract:
Author(s): D. Köhnke, H.-C. Ahlswede, T. Bayer, and M. Wollenhaupt

We employ, for the first time, bichromatic three-dimensional (3D) polarization-shaped ultrashort laser fields in atomic multiphoton ionization to create previously inaccessible free-electron angular momentum wave packets. The 3D fields are created by the noncollinear superposition of two polarizatio…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033048] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses bichromatic three-dimensional polarization-shaped laser fields to create free-electron angular momentum wave packets in atomic multiphoton ionization.
motivation: To generate previously inaccessible free-electron angular momentum wave packets using novel 3D light fields.
method: Noncollinear superposition of two polarization-shaped ultrashort laser pulses to create 3D fields, applied to atomic multiphoton ionization.
result: Demonstration of free-electron angular momentum wave packets created by the 3D fields.
conclusion: The technique enables new control over electron dynamics in multiphoton ionization.

Hwang, and Zhi-Xun Shen

Angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy of bilayer nickelate thin films reveals that the out-of-plane nickel orbital band shifts with strain and doping but is not required at the Fermi level for superconductivity.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031008] Published Wed Jul 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the electronic structure of compressively strained bilayer nickelate thin films using angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy.
motivation: To understand the role of out-of-plane nickel orbital bands in superconductivity of bilayer nickelates.
method: Angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES) measurements on thin films under compressive strain and doping.
result: The out-of-plane nickel orbital band shifts with strain and doping but is not required at the Fermi level for superconductivity.
conclusion: The electronic structure of bilayer nickelates is sensitive to strain and doping, but the out-of-plane band is not essential for superconductivity.

title: General Framework Enabling Polarity-Tunable Time-Reversal Symmetric Superconducting Diode Effects In Gate-Defined Homojunctions
authors: Hongwei Zhang, Chunsheng Wang, Ran Wang, Senyang Pan, Hengning Wang, Jiaqiang Cai, Yonglai Liu, Zhe Qu, Xiangde Zhu, Wei Ning, Chuanying Xi, Jinglei Zhang, Ning Hao, Guolin Zheng, And Mingliang Tian

title: Elastic And Structural Anisotropy In Silica Thin Films For Gravitational-Wave Detectors
authors: Brenda Bracco, Michele Magnozzi, Stefano Colace, Maurizio Canepa, Giulio Favaro, Marco Bazzan, Massimo Granata, David Hofman, Alessandro Di Michele, Laura Silenzi, Gianpietro Cagnoli, Giovanni Carlotti, Paola Sassi, And Silvia Corezzi
abstract:
Author(s): Brenda Bracco, Michele Magnozzi, Stefano Colace, Maurizio Canepa, Giulio Favaro, Marco Bazzan, Massimo Granata, David Hofman, Alessandro Di Michele, Laura Silenzi, Gianpietro Cagnoli, Giovanni Carlotti, Paola Sassi, and Silvia Corezzi

Researchers find that silica films in mirror coatings of gravitational-wave detectors have hidden anisotropy that resists standard heat treatment. This discovery informs coating design and deposition and postprocessing strategies aimed at reducing thermal noise.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021036] Published Fri May 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies elastic and structural anisotropy in silica thin films used in gravitational-wave detector mirror coatings, focusing on material properties and thermal noise reduction.
motivation: Thermal noise in mirror coatings limits the sensitivity of gravitational-wave detectors; understanding and mitigating anisotropy in silica films could improve detector performance.
method: The authors characterize the elastic and structural properties of silica thin films using experimental techniques to detect hidden anisotropy and evaluate the effectiveness of standard heat treatments.
result: Silica films exhibit hidden anisotropy that resists standard heat treatment, informing coating design and postprocessing strategies.
conclusion: The findings guide the development of deposition and postprocessing strategies to reduce thermal noise in gravitational-wave detectors.

title: Radiation Forces And Torques In Optics And Acoustics
authors: Ivan Toftul, Sebastian Golat, Francisco J. Rodríguez-Fortuño, Franco Nori, Yuri Kivshar, And Konstantin Y. Bliokh
abstract:
Author(s): Ivan Toftul, Sebastian Golat, Francisco J. Rodríguez-Fortuño, Franco Nori, Yuri Kivshar, and Konstantin Y. Bliokh

This review presents a unified perspective of how local energy, momentum, and spin densities in optical and acoustic wave fields induce forces and torques on particles—a topic that has captivated researchers for centuries. Applications discussed include trapping and manipulation of atoms and nanoparticles by light, sorting of biological cells by the combination of acoustics and microfluidics, and pulling forces that draw particles against the direction of wave propagation.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025002] Published Thu Apr 30, 2026.
tldr: This review unifies the description of radiation forces and torques in optical and acoustic fields, focusing on momentum and spin densities.
motivation: Understanding how wave fields exert forces and torques on particles is fundamental for applications like optical trapping and acoustic manipulation.
method: The authors present a unified theoretical framework based on local energy, momentum, and spin densities in optical and acoustic waves.
result: They show that both optical and acoustic forces and torques can be described within the same formalism, highlighting similarities and differences.
conclusion: The unified perspective aids in designing advanced particle manipulation techniques using light and sound.

title: Pressure Effects On Metals, Alloys, And Compounds Of Transplutonium Elements
authors: Tyler W. Hines, Nicholas B. Beck, Kacy N. Mendoza, Joseph M. Sperling, And Thomas E. Albrecht
abstract:
Author(s): Tyler W. Hines, Nicholas B. Beck, Kacy N. Mendoza, Joseph M. Sperling, and Thomas E. Albrecht

Materials containing transplutonium elements (the actinides Am–Cm that come after Pu in the periodic table) are important for nuclear power, nuclear waste management, and long-term storage. They also have fascinating properties, with 5
[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 015004] Published Tue Mar 31, 2026.
tldr: A review of the physics and chemistry of transplutonium elements under high pressure, focusing on their electronic properties and material behavior.
motivation: Transplutonium materials are important for nuclear applications and exhibit unique electronic behavior at the boundary between localized and itinerant 5f electrons.
method: The paper reviews experimental and theoretical studies of transplutonium metals, alloys, and coordination complexes under high pressure.
result: The review summarizes the current understanding of pressure-induced changes in electronic structure, bonding, and phase transitions in these materials.
conclusion: High-pressure studies reveal complex behavior in transplutonium compounds, but the work is primarily materials science and condensed matter physics without direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Quantum Physics Of Stars
authors: M. Wiescher, C. A. Bertulani, C. R. Brune, R. J. Deboer, A. Diaz-Torres, L. R. Gasques, K. Langanke, P. Navrátil, W. Nazarewicz, J. Okołowicz, D. R. Phillips, M. Płoszajczak, S. Quaglioni, And A. Tumino
abstract:
Author(s): M. Wiescher, C. A. Bertulani, C. R. Brune, R. J. deBoer, A. Diaz-Torres, L. R. Gasques, K. Langanke, P. Navrátil, W. Nazarewicz, J. Okołowicz, D. R. Phillips, M. Płoszajczak, S. Quaglioni, and A. Tumino

There are many nuclear reactions that are of central importance for stellar burning and element formation. In typical stars, these reactions take place at very low energy, and many of them have very small rates, making it difficult to measure them directly in the laboratory. On the theoretical side, the low-energy regime is governed by quantum-mechanical phenomena like tunneling, near-threshold resonances, and interference effects. This review summarizes the state of the art in the theory of low-energy nuclear reactions in stars and describes new ideas for studying these reactions on Earth.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025003] Published Tue May 27, 2025.
tldr: This review summarizes the state of the art in low-energy nuclear reactions in stars, focusing on quantum tunneling, resonances, and interference effects.
motivation: Nuclear reactions at stellar energies are difficult to measure directly due to very small rates, and theoretical understanding is needed to model stellar burning and nucleosynthesis.
method: The paper reviews theoretical approaches for low-energy nuclear reactions, including quantum tunneling, near-threshold resonances, and interference effects, and discusses new experimental ideas.
result: The review provides a comprehensive overview of current theoretical methods and experimental challenges in low-energy nuclear astrophysics.
conclusion: Advances in theory and experiment are needed to better understand nuclear reactions that power stars and create elements.

title: Codata Recommended Values Of The Fundamental Physical Constants: 2022
authors: Peter J. Mohr, David B. Newell, Barry N. Taylor, And Eite Tiesinga
abstract:
Author(s): Peter J. Mohr, David B. Newell, Barry N. Taylor, and Eite Tiesinga

This review contains the 2022 self-consistent set of values of the constants and conversion factors of physics and chemistry recommended by the Committee on Data for Science and Technology (CODATA). The CODATA values are based on a least-squares adjustment that takes into account all data available up to the end of 2022. Details of the data selection and methodology are described.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025002] Published Wed Apr 30, 2025.
tldr: This paper presents the 2022 CODATA recommended values of fundamental physical constants based on a least-squares adjustment of all available data.
motivation: Accurate and consistent values of fundamental constants are essential for science and technology, and periodic updates incorporate new measurements and improve precision.
method: A least-squares adjustment is performed on a global dataset of measurements, taking into account correlations and uncertainties to produce self-consistent constant values.
result: The 2022 set of recommended values for fundamental constants and conversion factors is provided, with updated uncertainties compared to previous adjustments.
conclusion: The CODATA recommended values serve as the internationally accepted standard for fundamental constants, supporting research and applications across physics and chemistry.

title: Self-aligning Polar Active Matter
authors: Paul Baconnier, Olivier Dauchot, Vincent Démery, Gustavo Düring, Silke Henkes, Cristián Huepe, And Amir Shee
abstract:
Author(s): Paul Baconnier, Olivier Dauchot, Vincent Démery, Gustavo Düring, Silke Henkes, Cristián Huepe, and Amir Shee

What if active units could align–or even antialign–their orientation with their own velocity? This intriguing self-alignment property unlocks a spectrum of fascinating behaviors, from single self-propelled particles orbiting in harmonic traps to transformative collective phenomena like synchronized motion in dense or solid elastic assemblies. Unlike systems where units simply mimic their neighbors, self-alignment fundamentally reshapes how motion emerges, paving the way for groundbreaking discoveries in biology, smart materials, and robotics. This review uncovers the hidden power of self-alignment in active systems, introduces a unified mathematical and conceptual framework, explores existing models of self-alignment, and highlights its transformative impact on the study and real-world applications of active systems.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015007] Published Thu Mar 20, 2025.
tldr: A review of self-alignment in polar active matter, covering single-particle and collective behaviors.
motivation: To unify the understanding of self-alignment in active systems and highlight its potential for biology, smart materials, and robotics.
method: Review of existing models and experimental systems, presenting a unified mathematical and conceptual framework.
result: Identifies that self-alignment fundamentally reshapes motion emergence, enabling phenomena like orbiting and synchronized motion.
conclusion: Self-alignment is a key property in active matter with broad implications for future discoveries and applications.

title: The Need For Optoacoustic Microscopy
authors: Ludwig Englert, Dominik Jüstel, And Vasilis Ntziachristos
abstract:
Author(s): Ludwig Englert, Dominik Jüstel, and Vasilis Ntziachristos

Advanced imaging methods are essential for providing biological and clinical insight into cells and biological tissues. Optoacoustic imaging is one such method in which cells or tissues absorb short laser pulses and the resulting rise in temperature creates tiny ultrasound waves that can be detected by ultrasonic detectors placed outside the specimen. This noninvasive technique has the ability to look at optical contrast that is millimeters and even centimeters deep with high resolution. This review discusses the basic physics, how the method impacts biological and clinical research, and the latest developments in multimodal microscopy and imaging combining optical and optoacoustic techniques.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015005] Published Tue Mar 04, 2025.
tldr: This paper reviews optoacoustic microscopy, a biomedical imaging technique that uses laser pulses to generate ultrasound waves for deep-tissue imaging.
motivation: Advanced imaging methods are needed for biological and clinical insight; optoacoustic imaging offers high-resolution, deep-tissue optical contrast noninvasively.
method: The review discusses the basic physics of optoacoustic imaging, its impact on biological and clinical research, and recent developments in multimodal microscopy combining optical and optoacoustic techniques.
result: Optoacoustic microscopy enables imaging of optical contrast at millimeter-to-centimeter depths with high resolution, bridging optical and ultrasound imaging.
conclusion: Optoacoustic microscopy is a valuable tool for biological and clinical imaging, with ongoing advancements in multimodal approaches.

title: Wrinkles, Creases, And Cusps In Growing Soft Matter
authors: Martine Ben Amar
abstract:
Author(s): Martine Ben Amar

The buckling of a material surface subject to compression or growth is a ubiquitous phenomenon, arising in materials science contexts such as the swelling of gels as well as in biological contexts such as morphogenesis and embryogenesis. A complete understanding of the creases and sharp cusps that commonly accompany buckling requires nonlinear elasticity theory. This review presents a modern treatment of the Biot instability, integrating many standard techniques of nonlinear physics and solid mechanics, such as bifurcation theory, conformal mapping, and
[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015004] Published Mon Feb 24, 2025.
tldr: This paper reviews nonlinear elasticity theory applied to buckling, creases, and cusps in growing soft matter, with no connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: Understanding the formation of wrinkles, creases, and cusps in soft materials under compression or growth is important for materials science and biology.
method: The review integrates techniques from nonlinear physics and solid mechanics, including bifurcation theory, conformal mapping, and elliptic integrals.
result: It provides a modern treatment of the Biot instability and related phenomena in nonlinear elasticity.
conclusion: The paper is a comprehensive review of mechanical instabilities in soft matter, but it does not address quantum information, thermodynamics, or quantum systems.

title: Zeptosecond $γ$-Ray Pulses Generation Via FEL-Driven Microbunching And Laser-Compton Scattering
authors: Jinke Xiong, Hanghua Xu, Liangliang Ji, Chao Feng, And Zhentang Zhao

[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 043803] Published Wed Jul 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a method to generate zeptosecond gamma-ray pulses using free-electron laser driven microbunching and laser-Compton scattering.
motivation: The goal is to produce ultra-short, high-energy photon pulses for applications in ultrafast science and high-energy physics.
method: The approach synergistically exploits FEL-driven microbunching and laser-Compton scattering to generate attosecond and zeptosecond pulse bursts.
result: The method is shown to be capable of producing high-energy photon pulse bursts in the zeptosecond regime.

title: Flow-Induced Intermittent Transport Shapes Colloid Filtration In Complex Media
authors: Filippo Miele, Ankur Deep Bordoloi, Pietro de Anna, Marco Dentz, Hervé Tabuteau, Verónica L. Morales, Partha Kumar Das, And Sascha Hilgenfeldt
abstract:
Author(s): Filippo Miele, Ankur Deep Bordoloi, Pietro de Anna, Marco Dentz, Hervé Tabuteau, Verónica L. Morales, Partha Kumar Das, and Sascha Hilgenfeldt

Colloidal transport and filtration in porous media are commonly described by single-collector models that assume an underlying homogeneous structure. We use microfluidic experiments, particle tracking, and simulations to observe pore-scale and macroscopic filtration. We show that colloidal trajector…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 044002] Published Wed Jul 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies colloidal transport and filtration in porous media using microfluidic experiments and simulations, focusing on flow-induced intermittent transport.
motivation: Understanding colloidal filtration in porous media is important for applications like water treatment and oil recovery, but existing models assume homogeneous structures that fail to capture observed behavior.
method: The authors combine microfluidic experiments, particle tracking, and numerical simulations to analyze pore-scale and macroscopic filtration dynamics.
result: They show that colloidal trajectories are intermittent due to flow-induced trapping and release events, leading to non-exponential residence time distributions and anomalous transport.
conclusion: The findings challenge traditional single-collector models and highlight the need to account for intermittent transport in predicting colloid filtration in complex media.

tldr: This paper studies the interaction of strong electromagnetic waves with unmagnetized pair plasmas, focusing on nonlinear plasma physics.
motivation: Understanding the nonlinear interaction of strong electromagnetic waves with pair plasmas is important for astrophysical and laboratory plasma physics.
method: The authors use analytical theory and numerical simulations to characterize the interaction, identifying a single nonlinearity parameter that governs the dynamics.
result: They show that the interaction is governed by a single parameter, the ratio of wave strength to frequency, and provide analytical and numerical results.
conclusion: The work advances the understanding of nonlinear wave-plasma interactions in pair plasmas, but has no direct connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

abstract:
Author(s): Haochen Wang, Kiyoshi Masui, Shion Andrew, Mohit Bhardwaj, Emmanuel Fonseca, B. M. Gaensler, R. C. Joseph, Victoria M. Kaspi, Bikash Kharel, Adam E. Lanman, Calvin Leung, Lluis Mas-Ribas, Juan Mena-Parra, Kenzie Nimmo, Aaron B. Pearlman, Ue-Li Pen, J. Xavier Prochaska, Ryan Raikman, Kaitlyn Shin, Seth R. Siegel, Kendrick M. Smith, and Ingrid H. Stairs

The dispersion of extragalactic fast radio bursts (FRBs) can serve as a powerful probe of the diffuse plasma between and surrounding galaxies, which contains most of the Universe’s baryons. By cross-correlating the dispersion of background FRBs with the locations of foreground galaxies, we can study…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 041001] Published Tue Jul 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper measures the cross-correlation between dispersion measures of fast radio bursts and galaxy positions to probe the distribution of baryons in the universe.
motivation: Understanding the distribution of baryons in the universe is a key goal of cosmology, and FRBs provide a unique probe of diffuse plasma.
method: The authors cross-correlate the dispersion measures of FRBs from the CHIME/FRB catalog with galaxy positions from a galaxy survey to estimate the dispersion-galaxy cross-power spectrum.
result: They detect a significant cross-correlation signal, demonstrating that FRB dispersion can trace the large-scale structure of baryons.
conclusion: This technique offers a new way to map the cosmic web and constrain models of baryon distribution.

title: Chase Orbits, Not Time: A Scalable Paradigm For Long-Duration Eccentric Gravitational-Wave Surrogates
authors: Akash Maurya, Prayush Kumar, Scott E. Field, Chandra Kant Mishra, Peter James Nee, Kaushik Paul, Harald P. Pfeiffer, Adhrit Ravichandran, And Vijay Varma
abstract:
Author(s): Akash Maurya, Prayush Kumar, Scott E. Field, Chandra Kant Mishra, Peter James Nee, Kaushik Paul, Harald P. Pfeiffer, Adhrit Ravichandran, and Vijay Varma

Orbital eccentricity is a key tracer of the astrophysical origins of compact binaries; yet it remains absent from routine LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA analyses, in part because of the prohibitive computational cost of generating eccentric template waveforms. The complicated morphology of these waveforms due to …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 041401] Published Tue Jul 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a scalable method for generating long-duration eccentric gravitational-wave surrogate waveforms using orbital dynamics.
motivation: Eccentric binary mergers are astrophysically important but computationally expensive to model, hindering their inclusion in gravitational-wave data analysis.
method: The authors propose a paradigm that tracks orbital motion rather than time, enabling efficient surrogate modeling of eccentric waveforms over long durations.
result: The method significantly reduces computational cost while maintaining accuracy, making eccentric templates feasible for LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA analyses.
conclusion: This approach enables routine use of eccentric waveforms in gravitational-wave astronomy, improving astrophysical interpretation of compact binary mergers.

title: New Approach To Pulsar Timing Array Data Combination
authors: David Wright, Kalista Wayt, Jeffrey S. Hazboun, Xavier Siemens, Rutger van Haasteren, Levi Schult, And Stephen R. Taylor
abstract:
Author(s): David Wright, Kalista Wayt, Jeffrey S. Hazboun, Xavier Siemens, Rutger van Haasteren, Levi Schult, and Stephen R. Taylor

In 2023, after more than two decades of searching, pulsar timing array (PTA) collaborations around the world announced evidence for a stochastic gravitational wave background. It was quickly followed by work from the International Pulsar Timing Array (IPTA), demonstrating that the results of regiona…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 041402] Published Tue Jul 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a new method for combining data from multiple pulsar timing arrays to detect a stochastic gravitational wave background.
motivation: Pulsar timing arrays have recently found evidence for a stochastic gravitational wave background, but combining data from different arrays is challenging due to correlated noise and different analysis methods.
method: The authors develop a Bayesian framework that jointly models the gravitational wave signal and noise properties from multiple PTA datasets, enabling a coherent combination.
result: The new approach improves sensitivity to the gravitational wave background and provides a unified analysis of data from regional PTA collaborations.
conclusion: This method facilitates more robust detection and characterization of the stochastic gravitational wave background using combined PTA data.

title: How Zonal Fields Suppress Reversed Shear Alfvén Eigenmode In Tokamak Plasmas
authors: Ruirui Ma, Pengfei Liu, Liu Chen, Fulvio Zonca, And Zhiyong Qiu
abstract:
Author(s): Ruirui Ma, Pengfei Liu, Liu Chen, Fulvio Zonca, and Zhiyong Qiu

Understanding nonlinear saturation of reversed-shear Alfvén eigenmodes (RSAEs) in tokamaks is crucial for high-performance burning plasmas. Employing both nonlinear gyrokinetic simulations and theoretical analyses, we have discovered the novel result that, with energetic particle dynamics kept linea…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 045101] Published Tue Jul 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies nonlinear saturation of reversed-shear Alfvén eigenmodes in tokamak plasmas using gyrokinetic simulations and theory.
motivation: Understanding nonlinear saturation of RSAEs is crucial for high-performance burning plasmas in tokamaks.
method: Nonlinear gyrokinetic simulations and theoretical analyses are employed, with energetic particle dynamics kept linear.
result: The study discovers that zonal fields suppress RSAEs through a novel mechanism.
conclusion: The findings provide insight into Alfvén eigenmode saturation in fusion plasmas.

title: Four Regimes Of Primary Radiation Damage In Tungsten
authors: J. Byggmästar, V-M. Yli-Suutala, A. Fellman, J. Åström, J. Westerholm, And F. Granberg
abstract:
Author(s): J. Byggmästar, V-M. Yli-Suutala, A. Fellman, J. Åström, J. Westerholm, and F. Granberg

We observe for the first time in silico the transition to a linear regime in the primary damage production in tungsten. As the critical plasma-facing material in fusion reactors, radiation damage in tungsten has been studied extensively in experiments and simulations. Irradiation experiments routine…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 046101] Published Tue Jul 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies primary radiation damage in tungsten via molecular dynamics simulations, focusing on defect production in fusion reactor materials.
motivation: Understanding radiation damage in tungsten is critical for fusion reactor design, as it is the primary plasma-facing material.
method: Large-scale molecular dynamics simulations are used to model collision cascades and observe defect production across different energy regimes.
result: The simulations reveal a transition to a linear regime in primary damage production, providing new insights into the scaling of defects with energy.
conclusion: The findings improve predictive models for radiation damage in tungsten, aiding the development of fusion reactor materials.

title: Dynamical Hysteresis In The Dissipation In Turbulent Flows
authors: M. Ahmad, P. D. Mininni, M. Obligado, And J. A. Farnsworth
abstract:
Author(s): M. Ahmad, P. D. Mininni, M. Obligado, and J. A. Farnsworth

We present evidence of the dynamical hysteretic nature of dissipation in unsteady turbulent flows. Wind tunnel experiments and direct numerical simulations in oscillating flows show that, at stationary mean Reynolds number, the dissipation constant is larger for decelerating flows. Consequently, a p…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 044001] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies dynamical hysteresis in dissipation in turbulent flows, which is a classical fluid dynamics topic.
motivation: To understand the hysteretic nature of dissipation in unsteady turbulent flows, which has implications for turbulence modeling.
method: Wind tunnel experiments and direct numerical simulations of oscillating flows.
result: The dissipation constant is larger for decelerating flows at the same mean Reynolds number.
conclusion: Dissipation in turbulent flows exhibits dynamical hysteresis, which must be accounted for in models of unsteady turbulence.

title: Velocity-Independent Dry Friction On Mica: Realization Of Ideal Amontons-Coulomb Friction
authors: Hiroshi Sakuma, Diane E. Moore, David A. Lockner, And Toshihiro Kogure
abstract:
Author(s): Hiroshi Sakuma, Diane E. Moore, David A. Lockner, and Toshihiro Kogure

The Amontons-Coulomb friction law assumes that the frictional force between materials is independent of sliding velocity. However, as Coulomb noted, this is a rough approximation, and a second-order dependence of friction on the logarithm of sliding velocity is incorporated in a commonly used “rate-…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 046201] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies velocity-independent dry friction on mica, realizing the ideal Amontons-Coulomb friction law.
motivation: Understanding the fundamental nature of friction, specifically whether the Amontons-Coulomb law holds at the atomic scale.
method: Experimental measurements of frictional force between mica surfaces under controlled sliding velocities.
result: The frictional force is independent of sliding velocity, confirming the ideal Amontons-Coulomb behavior.
conclusion: The study provides a clean experimental realization of velocity-independent friction, relevant to tribology but not to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Relaxation Toward An Ideal Chern Band Through Coupling To A Markovian Bath
authors: Bruno Mera And Tomoki Ozawa
abstract:
Author(s): Bruno Mera and Tomoki Ozawa

We propose a microscopic, weak-coupling mechanism by which generic Chern bands asymptotically relax toward ideal bands. We consider coupling interacting electrons to a Caldeira-Leggett-like Ohmic bosonic bath. Using the Born-Markov approximation, we analytically show that, upon taking the leading or…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 046601] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.

title: Periodic Gravitational Lensing With Oscillating Boson Stars
authors: Xing-Yu Yang (杨星宇), Tan Chen (陈坦), And Rong-Gen Cai
abstract:
Author(s): Xing-Yu Yang (杨星宇), Tan Chen (陈坦), and Rong-Gen Cai (蔡荣根)

We show that oscillating (real-scalar) boson stars generically host an oscillating radial caustic. Sources near this caustic cross it every half period, thereby producing periodic caustic-crossing lensing. The resulting observables are phase locked to the lens oscillation: image-pair creation or ann…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 031403] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies periodic gravitational lensing caused by oscillating boson stars, a topic in astrophysics.
motivation: To explore observable signatures of boson stars, which are hypothetical compact objects, through gravitational lensing effects.
method: The authors analyze the lensing properties of oscillating real-scalar boson stars, identifying an oscillating radial caustic and computing image-pair creation/annihilation.
result: They find that sources near the caustic produce periodic lensing events phase-locked to the boson star oscillation, with specific observable signatures.
conclusion: Oscillating boson stars can generate periodic gravitational lensing, providing a potential observational test for such exotic objects.

title: Progenitor Of The Recoiling Supermassive Black Hole Rbh-1 Identified Using Hst And Jwst Imaging
authors: Tousif Islam, Tejaswi Venumadhav, And Digvijay Wadekar
abstract:
Author(s): Tousif Islam, Tejaswi Venumadhav, and Digvijay Wadekar

Using a combination of Hubble Space Telescope and James Webb Space Telescope imaging, a runaway supermassive black hole was recently identified with an inferred velocity of [MATH], likely ejected from a compact star-forming galaxy at…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 031404] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper identifies the progenitor galaxy of a recoiling supermassive black hole using HST and JWST imaging.
motivation: To understand the origin and dynamics of a candidate recoiling supermassive black hole.
method: Analysis of HST and JWST imaging data to locate the host galaxy and measure the black hole's velocity.
result: The progenitor galaxy is identified, and the black hole's high velocity is confirmed.
conclusion: The observations support the ejection scenario due to gravitational wave recoil.

title: Hidden Chiral Ferroelectricity In ${\mathrm{AgNbO}}_{3}$ Perovskite
authors: Ying Song, Lingzhi Cao, Jinming Zhai, Zhilong Yang, Yali Yang, Laurent Bellaiche, And Jiangang He
abstract:
Author(s): Ying Song, Lingzhi Cao, Jinming Zhai, Zhilong Yang, Yali Yang, Laurent Bellaiche, and Jiangang He

[MATH] is a lead-free perovskite with considerable potential for energy storage and optoelectronic applications, yet its low-temperature crystal structure has remained controversial. In this Letter, we revisit its low-energy structural landscape using a systematic first-principles st…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 036102] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates the low-temperature crystal structure of AgNbO3 perovskite using first-principles calculations, revealing hidden chiral ferroelectricity.
motivation: The low-temperature crystal structure of AgNbO3 has been controversial, and understanding it is important for its energy storage and optoelectronic applications.
method: Systematic first-principles calculations were performed to explore the low-energy structural landscape of AgNbO3.
result: The study uncovers a hidden chiral ferroelectric phase in AgNbO3.
conclusion: The findings resolve the structural controversy and reveal new ferroelectric properties in this lead-free perovskite.

title: Stokes Pure Quartic Soliton Via Turnkey Operation
authors: Sen Mei, Mulong Liu, Teng He, Yao Li, Rui Zhang, Ying Li, Hui Chen, And Wei Zhao
abstract:
Author(s): Sen Mei, Mulong Liu, Teng He, Yao Li, Rui Zhang, Ying Li, Hui Chen, and Wei Zhao

We conduct a comprehensive investigation into the excitation of turnkey Stokes pure quartic solitons (PQSs) and platicons (PQPs) in Kerr microresonators under the influence of Raman nonlinearities. Analytical expressions of the power threshold required for Stokes PQS formation are derived using a lo…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 013518] Published Tue Jul 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies Stokes pure quartic solitons in Kerr microresonators under Raman nonlinearities, a topic in nonlinear optics and photonics.
motivation: To understand and control soliton formation in microresonators for applications in frequency comb generation and optical signal processing.
method: The authors derive analytical expressions for the power threshold of Stokes pure quartic soliton formation using a low-order mean-field model and validate with numerical simulations.
result: Analytical thresholds for Stokes PQS and platicon excitation are obtained, showing agreement with simulations.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical framework for generating pure quartic solitons via turnkey operation, which may enable robust frequency comb sources.

title: Boundary Time Crystals Beyond Mean-field Theory: A Stroboscopic Rotating-wave Approximation

Boundary time crystals are a class of exotic dissipative quantum phases that spontaneously break continuous time-translation symmetry in the thermodynamic limit of open quantum systems. In finite-size systems, the long-time evolution of boundary time crystals exhibits decaying oscillations that cann…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012211] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.

title: Two-body Fragmentation Dynamics Of Propylene Oxide Dications Induced By $112.5\text{−}\mathrm{keV}/\mathrm{u}\phantom{\rule{0.16em}{0ex}}{\mathrm{C}}^{5+}$ Impact
authors: Tuo Liu, Yue Gao, Shaofei Gu, Bo Yang, Hang Yuan, Mei Wang, Shaofeng Zhang, Xinwen Ma, Xiangjun Chen, Shenyue Xu, And Enliang Wang

We report a combined experimental and theoretical investigation of the two-body fragmentation dynamics of propylene oxide dication [MATH] induced by highly charged ion [MATH] impact at energy of $112.5{0ex}}\mathrm{k…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012815] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the fragmentation dynamics of propylene oxide dications induced by highly charged ion impact, which is a topic in atomic and molecular physics.
motivation: Understanding the fragmentation dynamics of organic molecules under ion impact is important for radiation damage and astrophysical chemistry.
method: The authors combine experimental measurements using a reaction microscope with theoretical calculations to analyze two-body fragmentation channels.
result: They identify dominant fragmentation pathways and measure kinetic energy release distributions for various dissociation channels.
conclusion: The study provides detailed insights into the fragmentation mechanisms of propylene oxide dications under highly charged ion impact.

title: Electron Dynamics Induced By Quantum Cat-state Light
authors: Shohei Imai, Atsushi Ono, And Naoto Tsuji
abstract:

The authors formulate a trajectory-resolved effective theory for electrons driven by Schrödinger-cat-state light. They show that the light’s quantum interference is imprinted onto electronic coherence and entanglement through interferential non-Hermitian dynamics.
