abstract:
Author(s): Tong Wu, Zitan Zuo, Xiang Li, Shengzhe Pan, Shicheng Jiang, Ruifeng Lu, and Jian Wu

In this work, we experimentally observe orientation-dependent high-harmonic spectra in rocksalt crystal MgO driven by a linearly polarized 790 nm laser, featuring distinct peaks at [MATH], and [MATH] that correspond to orientation angles between the laser polarization and [100] crys…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 045122] Published Tue Jul 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies orientation-dependent high-harmonic generation in MgO crystal, a topic in condensed matter physics and nonlinear optics.
motivation: To understand the microscopic mechanism of high-harmonic generation in solids and its dependence on crystal orientation.
method: Experimental measurement of high-harmonic spectra from MgO driven by a linearly polarized 790 nm laser at various crystal orientations, combined with theoretical analysis using localized orbitals.
result: Observed distinct peaks in the harmonic spectra that vary with orientation angle, explained by the anisotropic electronic structure of MgO.
conclusion: The orientation-dependent features arise from the localized orbital nature of the material, providing insight into solid-state high-harmonic generation.

title: Rheological Measurements On Dense Suspensions Containing Dendrite-like Particles
authors: Andreas Ludwig, Mihaela Stefan-Kharicha, Christian Gomes Rodrigues, Johann Mogeritsch, Menghuai Wu, And Abdellah Kharicha
abstract:
Author(s): Andreas Ludwig, Mihaela Stefan-Kharicha, Christian Gomes Rodrigues, Johann Mogeritsch, Menghuai Wu, and Abdellah Kharicha

During alloy solidification, equiaxed dendrites often move within the solidifying liquid. As this motion is one of the main causes of macrosegregation, a deeper understanding of the behavior of suspensions containing dendrite-like particles is particularly important. Inspired by rheological investig…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 015417] Published Wed Jul 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the rheological behavior of dense suspensions containing dendrite-like particles, relevant to alloy solidification and macrosegregation.
motivation: Understanding the motion of equiaxed dendrites in solidifying alloys is crucial for predicting macrosegregation, a common defect in casting.
method: Rheological measurements were performed on suspensions with dendrite-like particles to characterize their flow properties.
result: The study provides quantitative data on the viscosity and yield stress of such suspensions as a function of particle concentration and morphology.
conclusion: The findings help model the flow of semisolid alloys during solidification, potentially improving casting quality.

title: Gravity-driven Granular Flow From A Wedge-shaped Hopper: Analysis Of The Exit Region
authors: Jeetram Yogi And Devang Khakhar
abstract:
Author(s): Jeetram Yogi and Devang Khakhar

We present results of experimental measurements and discrete element method simulations for granular flow in the exit region of a quasi-two-dimensional (2D) wedge-shaped hopper with glass front and back walls. The results are important from a practical viewpoint, since the mass flow rate from hopper…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 015418] Published Wed Jul 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies granular flow from a wedge-shaped hopper using experiments and simulations.
motivation: Understanding granular flow in hoppers is important for industrial applications.
method: Experimental measurements and discrete element method simulations were performed for a quasi-2D wedge-shaped hopper.
result: The mass flow rate and exit region dynamics were characterized.
conclusion: The results provide insights into granular flow behavior in hoppers.

title: Generating Consensus And Dissent On Massive Discussion Platforms With A Semantic-vector Model
authors: Alfredo Ferrer, David Muñoz-Jordán, Alejandro Rivero, Alfonso Tarancón, Carlos Tarancón, And David Yllanes
abstract:
Author(s): Alfredo Ferrer, David Muñoz-Jordán, Alejandro Rivero, Alfonso Tarancón, Carlos Tarancón, and David Yllanes

Reaching consensus on massive discussion networks is critical for reducing noise and achieving optimal collective outcomes. However, the natural tendency of humans to preserve their initial ideas constrains the emergence of global solutions. To address this, collective intelligence (CI) platforms fa…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014311] Published Tue Jul 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a semantic-vector model for generating consensus and dissent on massive discussion platforms, using collective intelligence techniques.
motivation: Reaching consensus on large discussion networks is challenging due to human tendency to preserve initial ideas, and existing platforms need better methods to reduce noise and achieve optimal collective outcomes.
method: The authors develop a semantic-vector model that represents user opinions as vectors and uses algorithms to facilitate consensus or dissent generation on massive discussion platforms.
result: The model demonstrates effectiveness in generating consensus and dissent, improving collective decision-making outcomes on simulated and real-world discussion platforms.
conclusion: The semantic-vector model offers a promising approach for managing large-scale discussions and enhancing collective intelligence, with potential applications in online deliberation and decision-making systems.

title: Theory Of Cell Body Lensing And Phototaxis Sign Reversal In “eyeless” Mutants Of Chlamydomonas
authors: Sumit Kumar Birwa, Ming Yang, Adriana I. Pesci, And Raymond E. Goldstein
abstract:
Author(s): Sumit Kumar Birwa, Ming Yang, Adriana I. Pesci, and Raymond E. Goldstein

Phototaxis of many species of green algae relies upon directional sensitivity of their membrane-bound photoreceptors, which arises from the presence of a pigmented “eyespot” behind them that blocks light passing through the cell body from reaching the photoreceptor. A decade ago it was discovered th…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014408] Published Tue Jul 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies phototaxis in Chlamydomonas mutants lacking an eyespot, attributing directional sensitivity to cell body lensing.
motivation: To understand how 'eyeless' mutants of Chlamydomonas can still exhibit phototaxis, challenging the prevailing model that requires an eyespot.
method: The authors develop a theoretical model of cell body lensing, where the spherical cell body focuses light onto the photoreceptor, and analyze how this mechanism can produce phototaxis sign reversal.
result: The model shows that cell body lensing can account for phototaxis in eyeless mutants and predicts sign reversal under certain conditions.
conclusion: Cell body lensing is a viable mechanism for phototaxis in the absence of an eyespot, expanding our understanding of algal phototaxis.

title: Reduced-order Model For Solute Transport In Mixed Electro-osmotic And Pressure-driven Flows Of Viscoelastic Fluids In Microchannels
authors: Morteza Dejam And Hassan Hassanzadeh
abstract:
Author(s): Morteza Dejam and Hassan Hassanzadeh

The solute transport due to mixed electro-osmotic and pressure-driven flows of viscoelastic fluids in microchannels is studied here. The Reynolds decomposition technique, in combination with the assumptions underlying the Taylor-Aris theory, is used to derive a reduced-order model that yields the di…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 015105] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies solute transport in mixed electro-osmotic and pressure-driven flows of viscoelastic fluids in microchannels using a reduced-order model.
motivation: Understanding solute transport in microfluidic devices is important for applications like chemical analysis and drug delivery, but viscoelastic fluids add complexity.
method: The authors apply Reynolds decomposition and Taylor-Aris theory to derive a reduced-order model for the dispersion coefficient.
result: The model predicts the effective solute transport behavior under combined electro-osmotic and pressure-driven flows.
conclusion: The reduced-order model provides a useful tool for designing microfluidic systems involving viscoelastic fluids.

title: Erratum: Conformal Invariance Constraints In The $o(n)$ Models: A Study Within The Nonperturbative Renormalization Group [Phys. Rev. E 111, 054126 (2025)]

[Phys. Rev. E 114, 019902] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: This is an erratum correcting a previous paper on conformal invariance in O(n) models using nonperturbative renormalization group, with no relevance to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: The erratum corrects errors in a previously published paper on statistical field theory.
method: The original paper used nonperturbative renormalization group methods to study conformal invariance constraints.
result: The erratum provides corrections to the original results.
conclusion: The corrected results maintain the original conclusions.

title: Avalanches Of A Granular Medium Reinforced With Flexible Fibers
authors: Ladislas Wierzchalek, Georges Gauthier, And Baptiste Darbois Texier
abstract:
Author(s): Ladislas Wierzchalek, Georges Gauthier, and Baptiste Darbois Texier

The addition of a small fraction of flexible fibers to a granular medium is known to enhance the bulk mechanical strength of the material. However, their effect on the free-surface flow of grains remains largely unexplored. To address this gap, we investigate the influence of flexible fibers on dry …


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 015414] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the effect of flexible fibers on avalanches in dry granular media, a topic in soft matter physics.
motivation: The mechanical reinforcement of granular media by fibers is known, but their influence on free-surface flows is unexplored.
method: Experimental investigation of dry granular flows with added flexible fibers, measuring avalanche dynamics.
result: Flexible fibers alter avalanche behavior, likely due to fiber-grain interactions.
conclusion: The study provides insights into granular flow mechanics but has no connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Wettability-mediated Transition From Circular To Radial Cracks In Dried Deposit Of Colloidal Ellipsoids
authors: Sanket Kumar, Madivala G. Basavaraj, And Dillip K. Satapathy
abstract:
Author(s): Sanket Kumar, Madivala G. Basavaraj, and Dillip K. Satapathy

We report a transition in the orientation of primary cracks in colloidal ellipsoid deposits driven exclusively by variations in substrate wettability. On highly wettable substrates, the primary cracks in the deposit of ellipsoids are predominantly along the circumferential direction. In contrast, wi…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 015505] Published Thu Jul 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies crack patterns in drying colloidal ellipsoid deposits as a function of substrate wettability.
motivation: Understanding crack formation in colloidal deposits is important for applications like coatings and paints, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: Experiments with colloidal ellipsoids on substrates of varying wettability, observing crack orientation.
result: On wettable substrates, cracks are circular; on less wettable substrates, they become radial.
conclusion: Substrate wettability can control crack orientation in colloidal ellipsoid deposits.

title: Exact Constant-intensity Solutions And Modulational Instability In A Higher-order Nonlinear Schrödinger Equation With Real Potential
authors: Nicholas J. Ossi, Savvas Sardelis, And Ziad H. Musslimani
abstract:
Author(s): Nicholas J. Ossi, Savvas Sardelis, and Ziad H. Musslimani

Constant-intensity (CI) waves are plane-wave-like solutions that are known to propagate in non-Hermitian inhomogeneous media with complex external potential (with the real part corresponding to the refractive index and the imaginary part representing a distribution of gain and loss) while keeping th…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014213] Published Wed Jul 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies constant-intensity waves and modulational instability in a higher-order nonlinear Schrödinger equation with a real potential.
motivation: To understand wave propagation in non-Hermitian inhomogeneous media with gain and loss, and to find exact solutions.
method: Analytical derivation of constant-intensity solutions and linear stability analysis for modulational instability.
result: Exact constant-intensity solutions are found, and conditions for modulational instability are determined.
conclusion: The work provides insights into nonlinear wave dynamics in complex potentials, but has no connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Ring Solitons And Lump Waves Of The Elliptic Cylindrical Kadomtsev-Petviashvili Equation In Physical Coordinates
authors: Tianwei Qiu, Zhen Wang, And Xiangyu Yang
abstract:
Author(s): Tianwei Qiu, Zhen Wang, and Xiangyu Yang

The elliptic cylindrical Kadomtsev-Petviashvili (ecKP) equation is derived from the incompressible Euler equations governing surface gravity waves with nearly elliptic fronts. Using Hirota's bilinear method, this paper systematically investigates ring solitons, lump chains, and lump waves of the ecK…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014216] Published Wed Jul 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies ring solitons and lump waves of the elliptic cylindrical Kadomtsev-Petviashvili equation, which is a classical nonlinear wave equation in fluid dynamics.
motivation: To understand nonlinear wave phenomena in elliptic cylindrical coordinates, which have applications in oceanography and fluid dynamics.
method: Uses Hirota's bilinear method to derive exact solutions for ring solitons, lump chains, and lump waves.
result: Obtains explicit analytical solutions for ring solitons and lump waves, demonstrating their propagation and interaction properties.
conclusion: The ecKP equation admits rich soliton and lump wave structures that may be relevant for describing surface gravity waves with nearly elliptic fronts.

title: Dynamical Origin Of Extreme Events In Mutually Coupled And Networked Brusselator
authors: S. V. Manivelan, S. Sabarathinam, K. Thamilmaran, And I. Manimehan

title: Fundamentals Of Vacuum Breakdown In High-gradient Accelerator Structures
authors: Walter Wuensch, Sergio Calatroni, Flyura Djurabekova, Andreas Kyritsakis, And Yinon Ashkenazy
abstract:
Author(s): Walter Wuensch, Sergio Calatroni, Flyura Djurabekova, Andreas Kyritsakis, and Yinon Ashkenazy

Vacuum breakdown or arcing happens when a very strong electric field causes a metal surface in a vacuum to suddenly form plasma, allowing large electrical currents to flow. Breakdown can damage particle accelerators, fusion reactors, satellites, and x-ray devices, though it is useful in technologies like plasma thrusters. Scientists have studied this unpredictable and fast phenomenon for over a century. Recent advances in experiments and computer simulations now provide a coherent mechanistic picture: tiny surface defects, electrical stress, heat, and emitted particles interact in complex ways to trigger breakdowns. These insights could improve high-power technologies and make advanced accelerators more reliable and efficient.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025004] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper reviews the physics of vacuum breakdown in high-gradient accelerator structures, focusing on the role of surface defects, electrical stress, and plasma formation.
motivation: Vacuum breakdown limits the performance of particle accelerators, fusion reactors, and other high-power devices; understanding its mechanism is crucial for improving reliability and efficiency.
method: The authors synthesize experimental observations and computer simulations to build a coherent mechanistic picture of the breakdown process, from defect initiation to plasma formation.
result: A unified model emerges where tiny surface defects, electrical stress, heat, and emitted particles interact to trigger breakdown, explaining the unpredictable and fast nature of the phenomenon.
conclusion: These insights can guide the design of more robust accelerator structures and other high-power technologies, potentially enabling more reliable and efficient advanced accelerators.

title: Colloquium: Hadron Production In Open-charm Meson Pairs At ${e}^{+}{e}^{−}$ Colliders
authors: Xiongfei Wang, Xiang Liu, And Yuanning Gao
abstract:
Author(s): Xiongfei Wang, Xiang Liu, and Yuanning Gao

Hadron spectroscopy is a frontier of particle physics; searching for new hadrons is crucial for validating the theory of strong interaction (QCD). Investigating how charmonium, a bound state of charm and anticharm quarks, decays and searching for new charmoniumlike states yield valuable insights into strong interaction mechanisms, including quark confinement and gluon binding. Hadrons produced at e− collisions decaying to open-charm meson pairs are a primary source of experimental information for these investigations. This Colloquium reviews current progress from BARBAR, Belle, CLEO-c, and BESIII experiments. As BESIII accumulates high-precision data, it has emerged as the leading facility for measuring hadron production in charm-meson pair systems, and recent advances are highlighted.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 021001] Published Fri Apr 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper reviews hadron production in open-charm meson pairs at e+e- colliders, focusing on charmonium spectroscopy and strong interaction mechanisms.
motivation: Understanding charmonium decays and searching for new hadrons is crucial for validating quantum chromodynamics (QCD) and exploring quark confinement.
method: The paper reviews experimental progress from BESIII, Belle, BaBar, and CLEO-c, highlighting measurements of hadron production in charm-meson pair systems.
result: BESIII has emerged as the leading facility for such measurements, providing high-precision data on charmoniumlike states and decay mechanisms.
conclusion: The review summarizes current knowledge and recent advances in hadron spectroscopy from e+e- colliders, emphasizing the role of BESIII in future discoveries.

title: Colloquium: Planetary Radar At The Arecibo Observatory
authors: Michael C. Nolan, Lynn M. Carter, And Edgard G. Rivera-Valentín
abstract:
Author(s): Michael C. Nolan, Lynn M. Carter, and Edgard G. Rivera-Valentín

For more than two decades, the planetary radar installed at the Arecibo Telescope was the most sensitive instrument of its kind, harnessing the penetrating power of radio waves to perform observations of the (sub)surface of planets, moons, and asteroids in the Solar System—providing a unique perspective on those bodies that helped to drive in situ exploration. This Colloquium presents an overview of the scientific legacy of the Arecibo radar system, focusing on the period posterior to the Gregorian Update in the late 1990s until the unexpected demise of the telescope in 2020. After recalling the basics of planetary radar techniques, it reviews key Arecibo observations of Mercury, Venus, Mars, our Moon, and the Saturn system, and highlights its essential role in the characterization of a large sample of near-Earth asteroids and comets.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 011003] Published Tue Mar 31, 2026.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews the scientific legacy of the Arecibo planetary radar system, focusing on observations of solar system bodies.
motivation: Planetary radar provides unique subsurface and surface information about planets, moons, and asteroids, complementing in situ exploration.
method: The paper summarizes radar techniques and reviews key Arecibo observations of Mercury, Venus, Mars, the Moon, Saturn system, and near-Earth asteroids.
result: Arecibo radar significantly advanced knowledge of planetary surfaces and near-Earth asteroid characterization.
conclusion: The Arecibo radar system was a uniquely sensitive instrument whose loss leaves a gap in planetary radar capabilities.

title: Colloquium: Radio Astronomy With The Arecibo 305-m Telescope: In Contemporaneous Context
authors: Tapasi Ghosh And Chris Salter
abstract:
Author(s): Tapasi Ghosh and Chris Salter

The Arecibo Observatory, inaugurated in 1963 as the world’s largest single-dish radio telescope, remained at the forefront of astronomy and atmospheric science for more than five decades, until its catastrophic collapse in December 2020. This Colloquium focuses on Arecibo’s enduring legacy in radio astronomy, offering a historical perspective that emphasizes how successive major upgrades of the telescope continuously expanded its observational capabilities and scientific impact. It presents Arecibo’s most influential contributions in topics as diverse as pulsar studies, the mapping of neutral hydrogen (HI) in the Milky Way and other galaxies, the characterization of the interstellar medium, the imaging of extragalactic radio sources with very long baseline interferometry (VLBI), the search for extraterrestrial intelligence (SETI), and being a major contributor to the first-ever detection of a stochastic gravitational-wave background.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 011004] Published Tue Mar 31, 2026.
tldr: This paper is a historical review of the Arecibo radio telescope's contributions to radio astronomy and atmospheric science.
motivation: To document the legacy of the Arecibo Observatory and its impact on various fields of astronomy.
method: Historical narrative and summary of key scientific achievements enabled by successive upgrades of the telescope.
result: Highlights major contributions in pulsar studies, HI mapping, VLBI, SETI, and gravitational-wave detection.
conclusion: Arecibo's upgrades continuously expanded its capabilities, leading to enduring scientific impact across multiple disciplines.

title: Colloquium: Geospace Pathfinder Science At Arecibo Observatory
authors: J. D. Mathews, M. P. Sulzer, And Shikha Raizada
abstract:
Author(s): J. D. Mathews, M. P. Sulzer, and Shikha Raizada

The Arecibo Observatory housed the largest single-aperture radio telescope for approximately 50 years. A major scientific focus was studying the upper atmosphere; its highly sensitive radar facility, combined with lidars, optical sensors, and satellite-based systems, enabled unprecedented studies of ionospheric physics based on incoherent scattering of radio waves off free electrons. After establishing the fundamental concepts and observables of the incoherent scattering radar technique, this Colloquium reviews key advances obtained with the Arecibo suite of instruments in multiple areas of geospace science, including plasma physics, space weather, lidar studies of atomic metals in the ionosphere, and ionosphere-magnetosphere coupling.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 011005] Published Tue Mar 31, 2026.
tldr: This paper reviews geospace science advances using the Arecibo Observatory's radar and lidar instruments, focusing on ionospheric physics and space weather.
motivation: The Arecibo Observatory's unique capabilities for studying the upper atmosphere and ionosphere have enabled significant advances in geospace science, which this Colloquium aims to summarize.
method: The paper reviews key results obtained from incoherent scatter radar, lidar, optical, and satellite-based measurements at Arecibo, covering plasma physics, space weather, and ionosphere-magnetosphere coupling.
result: The review highlights advances in understanding ionospheric plasma processes, metal layers, and coupling between the ionosphere and magnetosphere.
conclusion: The Arecibo Observatory has been instrumental in geospace research, and its legacy continues to inform upper atmospheric science.

title: Colloquium: Multimessenger Astronomy With Continuous Gravitational Waves And Future Detectors

abstract:
Author(s): Benjamin J. Owen

The search for continuous gravitational waves from rotating neutron stars represents a key frontier of gravitational-wave astrophysics, with strong connections to electromagnetic astronomy, nuclear astrophysics, and condensed matter physics. This Colloquium discusses the detection prospects for these long-lived yet elusive signals in the upcoming generation of gravitational-wave detectors, emphasizing the importance of simultaneous electromagnetic observations. It also surveys the potential implications of such multimessenger observations for our understanding of the physical and astrophysical processes taking place in the extremely dense environments of their sources.

tldr: This paper discusses the prospects for detecting continuous gravitational waves from rotating neutron stars and the implications for multimessenger astronomy.
motivation: Continuous gravitational waves from neutron stars are a key frontier in gravitational-wave astrophysics, with connections to electromagnetic astronomy, nuclear astrophysics, and condensed matter physics.
method: The paper reviews detection prospects for upcoming gravitational-wave detectors and emphasizes the importance of simultaneous electromagnetic observations.
result: It surveys potential implications for understanding physical and astrophysical processes in dense environments.
conclusion: Multimessenger observations combining gravitational and electromagnetic waves will enhance our understanding of neutron star interiors and related physics.

title: Colloquium: Convection-cloud Chambers: Experiment And Theory
authors: Steven Krueger And Raymond A. Shaw
abstract:
Author(s): Steven Krueger and Raymond A. Shaw

In warm clouds, drops grow into raindrops through both condensation and collision coalescence, but the observed rapid transition between these mechanisms remains difficult to theoretically explain. The convection-cloud chamber, which reproduces key phenomena such as turbulent fluctuations in droplet concentrations and supersaturation under controlled laboratory conditions, offers a promising approach to addressing this long-standing bottleneck in understanding in cloud physics. This Colloquium reviews the physics underlying the precipitation bottleneck, examines how convection-cloud chambers capture the essential processes, and synthesizes insights from experiments, theory, and computational models that bridge laboratory and atmospheric scales.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 011001] Published Wed Feb 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper reviews convection-cloud chambers as a laboratory tool to study the precipitation bottleneck in warm clouds.
motivation: Understanding the rapid transition from condensation to collision-coalescence in warm clouds is a long-standing problem in cloud physics.
method: The authors review experimental, theoretical, and computational studies of convection-cloud chambers that reproduce key cloud phenomena under controlled conditions.
result: Convection-cloud chambers can capture turbulent fluctuations in droplet concentrations and supersaturation, helping to bridge laboratory and atmospheric scales.
conclusion: The convection-cloud chamber is a promising approach to address the precipitation bottleneck, but further work is needed to fully explain the rapid transition.

title: Colloquium: Gravitational Waves From Neutrino-driven Core Collapse Supernovae
authors: A. Mezzacappa And M. Zanolin
abstract:
Author(s): A. Mezzacappa and M. Zanolin

The observation of a core collapse supernova explosion of (near-)Galactic origin would constitute a landmark, once-in-a-century event for multimessenger astronomy, eagerly awaited by observers and modelers alike. The detection of gravitational waves, along with photons and neutrinos, from such an event would provide unique insights into the supernova central engine and the physics of the newly forming neutron star. This Colloquium presents the latest progress in core collapse supernova modeling and the associated gravitational wave signal predictions. It also provides an overview of the specific methods of detection and physical parameter estimation that can be implemented for such signals in ground-based laser interferometers, in the context of multimessenger research strategies.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 041002] Published Tue Dec 30, 2025.
tldr: This colloquium reviews gravitational wave signals from core collapse supernovae and their detection methods.
motivation: Observing a Galactic core collapse supernova would be a landmark event for multimessenger astronomy, providing insights into the supernova engine and neutron star physics.
method: The paper summarizes progress in supernova modeling and gravitational wave signal predictions, and discusses detection and parameter estimation methods for ground-based laser interferometers.
result: The review presents the latest modeling results and signal predictions, but does not introduce new results.
conclusion: Gravitational wave detection from core collapse supernovae is a promising multimessenger avenue, but the paper is a review without novel contributions to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Colloquium: The Cosmic Dipole Anomaly
authors: Nathan Secrest, Sebastian von Hausegger, Mohamed Rameez, Roya Mohayaee, And Subir Sarkar
abstract:
Author(s): Nathan Secrest, Sebastian von Hausegger, Mohamed Rameez, Roya Mohayaee, and Subir Sarkar

The cosmological principle, which states that the Universe must be statistically isotropic and homogeneous on large scales, is a foundational principle of the standard model of cosmology, known as lambda cold dark matter (ΛCDM). The validity of this principle can be tested by assessing the compatibility of a dipole anisotropy in the large-scale distribution of matter with the dipole observed in the cosmic microwave background, interpreted in the ΛCDM model as due to our local peculiar motion. This Colloquium describes the methodology for such a test and presents its outcome based on the analysis of recent large catalogs of radio galaxies and quasars, revealing a significant inconsistency between the two dipoles. The authors review these recent findings, as well as potential biases, systematic issues, and alternate interpretations, and discuss how this anomaly could challenge the standard description of our Universe based on the ΛCDM model.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 041001] Published Thu Dec 11, 2025.
tldr: This paper reviews the cosmic dipole anomaly, testing the cosmological principle by comparing the dipole in the large-scale distribution of matter with the CMB dipole.
motivation: To test the foundational cosmological principle of isotropy and homogeneity by examining a significant inconsistency between the matter dipole and the CMB dipole.
method: The authors analyze recent large catalogs of radio galaxies and quasars, compare the observed dipole with the CMB dipole, and review potential biases and systematic issues.
result: A significant inconsistency is found between the two dipoles, challenging the standard ΛCDM model.
conclusion: The cosmic dipole anomaly may indicate a violation of the cosmological principle or require modifications to the standard model of cosmology.

title: Astrophysical Tests Of Dark Matter Self-interactions
authors: Susmita Adhikari, Arka Banerjee, Kimberly K. Boddy, Francis-Yan Cyr-Racine, Harry Desmond, Cora Dvorkin, Bhuvnesh Jain, Felix Kahlhoefer, Manoj Kaplinghat, Anna Nierenberg, Annika H. G. Peter, Andrew Robertson, Jeremy Sakstein, And Jesús Zavala
abstract:
Author(s): Susmita Adhikari, Arka Banerjee, Kimberly K. Boddy, Francis-Yan Cyr-Racine, Harry Desmond, Cora Dvorkin, Bhuvnesh Jain, Felix Kahlhoefer, Manoj Kaplinghat, Anna Nierenberg, Annika H. G. Peter, Andrew Robertson, Jeremy Sakstein, and Jesús Zavala

Dark sectors, involving new particles that couple very weakly to the standard model ones, play an important role in current model-building efforts in particle physics, as they allow, for example, for new dark matter production and interaction mechanisms. This review focuses on self-interacting dark matter scenarios, their implications on the dynamics and distribution of dark matter halos in the Universe, and the related astrophysical tests and observations, from galaxies to large-scale structures. It is embedded in the framework of the Novel Probes Project, a forum connecting observers and theorists involved in the study of astrophysical tests of dark-sector interactions.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045004] Published Mon Dec 08, 2025.
tldr: This paper reviews astrophysical tests of self-interacting dark matter, focusing on dark matter halo dynamics and large-scale structure.
motivation: To understand the nature of dark matter and test models where dark matter particles self-interact, which can affect structure formation.
method: The paper is a review summarizing theoretical predictions and observational constraints from galaxies to large-scale structures, using simulations and astrophysical data.
result: It compiles current constraints on dark matter self-interaction cross-sections and discusses implications for dark matter models.
conclusion: Self-interacting dark matter remains a viable candidate, and future observations will further constrain its properties.

title: Prospects For Supersymmetry At High-Luminosity Lhc
authors: Howard Baer, Vernon Barger, Jessica Bolich, Juhi Dutta, Dakotah Martinez, Shadman Salam, Dibyashree Sengupta, And Kairui Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Howard Baer, Vernon Barger, Jessica Bolich, Juhi Dutta, Dakotah Martinez, Shadman Salam, Dibyashree Sengupta, and Kairui Zhang

Supersymmetry remains one of the leading candidates for physics beyond the standard model, offering a compelling framework to address the hierarchy of scales. Its theoretical appeal has inspired decades of intensive model building and experimental searches. Recent results have placed stringent bounds on the supersymmetric parameter space, sharpening the focus on the remaining viable models. This review surveys the current status and outlook for supersymmetry in light of experimental constraints and recent theoretical developments, and presents projections for the discovery potential of the High-Luminosity Large Hadron Collider across multiple search channels and a variety of well-motivated scenarios.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045001] Published Fri Oct 17, 2025.
tldr: This paper reviews the prospects for supersymmetry at the High-Luminosity LHC, focusing on experimental searches and model constraints.
motivation: Supersymmetry is a leading candidate for physics beyond the Standard Model, but recent LHC results have constrained its parameter space. The paper aims to survey the current status and future discovery potential.
method: The authors review theoretical models and experimental search channels, and project discovery potential for the High-Luminosity LHC based on current constraints.
result: The paper provides an overview of viable supersymmetric scenarios and their expected signatures at the HL-LHC, but does not present new theoretical or experimental results.
conclusion: Supersymmetry remains viable in certain regions of parameter space, and the HL-LHC will have significant discovery potential across multiple channels.

title: Solar Fusion Iii: New Data And Theory For Hydrogen-burning Stars
authors: B. Acharya et Al.
abstract:
Author(s): B. Acharya et al.

Approximately 90% of the stars in the Milky Way are on the main sequence, fusing hydrogen into helium through a network of nuclear reactions. This includes the nearest star, our Sun. A precise understanding of hydrogen burning is crucial to predicting its luminosity, neutrino production, and helioseismology. This review describes the theoretical and experimental work of the last decade that has advanced our understanding of the nuclear physics of hydrogen burning. It describes the plasma and atomic physics that influences the solar environment in which the nuclear reactions take place, as well as the diagnostics probes—including solar neutrinos and helioseismology—that allow us to test our resulting model of the solar interior.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 035002] Published Thu Sep 04, 2025.
tldr: This paper reviews nuclear physics of hydrogen burning in stars, focusing on solar fusion and neutrino production.
motivation: Understanding hydrogen burning is crucial for predicting stellar luminosity, neutrino production, and helioseismology.
method: The review summarizes theoretical and experimental advances in nuclear reaction rates, plasma physics, and solar modeling.
result: Updated nuclear reaction rates and improved solar models are presented, with comparisons to neutrino and helioseismic data.
conclusion: The paper provides a comprehensive update on hydrogen-burning nuclear physics, but does not address quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Nobel Lecture: Physics Is A Point Of View
authors: John J. Hopfield
abstract:
Author(s): John J. Hopfield

The 2024 Nobel Prize for Physics was shared by John Hopfield and Geoffrey Hinton. This paper is the text of the address given in conjunction with the award.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 030501] Published Mon Aug 25, 2025.
tldr: Nobel lecture by John Hopfield reflecting on his career and the nature of physics.
motivation: To share personal insights and perspectives on physics as a field of study.
method: Narrative and reflective lecture.
result: No novel research results; a retrospective on past contributions.
conclusion: Physics is a point of view that shapes how we understand the world.

title: Nobel Lecture: Boltzmann Machines
authors: Geoffrey Hinton
abstract:
Author(s): Geoffrey Hinton

The 2024 Nobel Prize for Physics was shared by John Hopfield and Geoffrey Hinton. This paper is the text of the address given in conjunction with the award.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 030502] Published Mon Aug 25, 2025.
tldr: This Nobel lecture describes Boltzmann machines, a class of stochastic neural networks, and their role in machine learning.
motivation: The lecture aims to explain the concept and significance of Boltzmann machines in the context of artificial intelligence and neural networks.
method: The lecture discusses the architecture, training algorithm (contrastive divergence), and probabilistic nature of Boltzmann machines.
result: Boltzmann machines can learn complex probability distributions and serve as building blocks for deep belief networks.
conclusion: Boltzmann machines have been influential in the development of deep learning, but they are not directly related to quantum information theory or quantum thermodynamics.

title: Gas Bubble Dynamics
authors: Dominique Legendre And Roberto Zenit
abstract:
Author(s): Dominique Legendre and Roberto Zenit

The motion of gas bubbles in liquids plays a vital role in numerous natural, industrial, and everyday phenomena. Unlike solid particles, gas bubbles are nearly weightless and highly responsive to forces from the surrounding fluid. Their dynamics are affected by added mass acceleration and deformable surfaces, and also by interactions with turbulent flows, other bubbles, and walls, with liquid rheology and surfactants further influencing their behavior. This review examines the intricate behavior of noncondensable gas bubbles, highlighting key advances over the past 20 years. Key topics include turbulence, non-Newtonian fluids, and electrolytes, offering insights to enhance modeling and guide future research in two-phase flow systems.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025001] Published Thu Apr 17, 2025.
tldr: This paper reviews the dynamics of gas bubbles in liquids, covering turbulence, non-Newtonian fluids, and electrolytes.
motivation: Understanding bubble dynamics is crucial for many natural and industrial processes, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The review synthesizes advances over the past 20 years in bubble dynamics, focusing on fluid mechanics.
result: Key insights include the effects of added mass, deformable surfaces, turbulence, and surfactants on bubble behavior.
conclusion: The review provides a comprehensive overview to guide future research in two-phase flow systems, but has no relevance to the user's research interests.
